Today, I’d like to continue and possibly complete our discussion of Regenerative Medicine. I want to consider where it stands today, and how Christians can navigate the complex maze of treatments. As you may recall, in the previous issue of this magazine we discussed that Regenerative Medicine is man’s attempt to re-create organ systems. We described how fetal tissue was attempted to be used, due to its low rate of rejection by the people receiving it. Medically speaking, it was problematic in that, if used on a large scale, it would require large amounts of aborted fetuses. Later, embryonic stem cells were studied in depth. Here, embryos, which are newly conceived humans in their earliest stages, are dissected (cut apart) and stem cells are taken.

Think of stem cells as indolent, immature adults, who live in their parents’ basements, without direction, not knowing what they want to do with their lives. With a little encouragement and direction, they can finally find their way, finding a specialized skill and important role in life. In like manner, scientists have discovered ways to “program” these stem cells, “encouraging” them to become specialized into types of cells, such as nerve, heart, blood, and insulin producing. These cells would then be grown in a lab, then used to repair or replace the diseased or injured tissue.

However, “taking” stem cells from embryos results in his or her (the embryo’s) destruction. This is obviously problematic for Christians, knowing that one of the seven things that the Lord says is an abomination is …hands that shed innocent blood –Pro 6:17. Additionally, the sixth commandment directs, Thou shalt not kill –Exo 20:13. Because these objections were recognized by the scientific community, there was pressure to find an alternative.

The Apostle Paul states, There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it –1Co 10:13. His words are as true today as they were 2000 years ago. While Christians suffer from disease just as commonly as non-Christians do, modern medicine can present the “temptation” of a treatment and relief from disease or injury that is actually immoral. But God is faithful, and his escape is twofold. First and foremost, He gave His son to bear our burdens. It is to this Great Physician that we should always turn to first.

In the case of stem cell treatments, it so happens that it was discovered that these immature stem cells are not only found in human embryos, but they are also found in all people, from infants to grown-ups as well. This may be the physical “escape” for His faithful children. These immature stem cells (usually obtained from a patient’s fat tissue or bone marrow) can be grown, cultured, and used just as well as embryonic stem cells. It turns out that “Adult Stem Cells” have actually been more clinically effective, since they are “custom designed” for each individual, and since they come from that person’s own body; therefore, there is very little problem with rejection.

Umbilical cord stem cells have also been shown to be useful, particularly in bone and cartilage treatments. Just as there have been obstacles to overcome when using embryonic stem cells, so too there are problems with developing treatments using adult or umbilical cord stem cells. Think again of a stem cell as an immature, indolent adult. Just having him “hang out” with a master carpenter will not make him a master carpenter if all he does is find entertainment on his cell phone. Stem cells, like an apprentice, need intense, focused training and direction to become specialists in their chosen field of expertise. Learning how to turn these “switches” on is perhaps one of the greatest challenges. The main idea here is that just injecting stem cells that have not been “programmed” or “trained” into damaged or diseased tissue will not automatically make them “know” what to become or how to function.

Similarly, just putting a young electronics apprentice on a bus that is traveling into a city that just had a power grid failure will not result in restoring the power. Here the parallel is placing stem cells into the brain of a stroke victim or a paraplegic accident victim, hoping that the stem cells will “know” what to do, and which specific connections to repair in order to restore function. This may not work as hoped. It would be fruitless to expect success unless and until these problems are also addressed.

Then there is the lingering problem of these eager youngsters (stem cells) knowing when to stop. The problem with fetal tissue turning into cancerous tumors is also a problem to be dealt with in stem cells. Considering this, there is one exception: umbilical cord stem cells are generally not known to turn malignant.1

Here is a short list of treatments that are in development that would use stem cells:

  • Macular Degeneration—Repair a damaged retina.
  • Spinal Cord Injury/Stroke—Repair nerve tissue.
  • Burns—Repair skin tissue.
  • Congestive Heart Failure—Repair damaged heart tissue.
  • Diabetes—Replace or increase the pancreatic tissue that makes insulin.
  • Arthritis—Repair damaged cartilage.
  • Autoimmune diseases (Lupus, Multiple Sclerosis) —Destroy the immune system that is attacking its own body and replace or “reset” it with a new immune system derived from one’s own stem cells.
  • Leukemias—Destroy the cancerous blood cells and replace them with new stem cell derived blood cells.
  • New organs—Replace diseased, damaged, or cancer-ridden organs, such as the kidney, liver, or pancreas, with organs derived from the patient’s own stem cells, grown in a lab, and transplanted surgically, without the need of anti-rejection drugs.

As you can see, there is a very long list of diseases and ailments that may result in effective treatments with stem cells. I am very optimistic that within a decade, remedies for many of these ailments will be commonly available. However, learning how to make stem cells that are expertly specialized into specific tissue types, learning how to turn stems cells on and then turning them off at the necessary time (once the job is finished), and learning how to “teach” the stem cells where and how to make repairs will take time.

I am not the only one who is excited about the possibilities. That is why hundreds of stem cell clinics have sprung up across the country, trying to get in on the excitement. But do the claims of any of these clinics align with reality? Which ones are legitimate? I know that there are many clinics offering stem cell treatments for various ailments, so let’s now look at some of the treatments that are available today—ones that have evidence of actually helping, as well as realistic expectations. Let’s also look at some of the possible complications, to help us make informed decisions.

First, the risks and complications

  • Introduction of infection—For example, bacteria living on the skin can enter a joint space from a simple injection, resulting in destruction of the joint, even under the cleanest of conditions.
  • Stems cells moving from their introduction site and not going where they are intended or not staying contained to the specific area of treatment—One study involving pigs treated with stem cells injected into areas of a damaged heart after a heart attack showed near complete return of function, but then the new heart tissue kept growing, eventually filling the heart’s pumping chamber, which caused all the pigs to die.
  • Stem cells changing into unexpected or inappropriate cell types—Stem cells used for a facial cosmetic effect have actually turned to bone.2
  • Growth of tumors—There are documented cases of different tumors, including brain and kidney tumors that have developed after patients were treated for stroke and kidney failure using stem cells.
  • Failure to work as expected—There are documented cases of people with macular degeneration, who were treated with stem cells injected into the eye, that have resulted in blindness.
  • Stem cells can’t be withdrawn—Unlike medicines such as a pill or an injection, if something goes wrong, one can’t just withhold the next dose. Once stem cells are introduced, they can’t be taken back. The course that has been set will continue.

The rates of complications are hard to know, since there are no reporting requirements when performed outside of formal clinical investigations.

Next, the known benefits

The FDA (the governmental Food and Drug Administration that is tasked with health safety) has approved stem cell treatments for dozens of blood cancers (leukemias) and blood diseases using umbilical cord stem cells. Though not FDA approved, studies have shown some benefit for using stem cells for orthopedic applications, particularly arthritis of the knees. (Using stem cells for such orthopedic uses, without the need to stimulate them to become cartilage cells beforehand, appears to be the exception to the rule. Remember most stem cells need to be specialized before being used.) That’s it! Aside from this, most other uses for stem cells should only be considered either highly experimental or highly suspect of exaggerated benefits. Could there be other beneficial treatments that are not FDA approved? Perhaps, but it’s important to realize that the claims have often far outpaced the science.

So how is one to know? Here are some things to consider when choosing providers of stem cell treatments, as well as red flags, to tell you if there are better places to go for your health care. (These points are also true for just about any other treatment):

  1. Informed consent—Every medical treatment has risks and benefits. These should be routinely discussed with you beforehand, without you needing to ask. Any practitioner who claims there are no risks, only benefits, either is not sufficiently knowledgeable or is not sufficiently honest!
  2. Can they handle the complications? —Joint injections can sometimes result in infection. These can be severe infections that can potentially destroy the joint. Such complications are not just simply treated with antibiotics, but with surgery. These stem cell treatments are better handled by an orthopedic surgeon or practitioner that has a close relationship with one, if complications should arise. Likewise, treatments involving nerves should be done by neurologists or neurosurgeons.
  3. Is the clinic adequately equipped? —Stem cells need to be handled appropriately. The transport of umbilical stem cells and improper thawing from the supplier can drastically reduce numbers, which may have a great deal to do with determining the success of the procedure. Additionally, these cells may be in a state of “shock,” unless they are appropriately re-cultured after being thawed. This allows them to re-enter a desirable growth phase again.3 This may mean having a specialized lab and microbiologist on staff to properly grow and care for the stem cells, ensuring good quality control. This usually requires a university setting, not just a small clinic or office that has a nurse to thaw the stem cells after receiving them from an overnight delivery service. Glitzy web sites, colorful brochures, and informational dinners are not enough.
  4. Guinea pigs and rats are “experimented on,” people go through “clinical trials.” —Please avoid any practitioner who says they are doing experiments. Clinical trials involving people, which have the oversight of ethics boards, only occur after experiments on animals have shown low risk of harm, and a good chance of success. If a treatment is very effective, the FDA has suggested that as few as 42 participants can demonstrate adequate safety to grant approval. This is not an outrageously high threshold to overcome. Additionally, patients involved in clinical trials are usually only expected to cover minimal costs, if any. Practitioners who “experiment” on people rarely do it for free.4
  5. Realistic claims. —Does your practitioner claim 100 percent success? If so, it is better to run away (if your knees will allow you to) than to simply walk away! Knee treatments, for example, may only delay knee replacements for many people. Some may avoid surgery, but certainly not all. Do not expect a cure. Also, do they make claims well outside of what is commonly recognized? “Cures” claimed for Alzheimers, Parkinson’s, or other ailments that are not FDA approved? I cannot totally exclude the possibility that such treatments may exist at some future time. However, these practitioners should be able to point to (and provide to you) published studies. If there is a miraculous cure, the world should be able to benefit from it, and he or she should be able to patent it, so as to reap the financial benefits of sharing their techniques and discoveries with the rest of the world. By doing so, it is independently tested and verified. Anyone who has a “secret” cure, that they alone possess, should be avoided.
  1. Does it make sense? —By simply injecting stem cells (that have not been induced by a lab into their specialty state such as nerve cells, heart cells, etc.) into the bloodstream to treat things like nerve disorders, for example, does not make sense. Clinical trials of legitimate treatments first specialize the stem cells, then directly apply them to the affected area. For example, specific types of nerve cells are injected directly into specific locations of the brain, and heart cells are injected directly into the scarred tissue of the heart. Remember the indolent adult (the unspecialized stem cell)? You can’t expect to put them on a bus (inject them into a vein), send them into the big city (the body), without instructions on what to do (leaving them unspecialized), not knowing where to go (to somehow find the diseased part of the body) and then magically expect success.
  2. The hard sell. —Are you being told that or are you made to feel that you are “missing out” if you decline? Do the clinic advertisements have testimonial bylines, something to the effect of “Individual results may vary, and testimonials are not claimed to represent typical results and are not intended to represent or guarantee that anyone will achieve the same or similar results…”? As the old adage goes, if it’s too good to be true (especially if they actually tell you so), then it probably is. In these cases, consider the claims to be most likely somewhat exaggerated, and also consider working with someone who can give a more honest set of expectations.

I pray that God may grant you wisdom: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –Jas 1:5.

Hari ini, saya ingin melanjutkan dan mungkin menyelesaikan pembahasan kita tentang Kedokteran Regeneratif. Saya ingin mempertimbangkan bagaimana keadaannya saat ini, dan bagaimana orang Kristen dapat menavigasi labirin perawatan yang rumit. Seperti yang mungkin Anda ingat, dalam edisi majalah sebelumnya kita membahas bahwa Kedokteran Regeneratif adalah upaya manusia untuk menciptakan kembali sistem organ. Kita menjelaskan bagaimana jaringan janin pernah dicoba untuk digunakan karena tingkat penolakannya rendah pada orang yang menerimanya. Dari segi medis, hal ini bermasalah karena, jika digunakan dalam skala besar, akan dibutuhkan banyak janin yang diaborsi. Belakangan, sel punca embrionik dipelajari secara mendalam. Dalam hal ini, embrio—manusia yang baru dikandung dalam tahap paling awal—dibedah (dipotong-potong), lalu sel puncanya diambil.

Bayangkan sel punca sebagai orang dewasa yang malas dan belum matang, tinggal di ruang bawah tanah rumah orang tua mereka, tanpa arah dan tidak tahu apa yang ingin mereka lakukan dalam hidup. Dengan sedikit dorongan dan arahan, akhirnya mereka dapat menemukan jalan, memperoleh keterampilan khusus dan peran penting dalam hidup. Demikian pula, para ilmuwan telah menemukan cara untuk “memprogram” sel punca ini, “mendorongnya” agar menjadi jenis sel khusus, seperti sel saraf, jantung, darah, dan sel penghasil insulin. Sel-sel ini kemudian akan dikembangkan di laboratorium, lalu digunakan untuk memperbaiki atau mengganti jaringan yang sakit atau cedera.

Namun, “mengambil” sel punca dari embrio mengakibatkan kematian embrio tersebut. Hal ini jelas bermasalah bagi orang Kristen, karena salah satu dari tujuh hal yang dikatakan Tuhan sebagai kekejian ialah …tangan yang menumpahkan darah orang yang tidak bersalah –Ams 6:17. Selain itu, perintah keenam menyatakan, Jangan membunuh –Kel 20:13. Karena keberatan-keberatan ini diakui oleh komunitas ilmiah, muncul tekanan untuk menemukan alternatif.

Rasul Paulus menyatakan, Pencobaan-pencobaan yang kamu alami ialah pencobaan-pencobaan biasa, yang tidak melebihi kekuatan manusia. Sebab Allah setia dan karena itu Ia tidak akan membiarkan kamu dicobai melampaui kekuatanmu. Pada waktu kamu dicobai Ia akan memberikan kepadamu jalan ke luar, sehingga kamu dapat menanggungnya –1Kor 10:13. Perkataannya sama benarnya hari ini seperti 2000 tahun yang lalu. Orang Kristen menderita penyakit sama seringnya dengan orang non-Kristen, tetapi pengobatan modern dapat menghadirkan “godaan” berupa perawatan dan kelegaan dari penyakit atau cedera yang sesungguhnya tidak bermoral. Namun, Allah setia, dan jalan keluar-Nya ada dua. Yang terutama, Dia mengutus Anak-Nya untuk menanggung beban kita. Kepada Tabib Agung inilah kita harus selalu berpaling terlebih dahulu.

Dalam kasus perawatan sel punca, ternyata sel punca yang belum matang ini tidak hanya ditemukan dalam embrio manusia, tetapi juga ada pada semua orang, dari bayi hingga orang dewasa. Ini mungkin merupakan “jalan keluar” jasmani bagi anak-anak-Nya yang setia. Sel punca yang belum matang ini (biasanya diperoleh dari jaringan lemak atau sumsum tulang pasien) dapat dikembangkan, dikultur, dan digunakan sama baiknya dengan sel punca embrionik. Ternyata, “Sel Punca Dewasa” secara klinis justru lebih efektif, karena “dirancang khusus” untuk setiap individu dan berasal dari tubuh orang itu sendiri; karena itu, masalah penolakan sangat kecil.

Sel punca tali pusat juga terbukti bermanfaat, khususnya dalam perawatan tulang dan tulang rawan. Sebagaimana ada kendala yang harus diatasi dalam penggunaan sel punca embrionik, demikian pula ada masalah dalam mengembangkan perawatan dengan sel punca dewasa atau sel punca tali pusat. Pikirkan kembali sel punca sebagai orang dewasa yang belum matang dan malas. Hanya membuatnya “bergaul” dengan seorang ahli pertukangan tidak akan menjadikannya ahli pertukangan jika yang dilakukannya hanya mencari hiburan di ponselnya. Sel punca, seperti seorang magang, membutuhkan pelatihan dan arahan yang intensif serta terarah agar menjadi spesialis di bidang keahlian yang dipilihnya. Mempelajari cara mengaktifkan “sakelar” ini mungkin merupakan salah satu tantangan terbesar. Gagasan utamanya di sini adalah bahwa menyuntikkan begitu saja sel punca yang belum “diprogram” atau “dilatih” ke dalam jaringan yang rusak atau sakit tidak akan otomatis membuatnya “tahu” akan menjadi apa atau bagaimana ia harus berfungsi.

Demikian pula, menempatkan seorang magang muda di bidang elektronika begitu saja di dalam bus yang menuju kota yang baru saja mengalami kegagalan jaringan listrik tidak akan memulihkan aliran listrik. Dalam perumpamaan ini, sel punca ditempatkan di otak korban stroke atau korban kecelakaan yang mengalami paraplegia, dengan harapan sel punca itu akan “tahu” apa yang harus dilakukan dan sambungan khusus mana yang perlu diperbaiki untuk memulihkan fungsi tubuh. Hal ini mungkin tidak berhasil seperti yang diharapkan. Mengharapkan keberhasilan akan sia-sia kecuali dan sampai masalah-masalah ini juga ditangani.

Lalu ada masalah berkelanjutan berupa anak-anak muda yang bersemangat ini (sel punca) tidak tahu kapan harus berhenti. Masalah jaringan janin yang berubah menjadi tumor kanker juga merupakan masalah yang harus ditangani dalam penggunaan sel punca. Dengan mempertimbangkan hal ini, ada satu pengecualian: sel punca tali pusat pada umumnya tidak diketahui berubah menjadi ganas.1

Berikut daftar singkat perawatan yang sedang dikembangkan dengan menggunakan sel punca:

  • Degenerasi Makula—Memperbaiki retina yang rusak.
  • Cedera Sumsum Tulang Belakang/Stroke—Memperbaiki jaringan saraf.
  • Luka Bakar—Memperbaiki jaringan kulit.
  • Gagal Jantung Kongestif—Memperbaiki jaringan jantung yang rusak.
  • Diabetes—Mengganti atau menambah jaringan pankreas yang menghasilkan insulin.
  • Artritis—Memperbaiki tulang rawan yang rusak.
  • Penyakit autoimun (Lupus, Sklerosis Multipel)—Menghancurkan sistem kekebalan yang menyerang tubuhnya sendiri dan menggantinya atau “mengatur ulang”-nya dengan sistem kekebalan baru yang berasal dari sel punca sendiri.
  • Leukemia—Menghancurkan sel darah kanker dan menggantinya dengan sel darah baru yang berasal dari sel punca.
  • Organ baru—Mengganti organ yang sakit, rusak, atau dipenuhi kanker, seperti ginjal, hati, atau pankreas, dengan organ yang berasal dari sel punca pasien sendiri, dikembangkan di laboratorium, dan ditransplantasikan melalui pembedahan, tanpa perlu obat anti-penolakan.

Seperti yang Anda lihat, ada daftar penyakit dan gangguan yang sangat panjang yang mungkin dapat ditangani secara efektif dengan sel punca. Saya sangat optimistis bahwa dalam satu dasawarsa, pengobatan untuk banyak gangguan ini akan tersedia secara luas. Namun, perlu waktu untuk mempelajari cara membuat sel punca terspesialisasi secara ahli menjadi jenis jaringan tertentu, cara mengaktifkan sel punca lalu menonaktifkannya pada saat yang diperlukan (setelah tugasnya selesai), dan cara “mengajari” sel punca di mana dan bagaimana melakukan perbaikan.

Saya bukan satu-satunya yang antusias dengan berbagai kemungkinan ini. Itulah sebabnya ratusan klinik sel punca bermunculan di seluruh negeri, berusaha ikut mengambil bagian dalam antusiasme ini. Namun, apakah klaim klinik-klinik tersebut sesuai dengan kenyataan? Klinik mana yang dapat dipercaya? Saya tahu banyak klinik menawarkan perawatan sel punca untuk berbagai gangguan, jadi sekarang mari kita melihat beberapa perawatan yang tersedia saat ini—perawatan yang memiliki bukti benar-benar membantu, serta harapan yang realistis. Mari kita juga melihat beberapa kemungkinan komplikasinya agar kita dapat mengambil keputusan yang tepat berdasarkan informasi.

Pertama, risiko dan komplikasi

  • Masuknya infeksi—Misalnya, bakteri yang hidup di kulit dapat masuk ke rongga sendi melalui suntikan sederhana, sehingga mengakibatkan kerusakan sendi, bahkan dalam kondisi yang paling bersih sekalipun.
  • Sel punca berpindah dari tempat penyuntikan dan tidak menuju tempat yang dimaksudkan atau tidak tetap terbatas pada area perawatan tertentu—Sebuah penelitian yang melibatkan babi yang diberi suntikan sel punca ke area jantung yang rusak setelah serangan jantung menunjukkan pemulihan fungsi yang hampir sempurna, tetapi jaringan jantung baru itu terus tumbuh hingga akhirnya memenuhi ruang pemompaan jantung, sehingga semua babi tersebut mati.
  • Sel punca berubah menjadi jenis sel yang tidak terduga atau tidak sesuai—Sel punca yang digunakan untuk tujuan kosmetik wajah ternyata berubah menjadi tulang.2
  • Pertumbuhan tumor—Ada kasus terdokumentasi mengenai berbagai tumor, termasuk tumor otak dan ginjal, yang berkembang setelah pasien dirawat dengan sel punca untuk stroke dan gagal ginjal.
  • Tidak bekerja sesuai harapan—Ada kasus terdokumentasi mengenai orang dengan degenerasi makula yang dirawat dengan suntikan sel punca ke dalam mata, dan akibatnya mengalami kebutaan.
  • Sel punca tidak dapat ditarik kembali—Tidak seperti obat seperti pil atau suntikan, jika terjadi kesalahan, seseorang tidak bisa begitu saja meniadakan dosis berikutnya. Setelah sel punca dimasukkan, sel itu tidak dapat diambil kembali. Perjalanan yang telah dimulai akan terus berlanjut.

Tingkat komplikasi sulit diketahui, karena tidak ada kewajiban pelaporan ketika prosedur dilakukan di luar penelitian klinis formal.

Selanjutnya, manfaat yang diketahui

FDA (Badan Pengawas Obat dan Makanan pemerintah yang bertugas menjaga keselamatan kesehatan) telah menyetujui perawatan sel punca untuk puluhan kanker darah (leukemia) dan penyakit darah dengan menggunakan sel punca tali pusat. Meskipun belum disetujui FDA, penelitian menunjukkan adanya beberapa manfaat penggunaan sel punca untuk keperluan ortopedi, khususnya artritis lutut. (Penggunaan sel punca untuk keperluan ortopedi seperti itu, tanpa perlu merangsangnya terlebih dahulu agar menjadi sel tulang rawan, tampaknya merupakan pengecualian terhadap kaidah umum. Ingat, sebagian besar sel punca perlu dikhususkan sebelum digunakan.) Hanya itu! Selain hal ini, sebagian besar penggunaan sel punca lainnya hanya boleh dianggap sebagai sangat eksperimental atau sangat patut dicurigai manfaatnya dibesar-besarkan. Mungkinkah ada perawatan bermanfaat lain yang belum disetujui FDA? Mungkin, tetapi penting untuk menyadari bahwa klaim sering kali jauh melampaui bukti ilmiah.

Jadi, bagaimana kita mengetahuinya? Berikut beberapa hal yang perlu dipertimbangkan saat memilih penyedia perawatan sel punca, serta tanda bahaya yang menunjukkan apakah ada tempat yang lebih baik untuk memperoleh layanan kesehatan. (Hal-hal ini juga berlaku untuk hampir semua perawatan lain):

  1. Persetujuan berdasarkan informasi—Setiap perawatan medis memiliki risiko dan manfaat. Hal-hal ini seharusnya dibahas secara rutin dengan Anda sebelumnya, tanpa perlu Anda tanyakan. Praktisi mana pun yang menyatakan tidak ada risiko, hanya manfaat, berarti pengetahuannya tidak memadai atau ia tidak cukup jujur!
  2. Apakah mereka mampu menangani komplikasi? —Suntikan ke sendi terkadang dapat mengakibatkan infeksi. Infeksi tersebut dapat parah dan berpotensi merusak sendi. Komplikasi seperti itu tidak cukup ditangani hanya dengan antibiotik, tetapi memerlukan pembedahan. Perawatan sel punca ini sebaiknya ditangani oleh dokter bedah ortopedi atau praktisi yang memiliki hubungan erat dengan dokter bedah ortopedi, jika terjadi komplikasi. Demikian pula, perawatan yang melibatkan saraf seharusnya dilakukan oleh dokter spesialis saraf atau bedah saraf.
  3. Apakah klinik memiliki perlengkapan yang memadai? —Sel punca harus ditangani dengan semestinya. Pengangkutan sel punca tali pusat dan pencairan yang tidak benar oleh pemasok dapat mengurangi jumlahnya secara drastis, yang mungkin sangat menentukan keberhasilan prosedur. Selain itu, sel-sel ini mungkin berada dalam keadaan “syok” kecuali dikultur ulang dengan semestinya setelah dicairkan. Hal ini memungkinkan sel-sel itu kembali memasuki fase pertumbuhan yang diinginkan.3 Ini mungkin berarti diperlukan laboratorium khusus dan ahli mikrobiologi sebagai staf untuk mengembangkan dan merawat sel punca dengan benar, serta memastikan kendali mutu yang baik. Hal ini biasanya memerlukan lingkungan universitas, bukan sekadar klinik atau kantor kecil yang memiliki perawat untuk mencairkan sel punca setelah menerimanya melalui jasa pengiriman semalam. Situs web yang mencolok, brosur berwarna-warni, dan jamuan makan malam informatif tidaklah cukup.
  4. Marmut dan tikus “dijadikan bahan eksperimen”; manusia menjalani “uji klinis”. —Hindari praktisi mana pun yang mengatakan bahwa mereka sedang melakukan eksperimen. Uji klinis yang melibatkan manusia dan diawasi oleh dewan etik hanya dilakukan setelah eksperimen pada hewan menunjukkan rendahnya risiko bahaya dan peluang keberhasilan yang baik. Jika suatu perawatan sangat efektif, FDA telah menyatakan bahwa hanya dengan 42 peserta pun keamanan yang memadai dapat dibuktikan untuk memperoleh persetujuan. Ambang batas ini tidaklah terlalu tinggi untuk dicapai. Selain itu, pasien yang terlibat dalam uji klinis biasanya hanya diharapkan menanggung biaya minimal, jika ada. Praktisi yang “bereksperimen” pada manusia jarang melakukannya secara gratis.4
  5. Klaim yang realistis. —Apakah praktisi Anda mengklaim keberhasilan 100 persen? Jika demikian, lebih baik lari menjauh (jika lutut Anda memungkinkan) daripada sekadar berjalan menjauh! Perawatan lutut, misalnya, mungkin hanya menunda operasi penggantian lutut bagi banyak orang. Sebagian orang mungkin dapat menghindari operasi, tetapi tentu tidak semuanya. Jangan berharap akan sembuh. Selain itu, apakah mereka membuat klaim yang jauh melampaui hal-hal yang diakui secara umum? Klaim “penyembuhan” Alzheimer, Parkinson, atau gangguan lain yang belum disetujui FDA? Saya tidak dapat sepenuhnya menutup kemungkinan bahwa perawatan semacam itu mungkin tersedia pada suatu waktu di masa depan. Namun, praktisi seperti ini seharusnya dapat menunjuk pada (dan memberikan kepada Anda) penelitian yang telah diterbitkan. Jika ada penyembuhan ajaib, dunia seharusnya dapat memperoleh manfaat darinya, dan praktisi tersebut seharusnya dapat mematenkannya agar memperoleh keuntungan finansial dari berbagi teknik dan penemuannya dengan seluruh dunia. Dengan demikian, hasilnya dapat diuji dan diverifikasi secara independen. Siapa pun yang memiliki penyembuhan “rahasia” yang hanya dimilikinya sendiri sebaiknya dihindari.
  1. Apakah masuk akal? —Menyuntikkan begitu saja sel punca (yang belum diarahkan di laboratorium untuk menjadi jenis sel khusus seperti sel saraf, sel jantung, dan sebagainya) ke dalam aliran darah untuk menangani hal-hal seperti gangguan saraf, misalnya, tidak masuk akal. Uji klinis untuk perawatan yang sah terlebih dahulu mengkhususkan sel punca, lalu menerapkannya langsung pada area yang terdampak. Misalnya, jenis sel saraf tertentu disuntikkan langsung ke lokasi tertentu di otak, dan sel jantung disuntikkan langsung ke jaringan jantung yang memiliki jaringan parut. Ingat orang dewasa yang malas (sel punca yang belum dikhususkan)? Anda tidak dapat berharap memasukkannya ke dalam bus (menyuntikkannya ke pembuluh darah), mengirimnya ke kota besar (tubuh), tanpa petunjuk tentang apa yang harus dilakukan (membiarkannya tanpa spesialisasi), tanpa mengetahui ke mana harus pergi (agar entah bagaimana menemukan bagian tubuh yang sakit), lalu secara ajaib mengharapkan keberhasilan.
  2. Tekanan penjualan yang agresif. —Apakah Anda diberi tahu, atau dibuat merasa bahwa Anda akan “kehilangan kesempatan” jika menolak? Apakah iklan klinik mencantumkan keterangan pada testimoni yang kurang lebih berbunyi, “Hasil tiap individu dapat berbeda, dan testimoni tidak dimaksudkan untuk menunjukkan hasil yang lazim serta tidak dimaksudkan untuk menyatakan atau menjamin bahwa siapa pun akan memperoleh hasil yang sama atau serupa…”? Seperti kata pepatah lama, jika sesuatu terlalu bagus untuk menjadi kenyataan (terutama jika mereka memang mengatakan demikian kepada Anda), kemungkinan besar memang begitu. Dalam kasus seperti ini, anggaplah klaim-klaim tersebut kemungkinan besar agak dilebih-lebihkan, dan pertimbangkan juga untuk bekerja sama dengan seseorang yang dapat memberikan harapan yang lebih jujur.

Saya berdoa agar Allah mengaruniakan hikmat kepada Anda: Jikalau di antara kamu ada yang kekurangan hikmat, hendaklah ia memintakannya kepada Allah, yang memberikan kepada semua orang dengan murah hati dan dengan tidak membangkit-bangkit; maka hal itu akan diberikan kepadanya –Yak 1:5.

Catatan Khusus:

Ada beberapa orang tua yang menyatakan minat untuk membawa anak-anak mereka ke Jepang agar divaksinasi di sana, jika kita tidak dapat mengirimkan vaksin ke Amerika Serikat. Jika ada pembaca majalah ini yang juga berminat, silakan hubungi The Berean Voice agar kita dapat merencanakan dan mengoordinasikannya. Informasi kontak dapat ditemukan di bagian dalam sampul depan setiap eksemplar majalah The Heartbeat of the Remnant.

A glorious morning unfolds before me, perfect and peaceful, unmarred by failure. The sky is clear and blue. The horizon is a soft, blushing pink, enhanced by a misty fog. The distant hills and trees are shaded a dusky blue in the misty morning coolness. The morning is ringing with the warbling, twittering, chirping of birds. The grass glows with millions of dew droplets sparkling in the morning light. The pink horizon above the distant, dusky hills gradually fades into a glowing orange sphere that becomes brighter and brighter.

I stand in awe of God. My heart is thrilled at the beauty spread out before me. I am also thrilled at what God has done in my life, and the beauty He has created out of ashes.

I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. God has brought me up out of the pit of despair and discouragement. He has set my feet upon the Rock, Jesus Christ, and He has established my goings. He knows the plans He has for me. His thoughts and His ways are much higher than mine.

He hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. I desire that God will be glorified through the work He has done and is continuing to do in my life. Many, O Lord, are Thy wonderful works which Thou hast done, and Thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto Thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

I delight to do Thy will, O God: yea, Thy law is within my heart. It is truly my delight to do the will of God; to love Him with my whole heart, soul, strength, and mind; to obey His commandments from my heart.

I have not hid Thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared Thy faithfulness and Thy salvation: I have not concealed Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth from the great congregation. It is such a blessing to have deep and edifying conversations with my brothers and sisters in the Lord, and to share together what the Lord is doing in our lives. It is a great strengthening to my faith.

Withhold not Thy tender mercies from me, O Lord: let Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth continually preserve me. Temptations and hard tests are a very real thing in life; the struggle to keep my heart with a diligence, the battle against stubborn pride, and the urge to utter hasty words of frustration. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me. Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.

The sun has risen above the distant hills and the countryside is now glowing gloriously. The mist has faded into the woods and the distant dusky blue hills and trees have exchanged their robes for vivid shades of green intermixed with hints of red and brown. The sparkling droplets of dew are dazzling in the brilliant sunlight.

Let those that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: let such as love Thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified. I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: Thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

עזרי ומצילי

תהילים מ׳:1 קַוֹּה קִוִּיתִי לַיהוָה וַיֵּט אֵלַי וַיִּשְׁמַע שַׁוְעָתִי. 2 וַיַּעֲלֵנִי מִבּוֹר שָׁאוֹן מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן וַיָּקֶם עַל־סֶלַע רַגְלַי כּוֹנֵן אֲשֻׁרָי. 3 וַיִּתֵּן בְּפִי שִׁיר חָדָשׁ תְּהִלָּה לֵאלֹהֵינוּ יִרְאוּ רַבִּים וְיִירָאוּ וְיִבְטְחוּ בַּיהוָה. 4 אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר אֲשֶׁר־שָׂם יְהוָה מִבְטַחוֹ וְלֹא־פָנָה אֶל־רְהָבִים וְשָׂטֵי כָזָב. 5 רַבּוֹת עָשִׂיתָ אַתָּה יְהוָה אֱלֹהַי נִפְלְאֹתֶיךָ וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ אֵלֵינוּ אֵין עֲרֹךְ אֵלֶיךָ אַגִּידָה וַאֲדַבֵּרָה עָצְמוּ מִסַּפֵּר. 6 זֶבַח וּמִנְחָה לֹא־חָפַצְתָּ אָזְנַיִם כָּרִיתָ לִּי עוֹלָה וַחֲטָאָה לֹא שָׁאָלְתָּ. 7 אָז אָמַרְתִּי הִנֵּה־בָאתִי בִּמְגִלַּת־סֵפֶר כָּתוּב עָלָי. 8 לַעֲשׂוֹת־רְצוֹנְךָ אֱלֹהַי חָפָצְתִּי וְתוֹרָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ מֵעָי. 9 בִּשַּׂרְתִּי צֶדֶק בְּקָהָל רָב הִנֵּה שְׂפָתַי לֹא אֶכְלָא יְהוָה אַתָּה יָדָעְתָּ. 10 צִדְקָתְךָ לֹא־כִסִּיתִי בְּתוֹךְ לִבִּי אֱמוּנָתְךָ וִישׁוּעָתְךָ אָמָרְתִּי לֹא־כִחַדְתִּי חַסְדְּךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ לְקָהָל רָב. 11 אַתָּה יְהוָה לֹא־תִכְלָא רַחֲמֶיךָ מִמֶּנִּי חַסְדְּךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ תָּמִיד יִצְּרוּנִי. 12 כִּי אָפְפוּ עָלַי רָעוֹת עַד־אֵין מִסְפָּר הִשִּׂיגוּנִי עֲוֹנֹתַי וְלֹא־יָכֹלְתִּי לִרְאוֹת עָצְמוּ מִשַּׂעֲרוֹת רֹאשִׁי וְלִבִּי עֲזָבָנִי. 13 רְצֵה יְהוָה לְהַצִּילֵנִי יְהוָה לְעֶזְרָתִי חוּשָׁה. 14 יֵבֹשׁוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ יַחַד מְבַקְשֵׁי נַפְשִׁי לִסְפּוֹתָהּ יִסֹּגוּ אָחוֹר וְיִכָּלְמוּ חֲפֵצֵי רָעָתִי. 15 יָשֹׁמּוּ עַל־עֵקֶב בָּשְׁתָּם הָאֹמְרִים לִי הֶאָח הֶאָח. 16 יָשִׂישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְחוּ בְךָ כָּל־מְבַקְשֶׁיךָ יֹאמְרוּ תָמִיד יִגְדַּל יְהוָה אֹהֲבֵי יְשׁוּעָתֶךָ. 17 וַאֲנִי עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אֲדֹנָי יַחֲשָׁב לִי עֶזְרָתִי וּמְפַלְטִי אַתָּה אֱלֹהַי אַל־תְּאַחַר.

בוקר נהדר נפרש לפניי, מושלם ושלו, ללא פגם של כישלון. השמיים בהירים וכחולים. האופק ורוד ורך, ומוסיף לו ערפל קל. הגבעות והעצים הרחוקים נצבעים בכחול כהה באוויר הקריר והמעורפל של הבוקר. הבוקר מצלצל בקולות ציוץ, שריקה ופכפוך של ציפורים. הדשא זוהר במיליוני טיפות טל נוצצות באור הבוקר. האופק הוורוד שמעל הגבעות הכהות והרחוקות הולך ומתחלף בכדור כתום זוהר, שהולך ומתבהר.

אני עומדת ביראת כבוד לפני אלוהים. לבי מתרגש מן היופי הפרוש לפניי. אני מתרגשת גם ממה שאלוהים עשה בחיי, ומהיופי שיצר מתוך האפר.

קַוֹּה קִוִּיתִי לַיהוָה וַיֵּט אֵלַי וַיִּשְׁמַע שַׁוְעָתִי. וַיַּעֲלֵנִי מִבּוֹר שָׁאוֹן מִטִּיט הַיָּוֵן וַיָּקֶם עַל־סֶלַע רַגְלַי כּוֹנֵן אֲשֻׁרָי. אלוהים העלה אותי מבור הייאוש והרפיון. הוא העמיד את רגליי על הסלע, ישוע המשיח, וכונן את דרכיי. הוא יודע אילו תוכניות יש לו עבורי. מחשבותיו ודרכיו גבוהות הרבה יותר משלי.

וַיִּתֵּן בְּפִי שִׁיר חָדָשׁ תְּהִלָּה לֵאלֹהֵינוּ יִרְאוּ רַבִּים וְיִירָאוּ וְיִבְטְחוּ בַּיהוָה. אני רוצה שאלוהים יתפאר באמצעות העבודה שעשה ומוסיף לעשות בחיי. רַבּוֹת עָשִׂיתָ אַתָּה אֲדֹנָי נִפְלְאֹתֶיךָ וּמַחְשְׁבוֹתֶיךָ אֵלֵינוּ אֵין עֲרֹךְ אֵלֶיךָ אַגִּידָה וַאֲדַבֵּרָה עָצְמוּ מִסַּפֵּר.

לַעֲשׂוֹת־רְצוֹנְךָ אֱלֹהַי חָפָצְתִּי וְתוֹרָתְךָ בְּתוֹךְ לִבִּי. אכן, שמחתי היא לעשות את רצון אלוהים; לאהוב אותו בכל לבי, נפשי, כוחי ושכלי; לציית למצוותיו מכל הלב.

צִדְקָתְךָ לֹא־כִסִּיתִי בְּתוֹךְ לִבִּי אֱמוּנָתְךָ וִישׁוּעָתְךָ אָמָרְתִּי לֹא־כִחַדְתִּי חַסְדְּךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ לְקָהָל רָב. זו ברכה גדולה לנהל שיחות עמוקות ובונות עם אחיי ואחיותיי באמונה, ולשתף יחד במה שהאדון עושה בחיינו. הדבר מחזק מאוד את אמונתי.

אַתָּה אֲדֹנָי לֹא־תִכְלָא רַחֲמֶיךָ מִמֶּנִּי חַסְדְּךָ וַאֲמִתְּךָ תָּמִיד יִצְּרוּנִי. פיתויים ומבחנים קשים הם מציאות של ממש בחיים; המאבק לשמור על לבי בשקידה, המלחמה בגאווה עיקשת והדחף לומר דברים נמהרים מתוך תסכול. רְצֵה אֲדֹנָי לְהַצִּילֵנִי אֲדֹנָי לְעֶזְרָתִי חוּשָׁה. יֵבֹשׁוּ וְיַחְפְּרוּ יַחַד מְבַקְשֵׁי נַפְשִׁי לִסְפּוֹתָהּ יִסֹּגוּ אָחוֹר וְיִכָּלְמוּ חֲפֵצֵי רָעָתִי.

השמש עלתה מעל הגבעות הרחוקות והנוף הכפרי זוהר עכשיו להפליא. הערפל נסוג אל תוך היערות, והגבעות והעצים הרחוקים, שצבעם היה כחול כהה, החליפו את גלימותיהם בגוונים עזים של ירוק, המשולבים בנגיעות של אדום וחום. טיפות הטל הנוצצות מסנוורות באור השמש הבוהק.

יָשִׂישׂוּ וְיִשְׂמְחוּ בְךָ כָּל־מְבַקְשֶׁיךָ יֹאמְרוּ תָמִיד יִגְדַּל יְהוָה אֹהֲבֵי יְשׁוּעָתֶךָ. וַאֲנִי עָנִי וְאֶבְיוֹן אֲדֹנָי יַחֲשָׁב לִי עֶזְרָתִי וּמְפַלְטִי אַתָּה אֱלֹהַי אַל־תְּאַחַר.

If we step back and look at our own life, can we honestly say that we trust in the Lord with all our heart? I often think of my children—they trust in me with all their hearts; there is no fear within them; they do not worry. My prayer is that I can trust in my Heavenly Father in the same way.

Here in Haiti a lot of people are driven by fear. They fear the uncertainty of tomorrow. They fear whether they will find food, work, and clothing. It is the opposite of trusting in God. In the western culture, people don’t fear those things. Food and clothing are easy to find, jobs are plentiful, and medical assistance is just one 911 call away.

The poor people here in Haiti say that it would be easier to trust God if they were in America, but is that truly the case? While very few in America fear whether they will have enough to eat, many fear whether they will be accepted by other people. There are some who may fear having enough money to live, but there are many who fear death. Whatever our fear is, trusting in God is our answer.

Let’s look at the life of David. David was a young boy. When his older brothers went to battle, young David went out to feed his father’s sheep. On the battlefield, there was a giant with the Philistine army named Goliath. He challenged the Israelites by saying that if one man would come out and fight him, the victor’s army would rule the other side. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 we read that Goliath said, …I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

Later on, we read that Jesse, David’s father, sent him to the place of battle to take some food to his older brothers. David arrived at the place of battle, and he heard Goliath speaking these same words. When David saw that the men of Israel were all afraid, he did not understand. Why were God’s people afraid of this uncircumcised Philistine?

Even though David was young, he was no amateur when it came to putting his trust in God. While he was watching his father’s sheep, most likely he talked much with God, asking Him to help guard the sheep. One day a bear came out to attack the sheep, and David killed the bear. Another day a lion came out to eat some sheep. Again, the God-trusting, fearless youth faced the threat and killed the lion. Now, facing a seemingly greater threat, David simply asks, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1Sa 17:26. David went to King Saul and said, I …will go and fight with this Philistine –1Sa 17:32. Once more putting his trust in his God, David took five smooth stones, ran out to meet the giant, and killed him. Upon seeing this sudden turn of events, the people marveled.

According to Psalm 20:7, when we put our trust in horses and chariots, then it is not in the Lord our God. In Matthew 21:21, the Bible says that with faith we can move mountains. Here in Haiti I have found myself in tough situations where God is my only option. When I have been forced to put my trust in God, I have discovered that He still works miracles. Just like David with the lion, the bear, and the giant, we too can learn that trusting God with our whole heart is the best way and not just a last resort. When we trust in the Lord first, we show the world something amazing—that this God we serve is alive, and that He is real.

Here in Haiti there was a man living in a shack up in the mountains with his wife and three young children. But there was a problem—he was deathly ill. One day he heard about a missionary who often traveled through the mountains. I received a message from him stating that he was almost dead and that he needed me to come and pray for him. I quickly went up to his home. I was amazed at his condition. His weight was probably not much more than 70 pounds. His wife told me that he had been in bed for over a year. He couldn’t talk, he only whispered with deep agonizing breaths. We spent quite a while discussing his life, his sin, and his future. He told me that if God would heal him, he would serve him and trust him for the rest of his life. I believed his sincerity, yet I was scared. I began to pray, but it was certainly not a powerful prayer full of faith. Rather it was a weak, humble cry.

As I went home and throughout that night, he was all I could think about. The devil began his attack. I had many confusing, troubling thoughts, “Did you do everything you could have done? What if he dies? Why didn’t you take him to the hospital?” I went to God in prayer. “Oh God,” I prayed, “this man wanted prayer. He didn’t ask for a hospital; he didn’t ask for medication. Please God, heal this man. If he dies, what will I do the next time? O Father, if not for him, please, heal him for me. I need you to, Father.”

I prayed like I had never prayed before, and then, God gave me peace. The next morning, I hurried up the mountain to his home, but he wasn’t there. “No, Lord!” I thought. I rushed around and poked my head in another shack. What I saw overwhelmed me. He was sitting there with a big smile on his face. His wife said that he had been working in the garden that morning. Repeatedly she said, “God healed him! God healed him!” I’ll never forget the feeling I had as I travelled back down that mountain. My heart welled up with joy and thankfulness. “My God is alive! He can do anything and everything! He is my God!” I thanked and praised Him like I never had before. “The lion” that I had faced was dead, and my faith was growing. The devil doesn’t want us to trust God, because when we put our trust in God, He does big things, and our faith grows.

When we put our trust in God there is a risk—what if God doesn’t work? We could be embarrassed, or worse—“What if I step out in faith and God does nothing?” Remember, it is not faith if we know the outcome. Faith is walking in obedience and believing God’s Word when we do not know the outcome. If God wouldn’t have helped David, Goliath surely would have killed him. It was Daniel’s faith that kept him praying to God, even though he knew a lion’s den awaited him. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had so much faith in God that they told the king that even if God chose to not deliver them from the fire, that they still would …not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up –Dan 3:18. Then there was Gideon and his three hundred men. The list goes on and on of godly men who put their life on the line, proving that their God was alive.

When we step out in faith, trusting our God, something always happens (sometimes now, sometimes later; sometimes in a way that makes sense, sometimes in a way that seems to make no earthly sense). Yet God does work, and our faith grows. When we truly believe in God, we will trust him. Then, sharing the Gospel message with others is much easier. Just like Joshua did not have a fleet of bulldozers on standby at Jericho, so also we do not need a backup plan when we trust in God.

It is true that the great minds and financial backing of many in America and other modern countries have replaced God. There is a way to do most physical things without God. In fact, most people say that trusting in God is not common sense. If you pray over a sick child, it’s not common sense. If you turn down a high paying job because you don’t believe that it’s God’s will, that’s not common sense. If you sell your possessions and give to the poor, it’s not common sense. These people are right—trusting in God is not common sense. Marching around a wall seven times, believing it will fall down, is not common sense. Going into battle with only 300 men against a great army who were like grasshoppers for multitude is not common sense either. Most things done by God-trusting Christians don’t make sense, but they do show the world that they really do put their trust in God, and that is what will turn the world upside down again, today.

I remember one day very well. I was away from home when I received a phone call from my wife. She told me to come home quickly—it was an emergency! Our two-year-old son had been stung by bees. I rushed home to see the neighborhood in chaos. People where running around everywhere. I found my wife and son at the neighbor’s house, a local pastor. My son lay in the arms of my wife who told me he had been stung several hundred times. The pastor looked at me quite gravely, telling me that if I didn’t get this boy to a hospital right away, he would surely die. I remember thinking one thing—God can heal! I picked up my son and took him across the street to our house, and I prayed. It didn’t take long before he began to recover—by the next day he was back out playing.

Many people here in Haiti take their sick to the witch doctor, and he heals them. It’s just what happens. How much more can our God do! Please don’t misunderstand me. I’m not saying we shouldn’t go to the medical doctor or to the hospital; rather, I’m trying to emphasize that our trust should be in God.

Years ago, I decided to take up a part-time job selling knives. I was to take these knives and travel from home to home. I didn’t have an interest in knives but was just trying to make some extra money. I was a terrible knife salesman. Everywhere I went everyone said no.

One day the boss took me into his office where he told me that he had noticed I wasn’t selling any knives and realized he had forgotten to show me how the knives worked. So, we sat there in his office as he talked about each knife. He had a small pile of kitchen utensils of another brand, which were known for their quality, that he used for a comparison. First, he held up a small piece of leather and asked me to cut it in half with one of the “other” knives. I sawed through the piece of leather with some ease. Then he instructed me to use one of his knives and do the same thing. The new knife sliced through the leather as if it wasn’t even there! I was truly amazed. He then picked up a penny and told me to cut it in half using the “other” scissors. I tried but failed; they simply would not cut it. He then told me to do the same using his scissors. It easily cut through the penny, and again I was amazed at the product. He told me that I now knew that these knives were the best and from now on I should be able to sell them. He was right. I began selling knives everywhere I went! I even remember walking into a poorly kept trailer home without much hope that they would buy. Surprisingly, they bought over $3,000 worth of knives.

The reason I began to make sales is obvious—I believed in my product. Likewise, if we put our trust in God, we will have confidence. In a day when most proclaiming Christians are ashamed of God and ashamed to stand up for truth, we can be a bright and shining light. We can be a people who go out into the world and into our communities with a Gospel that we truly believe in! As we do, the world will see it and respond. Many are seeking; they are looking for answers. When someone asks us a question about why we do the things we do or wear what we wear, what is our reply? Do we reply with confidence? Do we have a ready Bible verse? Or do we get embarrassed and desire a hole to climb into? If the world could see that we are confident in our God, and that we obey him with enthusiasm, it would be a powerful testimony.

I remember traveling through the airport with a small group. As we were standing in line, I overheard a lady ask one of the single sisters in our group why she wore that “thing” on her head. I was excited to listen unnoticed, and I rejoiced as I heard her response. “Have you ever read 1 Corinthians 11? There it instructs us that women should cover their heads. It’s a sign of submission.” The woman was shocked at her answer, saying she never heard that before, and that her father was a pastor. They continued to have a very interesting conversation that ended with that lady desiring to go home and study her Bible.

A tract can do a lot of good; so likewise, a powerful sermon or a printed article, but someone putting all his trust in God is what this world is looking for! They want to “see something that works,” and why not? Our God wants to use us to show Himself strong. Surely each one of us wants to be used by God. We can. Each one of us can. The answer is to trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding –Pro 3:5.

Si hacemos una pausa y examinamos nuestra propia vida, ¿podemos decir sinceramente que confiamos en el Señor con todo nuestro corazón? A menudo pienso en mis hijos: confían en mí con todo su corazón; no tienen miedo ni se preocupan. Mi oración es poder confiar en mi Padre celestial de la misma manera.

Aquí en Haití, muchas personas viven dominadas por el miedo. Temen la incertidumbre del mañana. Temen no encontrar comida, trabajo y ropa. Es lo contrario de confiar en Dios. En la cultura occidental, la gente no teme esas cosas. Es fácil conseguir comida y ropa, hay muchos empleos y basta con llamar al 911 para recibir asistencia médica.

Los pobres de aquí, en Haití, dicen que sería más fácil confiar en Dios si estuvieran en Estados Unidos, pero ¿es realmente así? Aunque muy pocos en Estados Unidos temen no tener suficiente para comer, muchos temen no ser aceptados por otras personas. Algunos quizá teman no tener suficiente dinero para vivir, pero muchos temen a la muerte. Sea cual sea nuestro miedo, confiar en Dios es la respuesta.

Veamos la vida de David. David era un muchacho. Cuando sus hermanos mayores fueron a la batalla, el joven David salió a cuidar las ovejas de su padre. En el campo de batalla había un gigante del ejército filisteo llamado Goliat. Desafió a los israelitas diciendo que, si un hombre salía a luchar contra él, el ejército del vencedor dominaría al otro bando. En 1 Samuel 17:10-11 leemos que Goliat dijo: …Hoy desafío a los ejércitos de Israel; denme un hombre para que luchemos. Cuando Saúl y todo Israel oyeron aquellas palabras del filisteo, se desalentaron y tuvieron mucho miedo.

Más adelante leemos que Isaí, el padre de David, lo envió al campo de batalla para llevar comida a sus hermanos mayores. David llegó al campo de batalla y oyó a Goliat pronunciar esas mismas palabras. Cuando David vio que todos los hombres de Israel tenían miedo, no lo entendió. ¿Por qué tenían miedo los hijos de Dios de aquel filisteo incircunciso?

Aunque David era joven, no era ningún novato cuando se trataba de poner su confianza en Dios. Mientras cuidaba las ovejas de su padre, seguramente hablaba mucho con Dios y le pedía que lo ayudara a protegerlas. Un día salió un oso para atacar a las ovejas, y David mató al oso. Otro día salió un león para devorar algunas ovejas. Una vez más, el joven intrépido que confiaba en Dios enfrentó la amenaza y mató al león. Ahora, ante una amenaza que parecía aún mayor, David simplemente pregunta: …¿Quién es este filisteo incircunciso, para que desafíe a los ejércitos del Dios viviente? –1Sa 17:26. David fue al rey Saúl y dijo: Yo… iré a pelear contra este filisteo –1Sa 17:32. Confiando una vez más en su Dios, David tomó cinco piedras lisas, corrió a enfrentarse al gigante y lo mató. Al ver este giro repentino de los acontecimientos, la gente quedó maravillada.

Según Salmos 20:7, cuando ponemos nuestra confianza en los caballos y los carros, no la ponemos en el Señor nuestro Dios. En Mateo 21:21, la Biblia dice que con fe podemos mover montañas. Aquí en Haití me he encontrado en situaciones difíciles en las que Dios era mi única opción. Cuando me he visto obligado a confiar en Dios, he descubierto que Él todavía hace milagros. Al igual que David con el león, el oso y el gigante, nosotros también podemos aprender que confiar en Dios con todo nuestro corazón es lo mejor, y no solo un último recurso. Cuando confiamos primero en el Señor, mostramos algo asombroso al mundo: que este Dios a quien servimos está vivo y es real.

Aquí en Haití había un hombre que vivía en una choza en las montañas con su esposa y sus tres hijos pequeños. Pero había un problema: estaba gravemente enfermo, a punto de morir. Un día oyó hablar de un misionero que viajaba a menudo por las montañas. Recibí un mensaje suyo en el que decía que estaba casi muerto y que necesitaba que yo fuera a orar por él. Fui rápidamente a su casa. Me asombró su estado. Probablemente no pesaba mucho más de 70 libras. Su esposa me dijo que llevaba más de un año en cama. No podía hablar; solo susurraba, respirando con dificultad y agonía. Pasamos bastante tiempo hablando de su vida, de su pecado y de su futuro. Me dijo que si Dios lo sanaba, serviría a Dios y confiaría en Él el resto de su vida. Creí que era sincero, pero aun así tenía miedo. Empecé a orar, pero sin duda no fue una oración poderosa, llena de fe. Más bien, fue un clamor débil y humilde.

Al volver a casa y durante toda aquella noche, no podía dejar de pensar en él. El diablo comenzó su ataque. Me asaltaron muchos pensamientos confusos y perturbadores: «¿Hiciste todo lo que podías? ¿Y si muere? ¿Por qué no lo llevaste al hospital?». Acudí a Dios en oración. «Oh Dios», oré, «este hombre pidió oración. No pidió un hospital; no pidió medicamentos. Por favor, Dios, sana a este hombre. Si muere, ¿qué haré la próxima vez? Oh Padre, si no lo haces por él, por favor, sáname a mí de esta preocupación. Te necesito, Padre».

Oré como nunca antes había orado, y entonces Dios me dio paz. A la mañana siguiente subí deprisa la montaña hasta su casa, pero él no estaba allí. «¡No, Señor!», pensé. Corrí de un lado a otro y asomé la cabeza por otra choza. Lo que vi me dejó abrumado. Él estaba sentado allí, con una gran sonrisa en el rostro. Su esposa dijo que aquella mañana había estado trabajando en el huerto. Repetía una y otra vez: «¡Dios lo sanó! ¡Dios lo sanó!». Nunca olvidaré lo que sentí al bajar de aquella montaña. Mi corazón se llenó de alegría y gratitud. «¡Mi Dios está vivo! ¡Puede hacer cualquier cosa, puede hacerlo todo! ¡Él es mi Dios!». Le di gracias y lo alabé como nunca antes. «El león» al que me había enfrentado estaba muerto, y mi fe iba creciendo. El diablo no quiere que confiemos en Dios, porque cuando ponemos nuestra confianza en Dios, Él hace grandes cosas y nuestra fe crece.

Cuando ponemos nuestra confianza en Dios, hay un riesgo: ¿y si Dios no obra? Podríamos quedar en ridículo o, peor aún: «¿Y si doy un paso de fe y Dios no hace nada?». Recuerden: no es fe si conocemos el resultado. La fe consiste en andar en obediencia y creer la Palabra de Dios cuando no conocemos el resultado. Si Dios no hubiera ayudado a David, Goliat seguramente lo habría matado. Fue la fe de Daniel la que lo mantuvo orando a Dios, aunque sabía que lo esperaba un foso de leones. Sadrac, Mesac y Abed-nego tenían tanta fe en Dios que le dijeron al rey que, aunque Dios decidiera no librarlos del fuego, aun así …no servirían a sus dioses ni adorarían la imagen de oro que él había levantado –Dan 3:18. Luego estaban Gedeón y sus trescientos hombres. La lista de hombres piadosos que arriesgaron la vida para demostrar que su Dios estaba vivo sigue y sigue.

Cuando damos un paso de fe y confiamos en nuestro Dios, siempre sucede algo (a veces ahora, a veces más adelante; a veces de una manera que tiene sentido y, a veces, de una manera que parece no tener ningún sentido terrenal). Sin embargo, Dios sí obra y nuestra fe crece. Cuando de verdad creemos en Dios, confiaremos en Él. Entonces es mucho más fácil compartir el mensaje del Evangelio con los demás. Así como Josué no tenía una flota de excavadoras lista en Jericó, tampoco nosotros necesitamos un plan alternativo cuando confiamos en Dios.

Es cierto que las grandes mentes y el respaldo financiero de muchos en Estados Unidos y otros países modernos han reemplazado a Dios. Es posible hacer casi todas las cosas materiales sin Dios. De hecho, la mayoría dice que confiar en Dios no es de sentido común. Si oras por un hijo enfermo, no es de sentido común. Si rechazas un empleo bien remunerado porque no crees que sea la voluntad de Dios, no es de sentido común. Si vendes tus posesiones y das el dinero a los pobres, no es de sentido común. Estas personas tienen razón: confiar en Dios no es de sentido común. Marchar alrededor de una muralla siete veces creyendo que se derrumbará no es de sentido común. Tampoco lo es ir a la batalla con solo 300 hombres contra un gran ejército que era numeroso como langostas. La mayoría de las cosas que hacen los cristianos que confían en Dios no tienen sentido, pero sí muestran al mundo que realmente ponen su confianza en Dios, y eso es lo que hará que el mundo vuelva a trastornarse hoy.

Recuerdo muy bien un día. Estaba lejos de casa cuando recibí una llamada de mi esposa. Me dijo que volviera rápido a casa: ¡era una emergencia! A nuestro hijo de dos años lo habían picado las abejas. Corrí a casa y encontré el vecindario sumido en el caos. Había gente corriendo por todas partes. Encontré a mi esposa y a mi hijo en la casa de un vecino, un pastor local. Mi hijo estaba en brazos de mi esposa, quien me dijo que lo habían picado varios cientos de veces. El pastor me miró con mucha seriedad y me dijo que, si no llevaba al niño al hospital de inmediato, seguramente moriría. Recuerdo haber pensado una sola cosa: ¡Dios puede sanarlo! Tomé a mi hijo y lo llevé al otro lado de la calle, a nuestra casa, y oré. No pasó mucho tiempo antes de que empezara a recuperarse: al día siguiente ya había vuelto a salir a jugar.

Muchas personas aquí en Haití llevan a sus enfermos al brujo, y él los sana. Así es como ocurre. ¡Cuánto más puede hacer nuestro Dios! Por favor, no me malinterpreten. No digo que no debamos ir al médico o al hospital; más bien, intento recalcar que nuestra confianza debe estar en Dios.

Hace años decidí buscar un trabajo a tiempo parcial vendiendo cuchillos. Tenía que llevar esos cuchillos y viajar de casa en casa. No me interesaban los cuchillos; solo intentaba ganar un poco de dinero extra. Era un pésimo vendedor de cuchillos. Adondequiera que iba, todos decían que no.

Un día, el jefe me llevó a su oficina y me dijo que se había dado cuenta de que no estaba vendiendo ningún cuchillo y que comprendía que se había olvidado de mostrarme cómo funcionaban. Así que nos sentamos en su oficina mientras él hablaba de cada cuchillo. Tenía un pequeño montón de utensilios de cocina de otra marca, conocida por su calidad, que usaba para comparar. Primero levantó un trozo pequeño de cuero y me pidió que lo cortara por la mitad con uno de los cuchillos «de la otra marca». Serré el trozo de cuero con bastante facilidad. Luego me indicó que usara uno de sus cuchillos y que hiciera lo mismo. ¡El cuchillo nuevo cortó el cuero como si ni siquiera estuviera allí! Me quedé realmente asombrado. Después tomó una moneda de un centavo y me dijo que la cortara por la mitad con las tijeras «de la otra marca». Lo intenté, pero no pude: simplemente no la cortaban. Entonces me dijo que hiciera lo mismo con sus tijeras. Cortaron la moneda con facilidad y, una vez más, me asombró el producto. Me dijo que ahora sabía que aquellos cuchillos eran los mejores y que, de ahí en adelante, debería poder venderlos. Tenía razón. ¡Empecé a vender cuchillos adondequiera que iba! Incluso recuerdo haber entrado en una casa rodante descuidada, sin muchas esperanzas de que compraran. Para mi sorpresa, compraron cuchillos por más de 3.000 dólares.

La razón por la que empecé a vender es evidente: creía en mi producto. Del mismo modo, si ponemos nuestra confianza en Dios, tendremos seguridad. En una época en que la mayoría de quienes profesan ser cristianos se avergüenzan de Dios y de defender la verdad, podemos ser una luz resplandeciente. ¡Podemos ser un pueblo que sale al mundo y a nuestras comunidades con un Evangelio en el que verdaderamente creemos! Si lo hacemos, el mundo lo verá y responderá. Muchos están buscando; buscan respuestas. Cuando alguien nos pregunta por qué hacemos lo que hacemos o por qué vestimos como vestimos, ¿qué respondemos? ¿Respondemos con seguridad? ¿Tenemos a mano un versículo de la Biblia? ¿O nos avergonzamos y quisiéramos que la tierra nos tragara? Si el mundo pudiera ver que tenemos confianza en nuestro Dios y que lo obedecemos con entusiasmo, sería un testimonio poderoso.

Recuerdo que una vez viajaba por el aeropuerto con un pequeño grupo. Mientras estábamos en la fila, oí a una mujer preguntarle a una de las hermanas solteras de nuestro grupo por qué llevaba esa «cosa» en la cabeza. Me entusiasmó escuchar sin que me notara, y me alegré al oír su respuesta. «¿Ha leído alguna vez 1 Corintios 11? Allí se nos enseña que las mujeres deben cubrirse la cabeza. Es una señal de sumisión». La mujer se quedó sorprendida por su respuesta. Dijo que nunca había oído eso antes y que su padre era pastor. Siguieron conversando de manera muy interesante, y al final la mujer quiso volver a casa y estudiar su Biblia.

Un tratado puede hacer mucho bien; también un sermón poderoso o un artículo impreso, pero ¡lo que este mundo busca es a alguien que ponga toda su confianza en Dios! Quieren «ver algo que funcione», ¿y por qué no? Nuestro Dios quiere usarnos para mostrar su poder. Sin duda, cada uno de nosotros quiere que Dios lo use. Y puede hacerlo. Puede usar a cada uno de nosotros. La respuesta es confía en el SEÑOR con todo tu corazón y no te apoyes en tu propia prudencia –Pro 3:5.

Today, I’d like to continue and possibly complete our discussion of Regenerative Medicine. I want to consider where it stands today, and how Christians can navigate the complex maze of treatments. As you may recall, in the previous issue of this magazine we discussed that Regenerative Medicine is man’s attempt to re-create organ systems. We described how fetal tissue was attempted to be used, due to its low rate of rejection by the people receiving it. Medically speaking, it was problematic in that, if used on a large scale, it would require large amounts of aborted fetuses. Later, embryonic stem cells were studied in depth. Here, embryos, which are newly conceived humans in their earliest stages, are dissected (cut apart) and stem cells are taken.

Think of stem cells as indolent, immature adults, who live in their parents’ basements, without direction, not knowing what they want to do with their lives. With a little encouragement and direction, they can finally find their way, finding a specialized skill and important role in life. In like manner, scientists have discovered ways to “program” these stem cells, “encouraging” them to become specialized into types of cells, such as nerve, heart, blood, and insulin producing. These cells would then be grown in a lab, then used to repair or replace the diseased or injured tissue.

However, “taking” stem cells from embryos results in his or her (the embryo’s) destruction. This is obviously problematic for Christians, knowing that one of the seven things that the Lord says is an abomination is …hands that shed innocent blood –Pro 6:17. Additionally, the sixth commandment directs, Thou shalt not kill –Exo 20:13. Because these objections were recognized by the scientific community, there was pressure to find an alternative.

The Apostle Paul states, There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it –1Co 10:13. His words are as true today as they were 2000 years ago. While Christians suffer from disease just as commonly as non-Christians do, modern medicine can present the “temptation” of a treatment and relief from disease or injury that is actually immoral. But God is faithful, and his escape is twofold. First and foremost, He gave His son to bear our burdens. It is to this Great Physician that we should always turn to first.

In the case of stem cell treatments, it so happens that it was discovered that these immature stem cells are not only found in human embryos, but they are also found in all people, from infants to grown-ups as well. This may be the physical “escape” for His faithful children. These immature stem cells (usually obtained from a patient’s fat tissue or bone marrow) can be grown, cultured, and used just as well as embryonic stem cells. It turns out that “Adult Stem Cells” have actually been more clinically effective, since they are “custom designed” for each individual, and since they come from that person’s own body; therefore, there is very little problem with rejection.

Umbilical cord stem cells have also been shown to be useful, particularly in bone and cartilage treatments. Just as there have been obstacles to overcome when using embryonic stem cells, so too there are problems with developing treatments using adult or umbilical cord stem cells. Think again of a stem cell as an immature, indolent adult. Just having him “hang out” with a master carpenter will not make him a master carpenter if all he does is find entertainment on his cell phone. Stem cells, like an apprentice, need intense, focused training and direction to become specialists in their chosen field of expertise. Learning how to turn these “switches” on is perhaps one of the greatest challenges. The main idea here is that just injecting stem cells that have not been “programmed” or “trained” into damaged or diseased tissue will not automatically make them “know” what to become or how to function.

Similarly, just putting a young electronics apprentice on a bus that is traveling into a city that just had a power grid failure will not result in restoring the power. Here the parallel is placing stem cells into the brain of a stroke victim or a paraplegic accident victim, hoping that the stem cells will “know” what to do, and which specific connections to repair in order to restore function. This may not work as hoped. It would be fruitless to expect success unless and until these problems are also addressed.

Then there is the lingering problem of these eager youngsters (stem cells) knowing when to stop. The problem with fetal tissue turning into cancerous tumors is also a problem to be dealt with in stem cells. Considering this, there is one exception: umbilical cord stem cells are generally not known to turn malignant.1

Here is a short list of treatments that are in development that would use stem cells:

  • Macular Degeneration—Repair a damaged retina.
  • Spinal Cord Injury/Stroke—Repair nerve tissue.
  • Burns—Repair skin tissue.
  • Congestive Heart Failure—Repair damaged heart tissue.
  • Diabetes—Replace or increase the pancreatic tissue that makes insulin.
  • Arthritis—Repair damaged cartilage.
  • Autoimmune diseases (Lupus, Multiple Sclerosis) —Destroy the immune system that is attacking its own body and replace or “reset” it with a new immune system derived from one’s own stem cells.
  • Leukemias—Destroy the cancerous blood cells and replace them with new stem cell derived blood cells.
  • New organs—Replace diseased, damaged, or cancer-ridden organs, such as the kidney, liver, or pancreas, with organs derived from the patient’s own stem cells, grown in a lab, and transplanted surgically, without the need of anti-rejection drugs.

As you can see, there is a very long list of diseases and ailments that may result in effective treatments with stem cells. I am very optimistic that within a decade, remedies for many of these ailments will be commonly available. However, learning how to make stem cells that are expertly specialized into specific tissue types, learning how to turn stems cells on and then turning them off at the necessary time (once the job is finished), and learning how to “teach” the stem cells where and how to make repairs will take time.

I am not the only one who is excited about the possibilities. That is why hundreds of stem cell clinics have sprung up across the country, trying to get in on the excitement. But do the claims of any of these clinics align with reality? Which ones are legitimate? I know that there are many clinics offering stem cell treatments for various ailments, so let’s now look at some of the treatments that are available today—ones that have evidence of actually helping, as well as realistic expectations. Let’s also look at some of the possible complications, to help us make informed decisions.

First, the risks and complications

  • Introduction of infection—For example, bacteria living on the skin can enter a joint space from a simple injection, resulting in destruction of the joint, even under the cleanest of conditions.
  • Stems cells moving from their introduction site and not going where they are intended or not staying contained to the specific area of treatment—One study involving pigs treated with stem cells injected into areas of a damaged heart after a heart attack showed near complete return of function, but then the new heart tissue kept growing, eventually filling the heart’s pumping chamber, which caused all the pigs to die.
  • Stem cells changing into unexpected or inappropriate cell types—Stem cells used for a facial cosmetic effect have actually turned to bone.2
  • Growth of tumors—There are documented cases of different tumors, including brain and kidney tumors that have developed after patients were treated for stroke and kidney failure using stem cells.
  • Failure to work as expected—There are documented cases of people with macular degeneration, who were treated with stem cells injected into the eye, that have resulted in blindness.
  • Stem cells can’t be withdrawn—Unlike medicines such as a pill or an injection, if something goes wrong, one can’t just withhold the next dose. Once stem cells are introduced, they can’t be taken back. The course that has been set will continue.

The rates of complications are hard to know, since there are no reporting requirements when performed outside of formal clinical investigations.

Next, the known benefits

The FDA (the governmental Food and Drug Administration that is tasked with health safety) has approved stem cell treatments for dozens of blood cancers (leukemias) and blood diseases using umbilical cord stem cells. Though not FDA approved, studies have shown some benefit for using stem cells for orthopedic applications, particularly arthritis of the knees. (Using stem cells for such orthopedic uses, without the need to stimulate them to become cartilage cells beforehand, appears to be the exception to the rule. Remember most stem cells need to be specialized before being used.) That’s it! Aside from this, most other uses for stem cells should only be considered either highly experimental or highly suspect of exaggerated benefits. Could there be other beneficial treatments that are not FDA approved? Perhaps, but it’s important to realize that the claims have often far outpaced the science.

So how is one to know? Here are some things to consider when choosing providers of stem cell treatments, as well as red flags, to tell you if there are better places to go for your health care. (These points are also true for just about any other treatment):

  1. Informed consent—Every medical treatment has risks and benefits. These should be routinely discussed with you beforehand, without you needing to ask. Any practitioner who claims there are no risks, only benefits, either is not sufficiently knowledgeable or is not sufficiently honest!
  2. Can they handle the complications? —Joint injections can sometimes result in infection. These can be severe infections that can potentially destroy the joint. Such complications are not just simply treated with antibiotics, but with surgery. These stem cell treatments are better handled by an orthopedic surgeon or practitioner that has a close relationship with one, if complications should arise. Likewise, treatments involving nerves should be done by neurologists or neurosurgeons.
  3. Is the clinic adequately equipped? —Stem cells need to be handled appropriately. The transport of umbilical stem cells and improper thawing from the supplier can drastically reduce numbers, which may have a great deal to do with determining the success of the procedure. Additionally, these cells may be in a state of “shock,” unless they are appropriately re-cultured after being thawed. This allows them to re-enter a desirable growth phase again.3 This may mean having a specialized lab and microbiologist on staff to properly grow and care for the stem cells, ensuring good quality control. This usually requires a university setting, not just a small clinic or office that has a nurse to thaw the stem cells after receiving them from an overnight delivery service. Glitzy web sites, colorful brochures, and informational dinners are not enough.
  4. Guinea pigs and rats are “experimented on,” people go through “clinical trials.” —Please avoid any practitioner who says they are doing experiments. Clinical trials involving people, which have the oversight of ethics boards, only occur after experiments on animals have shown low risk of harm, and a good chance of success. If a treatment is very effective, the FDA has suggested that as few as 42 participants can demonstrate adequate safety to grant approval. This is not an outrageously high threshold to overcome. Additionally, patients involved in clinical trials are usually only expected to cover minimal costs, if any. Practitioners who “experiment” on people rarely do it for free.4
  5. Realistic claims. —Does your practitioner claim 100 percent success? If so, it is better to run away (if your knees will allow you to) than to simply walk away! Knee treatments, for example, may only delay knee replacements for many people. Some may avoid surgery, but certainly not all. Do not expect a cure. Also, do they make claims well outside of what is commonly recognized? “Cures” claimed for Alzheimers, Parkinson’s, or other ailments that are not FDA approved? I cannot totally exclude the possibility that such treatments may exist at some future time. However, these practitioners should be able to point to (and provide to you) published studies. If there is a miraculous cure, the world should be able to benefit from it, and he or she should be able to patent it, so as to reap the financial benefits of sharing their techniques and discoveries with the rest of the world. By doing so, it is independently tested and verified. Anyone who has a “secret” cure, that they alone possess, should be avoided.
  1. Does it make sense? —By simply injecting stem cells (that have not been induced by a lab into their specialty state such as nerve cells, heart cells, etc.) into the bloodstream to treat things like nerve disorders, for example, does not make sense. Clinical trials of legitimate treatments first specialize the stem cells, then directly apply them to the affected area. For example, specific types of nerve cells are injected directly into specific locations of the brain, and heart cells are injected directly into the scarred tissue of the heart. Remember the indolent adult (the unspecialized stem cell)? You can’t expect to put them on a bus (inject them into a vein), send them into the big city (the body), without instructions on what to do (leaving them unspecialized), not knowing where to go (to somehow find the diseased part of the body) and then magically expect success.
  2. The hard sell. —Are you being told that or are you made to feel that you are “missing out” if you decline? Do the clinic advertisements have testimonial bylines, something to the effect of “Individual results may vary, and testimonials are not claimed to represent typical results and are not intended to represent or guarantee that anyone will achieve the same or similar results…”? As the old adage goes, if it’s too good to be true (especially if they actually tell you so), then it probably is. In these cases, consider the claims to be most likely somewhat exaggerated, and also consider working with someone who can give a more honest set of expectations.

I pray that God may grant you wisdom: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –Jas 1:5.
