دیکھو، خداوند کا جلال بادل میں ظاہر ہوا –خروج 16:10۔

ہمارے اوپر آسمان میں تیرتی ہوئی بخارات کی یہ مرتکز ڈھیری کیسی عجیب چیز ہے۔ ایک لمحے میں بادل ایسی بے پناہ برکت اور امید کا وسیلہ بن سکتا ہے، اور دوسرے لمحے میں چبھتی ہوئی بے یقینی اور یہاں تک کہ شدید خوف پیدا کرنے کا سبب۔ بلاشبہ بادل اکثر گلیل کے تھکے ماندے مچھیروں کے سروں پر خوش آئند سایہ اور محنت کش کسان کے لیے امید کا پیغام ہوتے تھے۔ کتنی ہی بار یہ بادل دوپہر کے وقت چھٹ جاتے ہیں تاکہ سورج کی چمکتی کرنیں زمین تک پہنچ سکیں۔ پھر شام کو وہ چاندی کی لکیر جیسی نفیس خوب صورتی کے لیے ایک غیر شفاف پس منظر مہیا کرتے ہیں۔

ہم 700,000 پاؤنڈ سے زیادہ وزن والے ہوائی جہاز کو پروں کے سہارے بلند ہو کر آسمان میں پرواز کرتے دیکھ کر حیران ہو سکتے ہیں، لیکن ایک بادل انسانی مداخلت کی کسی تدبیر کے بغیر لاکھوں ٹن پانی اٹھائے رہ سکتا ہے۔ بادل تب بنتے ہیں جب نم اور گرم ہوا بلندی پر ٹھنڈے مقام کی طرف اٹھتی ہے اور پانی خردبینی «بیجوں» مثلاً گرد، راکھ یا بیکٹیریا پر جمع ہو کر مائع بن جاتا ہے۔ اگر پانی کے بخارات کی مقدار ان جگہوں سے زیادہ ہو جہاں وہ جمع ہو سکتے ہیں، تو برف کے قلمے بھی بیج کا کام دے کر نمی جذب کر لیتے ہیں—وہ پانیوں کو اپنے گھنے بادلوں میں باندھ رکھتا ہے، اور بادل ان کے بوجھ سے پھٹتا نہیں –ایوب 26:8۔ آخرکار یہ بیج اتنے بھاری ہو جاتے ہیں کہ اوپر اٹھتی ہوا انہیں سنبھال نہیں پاتی، اور پھر، دیکھو، چھتری کا وقت آ پہنچتا ہے۔

ایلیاہ کے زمانے کی خشک زمین کے لیے سب سے چھوٹا بادل (1 سلاطین 18:44 میں آدمی کے ہاتھ کے برابر) قادرِ مطلق کی طرف سے جواب تھا کہ وہ اپنی قوم کو پھر سے بارش کی برکت دینے کے لیے تیار ہے۔ لیکن ایوب اور یرمیاہ جیسے دوسرے لوگوں کے لیے بادل شک، مایوسی اور دل شکستگی کی آخری علامت تھا۔ دہشتیں مجھ پر آ پڑی ہیں؛ وہ ہوا کی مانند میری جان کے پیچھے لگی ہیں؛ اور میری خوش حالی بادل کی طرح جاتی رہی –ایوب 30:15، اور تو نے اپنے آپ کو بادل سے ڈھانپ لیا ہے تاکہ ہماری دعا تجھ تک نہ پہنچے –نوحہ 3:44۔ اکثر ایسے ہی کٹھن حالات میں خدا خود کو بادل میں چھپانے کا انتخاب کرتا ہے۔ ان اوقات میں ہم گھنے اور خوف ناک دھندلکے میں روشنی کی راہ ڈھونڈتے ہوئے ٹٹولتے ہیں، لیکن وہ ہمیں نہیں ملتی۔ دل شکستگی میں ہم بادلوں سے خالی دن کی کرن کے آرزو مند ہو سکتے ہیں، لیکن وہ ہماری دسترس سے باہر رہتی ہے۔ ہم جانتے ہیں کہ خدا دھند کے بیچ میں ہے، لیکن ہم نہ اسے پا سکتے ہیں، نہ اس کی برکت دیکھ سکتے ہیں۔ وہ بادلوں سے روشنی کو ڈھانپتا ہے، اور بیچ میں آنے والے بادل کے باعث اسے چمکنے کا حکم نہیں دیتا –ایوب 36:32۔

ہمارا خدا، جو اپنی مخلوق یعنی ہم سے رفاقت رکھنا پسند کرتا ہے، خود کو بادل میں کیوں چھپائے گا؟ وہ اکثر ہمارے جستجو اور درد سے بھرے دلوں سے اپنی مرضی کیوں چھپاتا ہے؟ ہماری محدود عقلیں اکثر سوچتی ہیں کہ بظاہر اتنے دور خدا سے کون سا جلال برآمد ہو سکتا ہے، اور …یہ بربادی کس لیے؟ –متی 26:8۔ اگرچہ ہم کبھی یہ توقع نہیں کریں گے کہ خدا کا الٰہی منصوبہ ہمیں ہمیشہ دھندلے حواس میں چھوڑ دینا ہے، لیکن کچھ وقت کے لیے یہ اس کی مرضی ہو سکتی ہے۔ موت کے سایہ کی وادی میں سیر کی مانند، جس کی راہ میں کچھ عرصے کے لیے وضاحت نہ رہی ہو، اس کی روح میں ابدی کردار پیدا ہو سکتا ہے۔ ہم خوب جانتے ہیں کہ صادقوں کی راہ صبح کی روشنی کی مانند ہے، جو دوپہر تک بڑھتی اور زیادہ روشن ہوتی جاتی ہے –امثال 4:18۔ پھر بھی ہم میں سے بیشتر نے کبھی نہ کبھی وہ ناامید دھند محسوس کی ہے جو ہمارے حال اور مستقبل کو گھیر لیتی ہے۔ ایسے وقتوں میں ہم دن دہاڑے اندھیرے سے دوچار ہوتے اور دوپہر کے وقت رات کی طرح ٹٹولتے ہیں –ایوب 5:14۔ اپنی شکستہ دل مایوسی میں ہم خدا کی نیکی کو آسانی سے نظروں سے اوجھل کر سکتے ہیں۔ اس کے نتیجے میں شکرگزاری کا فقدان ہمیں بہت سی دوسری آزمائشوں کی یقینی راہ پر ڈال دیتا ہے، جبکہ مایوسی کا دیو ہمارے سروں پر بلند ہو کر گناہ کے خلاف ہماری مزاحمت کمزور کرنے کی کوشش کرتا ہے۔

ہم جانتے ہیں کہ ایلیاہ ہماری ہی طرح انسانی کمزوریوں کا آدمی تھا –یعقوب 5:17۔ پھر بھی ہم میں سے بہت کم لوگوں نے کبھی ایسی سرشاری بھری فتح کا تجربہ کیا ہے جیسی اسے کوہِ کرمل پر بعل کے نبیوں پر غالب آنے سے حاصل ہوئی۔ لیکن ہم میں سے بہت سے لوگ اس دل شکستگی سے بخوبی واقف ہیں جو اس کے بعد آئی، جب وہ حورب پہنچا اور وہاں ایک غار میں ٹھہرا۔ یہ وہی مقام ہے جو کوہِ سینا ہے، جہاں صحیفوں میں پہاڑ کا پہلا عظیم منظر ہمارے سامنے کھلا۔ اس وقت موسیٰ نے بادل میں خدا سے ملاقات کی تھی۔ شریعت دی گئی اور خدا کا جلال اس شان سے ظاہر ہوا کہ وہ منظر ایسا ہولناک تھا کہ موسیٰ نے کہا، میں بہت ڈرتا اور کانپتا ہوں –عبرانیوں 12:21۔ یہ چھوا جا سکنے والا پہاڑ ایک ہیبت ناک اور خوف انگیز پہاڑ تھا، جس کے اطراف میں ٹوٹے پھوٹے گہرے گرینائٹ کی چوٹیاں اور ناقابلِ بیان عظمت کی سخت کمر بند پہاڑیاں تھیں۔ حورب کا جری اور خوف ناک رخ، تیوری چڑھائے شان و شوکت کے ساتھ، سیدھی بلندی میں بارہ سو سے پندرہ سو فٹ تک اٹھتا ہے۔

ایلیاہ کی نظر دھندلا گئی تھی اور اس کی روح اب تک کی پست ترین حالت میں ڈوب رہی تھی، تو خدا نے حیرت انگیز طریقے سے اسے جواب دیا—…اور دیکھو، خداوند وہاں سے گزرا، اور ایک بڑی اور تیز آندھی نے پہاڑوں کو چیر ڈالا اور خداوند کے آگے چٹانوں کو توڑ پھوڑ دیا؛ لیکن خداوند آندھی میں نہ تھا؛ اور آندھی کے بعد زلزلہ آیا، لیکن خداوند زلزلے میں نہ تھا؛ اور زلزلے کے بعد آگ آئی، لیکن خداوند آگ میں نہ تھا؛ اور آگ کے بعد ایک دھیمی، مدھم آواز آئی۔ اور ایسا ہوا کہ جب ایلیاہ نے یہ سنا تو اپنا چہرہ چادر سے ڈھانپ لیا اور باہر نکل آیا… –1 سلاطین 19:11-13۔

کسی طرح ہم یہ ماننے لگے ہیں کہ زمین ہلا دینے والا تجربہ خدا کی ظاہر موجودگی کا اعلیٰ ترین مظہر ہے۔ ہمارا خیال ہے کہ خدا ایلیاہ کے قریب کوہِ کرمل پر کوہِ حورب کی نسبت زیادہ تھا۔ کوہِ کرمل پر بولتے ہوئے ایلیاہ کا وہ «دھوپ میں چمکنے کا دن» تھا۔ اس نے لوگوں کو ملامت کی اور نبیوں کا مذاق اڑایا۔ اس نے خداوند کے نام میں دلیری سے وعظ کیا اور لوگوں کو اپنی دوغلی وفاداری سے توبہ کرنے کا حکم دیا۔ لیکن اب اس کی آواز خاموش ہو چکی ہے اور وہ سن رہا ہے… سن رہا ہے اس دھیمی مدھم آواز کو جو اس کے اپنے اعمال اور ارادوں کا حساب مانگ رہی ہے۔ پس اگر ہم بس رک کر سنیں، تو ہماری افسوس ناک ناکامیوں کی یاد ہمیں اپنے خداوند کے آستانے تک لے جائے گی، بجائے اس کے کہ ہم اپنی سمجھی ہوئی کامیابیوں پر فخر کریں۔

بادل کی یہ بابرکت خدمت ہے۔ خداوند اکثر اسے اس وسیلے کے طور پر استعمال کرتا ہے جو ہمیں اس مقام تک پہنچاتا ہے جہاں ہم اپنے دلوں میں اس کا ظاہر جلال سچ مچ قبول کر سکتے ہیں۔ یہ کسی خوشگوار گرمیوں کے دن کے سفید، روئی جیسے کمولس بادل نہیں، بلکہ ہموار اور بے نقش اسٹریٹس بادل ہیں، جو مشرق سے مغرب تک آسمان کو ڈھانپ کر آسمانی دھوپ کی تمام کرنیں پوری طرح روک لیتے ہیں۔ وہ دوپہر کے عین وقت دن کو اداسی کے ایسے ذخیرے میں لپیٹ سکتے ہیں جو ہمارے دلوں کی گہرائی تک خلش پیدا کرتا ہے۔ وہ چھوٹی چھوٹی باتیں جن کا دوسرے دنوں میں ہمارے رویوں پر کچھ خاص اثر نہیں ہوتا، اب ہمارے سامنے دیو کی طرح بلند دکھائی دیتی ہیں۔ ہمیں ایسے حالات کا سامنا ہو سکتا ہے جن کے بارے میں ہم جانتے ہیں کہ وہ ہمارے اختیار سے باہر ہیں، لیکن ہمارے ذہن آرام کی حالت میں آنے سے انکار کرتے ہیں۔ ایسے وقت میں، اگر ہماری گفتگو کے دوسرے سرے پر کوئی بدقسمت شخص اسی جیسی مصیبت سے گزر رہا ہو، تو ہم خود اس بات کا تجربہ کر سکتے ہیں کہ …انسان مصیبت کے لیے پیدا ہوا ہے، جیسے چنگاریاں اوپر کو اڑتی ہیں –ایوب 5:7۔ دوسرے اوقات میں ہمارا افسردہ مزاج تنہائی اختیار کر کے اپنے ہی الگ تھلگ ترس اور دھندلی اداسی میں پرورش پاتا ہے۔

کچھ لوگ مایوسی میں ذہنی کیفیت کے لیے دوا کا رخ کرتے ہیں اور اس میں وقتی سکون کا ایک محدود راستہ پاتے ہیں۔ لیکن خدا ہمیں بادل میں اس لیے نہیں لایا کہ ہم معالجوں اور ماہرینِ نفسیات کی مدد تلاش کریں۔ بادل کی خدمت یہ ہے کہ وہ دوسرے تمام متبادل راستے بند کر دے تاکہ ہم اس سے اس کی تسلی کی پوری برکت حاصل کر سکیں۔ خدا چاہتا ہے کہ ہم آج کی چمکتی دھوپ قربان کریں تاکہ کل اس کی حضوری کی معموری پائیں۔

حالانکہ تم نہیں جانتے کہ کل کیا ہو گا۔ تمہاری زندگی ہے ہی کیا؟ وہ تو بخار کی مانند ہے، جو تھوڑی دیر دکھائی دیتا ہے، پھر غائب ہو جاتا ہے –یعقوب 4:14۔ گزرے ہوئے برسوں میں، میں نے اس آیت پر وعظ کیا، لوگوں کو زندگی کی مختصری کے بارے میں نصیحت کی اور انہیں ترغیب دی کہ اپنے برس ضائع نہ کریں۔ لیکن میں نے اس کی بنیاد کو بالکل نظرانداز کیا تھا—تم نہیں جانتے کہ کل کیا ہو گا۔ شاید دل سے جوان لوگوں کو یہ بات معمولی لگے، لیکن میری عمر کا پھل جوں جوں پکتا جا رہا ہے، عام اور ظاہر محاوروں کی قدر میرے دل میں بڑھتی جا رہی ہے۔ ہماری جدید سائنسی دنیا زندگی کی محبت کے پیچھے اس قدر شدت سے لگی ہوئی ہے کہ وہ محبت کی اس زندگی کی قدر نہیں کر سکتی جو دکھ سہنے سے جنم لیتی ہے۔ اگرچہ گزشتہ زمانوں میں جن لوگوں نے جسم میں دکھ سہے اور گناہ سے باز آئے (1 پطرس 4:1)، مجھے کوئی وجہ نظر نہیں آتی کہ ابر آلود ذہن کی نازک تکالیف سہنے والے بھی وہی جلال کیوں نہیں پا سکتے، بشرطیکہ وہ صبر کریں اور نتائج خدا پر چھوڑ دیں۔

ہم مغرور لوگ ہیں جو کل کی پیش گوئیوں پر بھروسا کرتے ہیں۔ ہمیں گمان ہے کہ ہم اپنی ریٹائرمنٹ کی منصوبہ بندی اور زندگی کے واقعات کا نہایت باریک بینی سے وقت مقرر کر سکتے ہیں۔ موسم کا حال بتانے والے ہمیں کل کے درجۂ حرارت کے بارے میں بتاتے ہیں تاکہ ہم اپنے دن کی منصوبہ بندی احتیاط سے کر سکیں۔ ہمارا بیمہ یقین دلاتا ہے کہ ہمیں مستقبل میں غربت کا سامنا نہیں ہو گا۔ ہمارے فریزر اور بینک کھاتے کل سے بھی آگے کے لیے کافی بھرے ہوئے ہیں، اور ہم یہ ماننے کے عادی ہو گئے ہیں کہ ہم …ملکہ کی طرح بیٹھی ہوں، بیوہ نہیں، اور غم نہ دیکھوں گی –مکاشفہ 18:7۔ لیکن دل کا غم زمینی آسائشوں سے اتنی آسانی سے دور نہیں کیا جا سکتا۔ ہماری زندگی بخار (بادل) ہے، کیونکہ ہم …نہیں جانتے کہ کل کیا ہو گا… –یعقوب 4:14۔ اپنی تمام ٹیکنالوجی کے باوجود ہم اس حقیقت کو نہیں مٹا سکتے۔ یہیں ہمیں اپنی زندگی کے بارے میں اپنے تمام اندازوں، توقعات اور ارادوں کو ایک طرف رکھ کر بادل میں اپنے خدا کو پانا ہے۔

وہ اپنے تخت کے چہرے کو چھپا لیتا ہے اور اس پر اپنا بادل پھیلا دیتا ہے –ایوب 26:9۔ خدا کے تخت کے چہرے کو بادل سے ڈھانپنے کا فائدہ کیا ہے؟ اگر اسے دیکھنا آسان ہوتا تو ہم میں سے زیادہ تر لوگ اس سے دور رہ کر ہی مطمئن ہوتے۔ تاہم، سامنے پھیلی دھند کے باعث ہمیں اس کی معموری کا تجربہ کرنے کے لیے قریب آنا پڑتا ہے۔ ہمیں کتنا شکر گزار ہونا چاہیے کہ معاملہ یوں ہی ہے، کیونکہ اگر ایسا نہ ہوتا تو ہمارا روحانی نقصان کتنا تباہ کن ہوتا۔

اگر ہماری خود کفیل زندگی ہمیشہ بھرپور اور شاداب رہتی اور خدا کو آسانی سے پا لیا جاتا، تو ہم… کھو دیتے۔

…ایمان

ہم اس ضمانت کے طالب ہیں کہ ہماری آزمائشوں کا اختتام ہمیشہ خوشی پر ہو گا اور ہماری دعائیں فطری طور پر غیر ضروری ہو جائیں گی۔ ایمان میں ہم خدا کی کفالت پر یقین رکھتے ہیں، لیکن یہ حقیقت کہ ہم نہیں جانتے کہ ایک دن کیا لے آئے گا، ہم سے تقاضا کرتی ہے کہ اپنے کمزور گھٹنوں کے بل گر کر دعا کریں۔ بہت سی باتیں ہمیں خدا پر بھروسا کرنے میں مشکل ڈال سکتی ہیں، لیکن پردے میں چھپا کل اسے آسان بنا دیتا ہے۔ محققین نے موسم کو قابو میں کرنے کی کوششوں پر لاکھوں خرچ کیے ہیں۔ بارش والے بادل پیدا کرنے کی خاطر انہوں نے ہوا میں ہر طرح کے قابلِ تصور بادل کے بیج بوئے ہیں۔ اسرائیل کے شمالی علاقے میں بادلوں میں بیج بونے کی چالیس برس کی کوششوں کا جائزہ لینے کے بعد تل ابیب یونیورسٹی کے محققین اس نتیجے پر پہنچے ہیں کہ بادلوں میں بیج بونے سے حقیقتاً اضافی بارش نہیں ہوتی۔ ہمیں کتنا شکر گزار ہونا چاہیے۔ جتنا زیادہ ہم نامعلوم کل کو قابو کر سکتے ہیں، کائنات کے مالک پر ہمیں اتنا ہی کم ایمان درکار ہوتا ہے۔

یعقوب نے ایک ناراض بھائی، مایوس باپ اور ماں سے ٹوٹا ہوا رشتہ پیچھے چھوڑتے ہوئے بالکل نامعلوم مستقبل کا سامنا کیا۔ یہ تخت تک جانے والی سیڑھی کا ایک حصہ ہے اور ہمارے قادرِ مطلق خدا سے عہد کو مضبوط کرتا ہے۔ اب ہم جزوی طور پر جانتے ہیں اور جزوی طور پر دیکھتے ہیں۔ شاید یہ چھوٹا سا ٹکڑا ہمیں اس سے زیادہ باطنی دولت دیتا ہے جتنا سب کچھ پوری طرح سمجھ لینے سے ملتی۔ اگر ہمارا مستقبل پوری طرح ہمارے قابو میں ہوتا، تو ہم ایک کامل فردوس وضع کرتے، جس میں بچوں کی کامل تعداد کامل گھر میں آسودگی سے رہتی، کامل ملازمت کی کفالت میں، کامل طور طریقوں سے گھری ہوئی—ایسی کامل پاکیزگی جو بے جان اور مردہ ہو۔

…امید

میں سوچتا ہوں کہ کیا ہمیں احساس ہے کہ ہماری شکرگزاری غیر متوقع چیزوں کی کتنی مرہونِ منت ہے۔ عبرانیوں کا مصنف ہماری امید کو …جان کا لنگر، جو مضبوط اور ثابت قدم ہے… –عبرانیوں 6:19۔ قرار دیتا ہے۔ بچے خوش ہوتے ہیں کیونکہ ان کے بڑے بڑے خواب ہوتے ہیں۔ اکثر کسی تقریب کی توقع اور منصوبہ بندی تقریباً اتنی ہی سنسنی خیز ہوتی ہے جتنا خود اس میں جانا۔ ہر دن بے داغ اور امید سے بھرے ذہن کے لیے ایک روشن، نئی کھڑکی ہے۔ جب تجربات کو گزشتہ مایوسیوں کی عینک سے دیکھا جائے تو وہ اکثر ہمیں بدگمانی اور تلخی کی دہلیز تک پہنچا دیتے ہیں۔ یعقوب نے اپنے بیٹے یوسف سے حیرت انگیز طور پر دوبارہ ملنے کے بعد بھی کہا، میرے دن تھوڑے اور بُرے رہے ہیں۔ اگرچہ فطری طور پر ایسا ہوتا ہے، مگر ایسا ہونا ضروری نہیں۔ پولس کہتا ہے، …مصیبت سے صبر پیدا ہوتا ہے؛ اور صبر سے پختگی، اور پختگی سے امید –رومیوں 5:3-4۔ یقیناً، اگر ہمیں معلوم ہوتا کہ کل کیا ہونے والا ہے (اچھا بھی اور برا بھی)، تو امید کا جانفزا عنصر کم ہو جاتا۔ حوا نے یہ خیال ظاہر کیا کہ اگر وہ مزید علم حاصل کر لے تو زندگی بہتر ہو گی۔ لیکن وضاحت کی اس ہوس بھری جستجو میں اس نے کتنی بابرکت امید کھو دی۔

محبت میں ایک آرزو بھری نرمی ہے جو صرف بے یقینی ہی دے سکتی ہے۔ ایک نوجوان اور دوشیزہ کے تعلق میں ایک ایسی بے یقینی بھری حیرت ہے جو ان کی راہ کو گھیرے رہتی ہے۔ کل کے نامعلوم خطرات ماں کو اپنے بچوں سے محبت کرنے اور ان کے لیے دعا کرنے پر آمادہ کرتے ہیں۔ اپنے خاندان کے لیے روشن تر کل کا تصور باپ کو اپنے روزمرہ کام میں محنت کرنے کی تحریک دیتا ہے۔ جہاں کہیں شوہر اور بیوی پاکیزہ ازدواجی بندھن کی بائبلی یگانگت میں جڑے ہوں، وہاں کل کو گھیرنے والا بھید ایک عظیم نغمے کے معمولی سُر کی مانند ہے۔ یہ خوشی میں ایک متوقع غم کی بات کرتا ہے اور غم کو چاروں طرف سے گھیرتی خوشی سے روشن کرتا ہے۔ اگر یعقوب کو معلوم ہوتا کہ کل کیا لائے گا تو کیا اس کے سات برس کا انتظار چند دنوں جیسا لگتا؟ اگر ہمیں سب کچھ معلوم ہوتا، تو محبت بہت مشکل ہو جاتی۔ اگر ہمیں سب کچھ معلوم ہوتا، تو محبت بہت آسان ہو جاتی۔ اگر ہمیں سب کچھ معلوم ہوتا، تو ہمارا دل ٹوٹ جاتا۔ اگر ہمیں سب کچھ معلوم ہوتا، تو ہمیں کوئی پروا نہ ہوتی۔ دوسرے لفظوں میں، بدترین بات سے ناواقف رہنا ہمیں مضبوط بناتا ہے اور بہترین بات سے ناواقف رہنا ہمیں زیادہ نرم دل بناتا ہے۔ کیونکہ ہماری دھندلی اور تاریک نگاہ میں …ایمان، امید اور محبت، یہ تینوں باقی ہیں؛ مگر ان میں سب سے بڑی محبت ہے –1 کرنتھیوں 13:13۔

The score is a judgment, not a measured percentage of accuracy. The ordinary threshold is 95/100; use the supplied task-specific quality_threshold when present. Accepted-publication upgrades require at least 98/100 and must preserve or improve fidelity against the supplied accepted_baseline.

Major or critical findings require concrete substantive errors: changed meaning or doctrine, changed negation or attribution, omitted substantive prose, invented facts or explanations, incorrect Scripture identity or numbers, or untranslated substantive passages. Do not classify a synonym, grammatical alternative, punctuation preference, or correct idiomatic rendering as a major error. An unchanged proper name, established title of a cited work, or identifier is not by itself an untranslated substantive passage; judge its role in context. Scripture quotations and other quoted substantive prose are translated as article text in this workflow, faithfully conveying the authoritative English as printed. Book names should use conventional target-language forms while preserving the exact chapter/verse numbers, ranges and the number and placement of references. If we step back and look at our own life, can we honestly say that we trust in the Lord with all our heart? I often think of my children—they trust in me with all their hearts; there is no fear within them; they do not worry. My prayer is that I can trust in my Heavenly Father in the same way.

Here in Haiti a lot of people are driven by fear. They fear the uncertainty of tomorrow. They fear whether they will find food, work, and clothing. It is the opposite of trusting in God. In the western culture, people don’t fear those things. Food and clothing are easy to find, jobs are plentiful, and medical assistance is just one 911 call away.

The poor people here in Haiti say that it would be easier to trust God if they were in America, but is that truly the case? While very few in America fear whether they will have enough to eat, many fear whether they will be accepted by other people. There are some who may fear having enough money to live, but there are many who fear death. Whatever our fear is, trusting in God is our answer.

Let’s look at the life of David. David was a young boy. When his older brothers went to battle, young David went out to feed his father’s sheep. On the battlefield, there was a giant with the Philistine army named Goliath. He challenged the Israelites by saying that if one man would come out and fight him, the victor’s army would rule the other side. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 we read that Goliath said, …I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

Later on, we read that Jesse, David’s father, sent him to the place of battle to take some food to his older brothers. David arrived at the place of battle, and he heard Goliath speaking these same words. When David saw that the men of Israel were all afraid, he did not understand. Why were God’s people afraid of this uncircumcised Philistine?

Even though David was young, he was no amateur when it came to putting his trust in God. While he was watching his father’s sheep, most likely he talked much with God, asking Him to help guard the sheep. One day a bear came out to attack the sheep, and David killed the bear. Another day a lion came out to eat some sheep. Again, the God-trusting, fearless youth faced the threat and killed the lion. Now, facing a seemingly greater threat, David simply asks, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1Sa 17:26. David went to King Saul and said, I …will go and fight with this Philistine –1Sa 17:32. Once more putting his trust in his God, David took five smooth stones, ran out to meet the giant, and killed him. Upon seeing this sudden turn of events, the people marveled.

According to Psalm 20:7, when we put our trust in horses and chariots, then it is not in the Lord our God. In Matthew 21:21, the Bible says that with faith we can move mountains. Here in Haiti I have found myself in tough situations where God is my only option. When I have been forced to put my trust in God, I have discovered that He still works miracles. Just like David with the lion, the bear, and the giant, we too can learn that trusting God with our whole heart is the best way and not just a last resort. When we trust in the Lord first, we show the world something amazing—that this God we serve is alive, and that He is real.

Here in Haiti there was a man living in a shack up in the mountains with his wife and three young children. But there was a problem—he was deathly ill. One day he heard about a missionary who often traveled through the mountains. I received a message from him stating that he was almost dead and that he needed me to come and pray for him. I quickly went up to his home. I was amazed at his condition. His weight was probably not much more than 70 pounds. His wife told me that he had been in bed for over a year. He couldn’t talk, he only whispered with deep agonizing breaths. We spent quite a while discussing his life, his sin, and his future. He told me that if God would heal him, he would serve him and trust him for the rest of his life. I believed his sincerity, yet I was scared. I began to pray, but it was certainly not a powerful prayer full of faith. Rather it was a weak, humble cry.

As I went home and throughout that night, he was all I could think about. The devil began his attack. I had many confusing, troubling thoughts, “Did you do everything you could have done? What if he dies? Why didn’t you take him to the hospital?” I went to God in prayer. “Oh God,” I prayed, “this man wanted prayer. He didn’t ask for a hospital; he didn’t ask for medication. Please God, heal this man. If he dies, what will I do the next time? O Father, if not for him, please, heal him for me. I need you to, Father.”

I prayed like I had never prayed before, and then, God gave me peace. The next morning, I hurried up the mountain to his home, but he wasn’t there. “No, Lord!” I thought. I rushed around and poked my head in another shack. What I saw overwhelmed me. He was sitting there with a big smile on his face. His wife said that he had been working in the garden that morning. Repeatedly she said, “God healed him! God healed him!” I’ll never forget the feeling I had as I travelled back down that mountain. My heart welled up with joy and thankfulness. “My God is alive! He can do anything and everything! He is my God!” I thanked and praised Him like I never had before. “The lion” that I had faced was dead, and my faith was growing. The devil doesn’t want us to trust God, because when we put our trust in God, He does big things, and our faith grows.

When we put our trust in God there is a risk—what if God doesn’t work? We could be embarrassed, or worse—“What if I step out in faith and God does nothing?” Remember, it is not faith if we know the outcome. Faith is walking in obedience and believing God’s Word when we do not know the outcome. If God wouldn’t have helped David, Goliath surely would have killed him. It was Daniel’s faith that kept him praying to God, even though he knew a lion’s den awaited him. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had so much faith in God that they told the king that even if God chose to not deliver them from the fire, that they still would …not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up –Dan 3:18. Then there was Gideon and his three hundred men. The list goes on and on of godly men who put their life on the line, proving that their God was alive.

When we step out in faith, trusting our God, something always happens (sometimes now, sometimes later; sometimes in a way that makes sense, sometimes in a way that seems to make no earthly sense). Yet God does work, and our faith grows. When we truly believe in God, we will trust him. Then, sharing the Gospel message with others is much easier. Just like Joshua did not have a fleet of bulldozers on standby at Jericho, so also we do not need a backup plan when we trust in God.

It is true that the great minds and financial backing of many in America and other modern countries have replaced God. There is a way to do most physical things without God. In fact, most people say that trusting in God is not common sense. If you pray over a sick child, it’s not common sense. If you turn down a high paying job because you don’t believe that it’s God’s will, that’s not common sense. If you sell your possessions and give to the poor, it’s not common sense. These people are right—trusting in God is not common sense. Marching around a wall seven times, believing it will fall down, is not common sense. Going into battle with only 300 men against a great army who were like grasshoppers for multitude is not common sense either. Most things done by God-trusting Christians don’t make sense, but they do show the world that they really do put their trust in God, and that is what will turn the world upside down again, today.

I remember one day very well. I was away from home when I received a phone call from my wife. She told me to come home quickly—it was an emergency! Our two-year-old son had been stung by bees. I rushed home to see the neighborhood in chaos. People where running around everywhere. I found my wife and son at the neighbor’s house, a local pastor. My son lay in the arms of my wife who told me he had been stung several hundred times. The pastor looked at me quite gravely, telling me that if I didn’t get this boy to a hospital right away, he would surely die. I remember thinking one thing—God can heal! I picked up my son and took him across the street to our house, and I prayed. It didn’t take long before he began to recover—by the next day he was back out playing.

Many people here in Haiti take their sick to the witch doctor, and he heals them. It’s just what happens. How much more can our God do! Please don’t misunderstand me. I’m not saying we shouldn’t go to the medical doctor or to the hospital; rather, I’m trying to emphasize that our trust should be in God.

Years ago, I decided to take up a part-time job selling knives. I was to take these knives and travel from home to home. I didn’t have an interest in knives but was just trying to make some extra money. I was a terrible knife salesman. Everywhere I went everyone said no.

One day the boss took me into his office where he told me that he had noticed I wasn’t selling any knives and realized he had forgotten to show me how the knives worked. So, we sat there in his office as he talked about each knife. He had a small pile of kitchen utensils of another brand, which were known for their quality, that he used for a comparison. First, he held up a small piece of leather and asked me to cut it in half with one of the “other” knives. I sawed through the piece of leather with some ease. Then he instructed me to use one of his knives and do the same thing. The new knife sliced through the leather as if it wasn’t even there! I was truly amazed. He then picked up a penny and told me to cut it in half using the “other” scissors. I tried but failed; they simply would not cut it. He then told me to do the same using his scissors. It easily cut through the penny, and again I was amazed at the product. He told me that I now knew that these knives were the best and from now on I should be able to sell them. He was right. I began selling knives everywhere I went! I even remember walking into a poorly kept trailer home without much hope that they would buy. Surprisingly, they bought over $3,000 worth of knives.

The reason I began to make sales is obvious—I believed in my product. Likewise, if we put our trust in God, we will have confidence. In a day when most proclaiming Christians are ashamed of God and ashamed to stand up for truth, we can be a bright and shining light. We can be a people who go out into the world and into our communities with a Gospel that we truly believe in! As we do, the world will see it and respond. Many are seeking; they are looking for answers. When someone asks us a question about why we do the things we do or wear what we wear, what is our reply? Do we reply with confidence? Do we have a ready Bible verse? Or do we get embarrassed and desire a hole to climb into? If the world could see that we are confident in our God, and that we obey him with enthusiasm, it would be a powerful testimony.

I remember traveling through the airport with a small group. As we were standing in line, I overheard a lady ask one of the single sisters in our group why she wore that “thing” on her head. I was excited to listen unnoticed, and I rejoiced as I heard her response. “Have you ever read 1 Corinthians 11? There it instructs us that women should cover their heads. It’s a sign of submission.” The woman was shocked at her answer, saying she never heard that before, and that her father was a pastor. They continued to have a very interesting conversation that ended with that lady desiring to go home and study her Bible.

A tract can do a lot of good; so likewise, a powerful sermon or a printed article, but someone putting all his trust in God is what this world is looking for! They want to “see something that works,” and why not? Our God wants to use us to show Himself strong. Surely each one of us wants to be used by God. We can. Each one of us can. The answer is to trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding –Pro 3:5.

As ons ’n tree terugstaan en na ons eie lewe kyk, kan ons eerlik sê dat ons met ons hele hart op die Here vertrou? Ek dink dikwels aan my kinders—hulle vertrou my met hulle hele hart; daar is geen vrees in hulle nie; hulle bekommer hulle nie. My gebed is dat ek my Hemelse Vader op dieselfde manier kan vertrou.

Hier in Haïti word baie mense deur vrees gedryf. Hulle vrees die onsekerheid van môre. Hulle vrees of hulle kos, werk en klere sal kry. Dit is die teenoorgestelde daarvan om op God te vertrou. In die Westerse kultuur vrees mense nie hierdie dinge nie. Kos en klere is maklik bekombaar, daar is baie werk, en mediese hulp is net ’n 911-oproep ver.

Die arm mense hier in Haïti sê dat dit makliker sou wees om op God te vertrou as hulle in Amerika was, maar is dit werklik so? Hoewel baie min mense in Amerika vrees dat hulle nie genoeg sal hê om te eet nie, vrees baie dat ander mense hulle nie sal aanvaar nie. Daar is sommige wat dalk vrees dat hulle nie genoeg geld sal hê om van te leef nie, maar daar is baie wat die dood vrees. Wat ook al ons vrees is, ons antwoord is om op God te vertrou.

Kom ons kyk na Dawid se lewe. Dawid was ’n jong seun. Toe sy ouer broers oorlog toe gegaan het, het die jong Dawid uitgegaan om sy vader se skape te versorg. Op die slagveld was daar ’n reus by die Filistynse leër met die naam Goliat. Hy het die Israeliete uitgedaag en gesê dat as een man sou uitkom en teen hom veg, die leër van die oorwinnaar oor die ander party sou heers. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 lees ons dat Goliat gesê het: …Ek daag vandag die leërs van Israel uit; gee my ’n man, dat ons saam kan veg. Toe Saul en die hele Israel hierdie woorde van die Filistyn hoor, was hulle verskrik en baie bevrees.

Later lees ons dat Isai, Dawid se vader, hom na die slagveld gestuur het om kos vir sy ouer broers te neem. Dawid het by die slagveld aangekom en gehoor hoe Goliat dieselfde woorde sê. Toe Dawid sien dat al die Israelitiese manne bang was, het hy dit nie verstaan nie. Waarom was God se volk bang vir hierdie onbesnede Filistyn?

Hoewel Dawid jonk was, was hy geen nuweling as dit daarby gekom het om sy vertroue op God te stel nie. Terwyl hy sy vader se skape opgepas het, het hy waarskynlik baie met God gepraat en Hom gevra om die skape te beskerm. Eendag het ’n beer gekom om die skape aan te val, en Dawid het die beer doodgemaak. ’n Ander dag het ’n leeu gekom om van die skape te vreet. Weer het die jong man, wat op God vertrou en geen vrees geken het nie, die bedreiging in die gesig gestaar en die leeu doodgemaak. Toe hy nou voor ’n skynbaar groter bedreiging te staan kom, vra Dawid eenvoudig: …wie is hierdie onbesnede Filistyn, dat hy die leërs van die lewende God moet uitdaag? –1Sa 17:26. Dawid het na koning Saul gegaan en gesê: Ek …sal gaan en teen hierdie Filistyn veg –1Sa 17:32. Dawid het weer op sy God vertrou, vyf gladde klippe geneem, gehardloop om die reus tegemoet te gaan en hom doodgemaak. Toe die mense hierdie skielike wending sien, was hulle verwonderd.

Volgens Psalm 20:7, wanneer ons op perde en strydwaens vertrou, is dit nie op die Here ons God nie. In Matteus 21:21 sê die Bybel dat ons deur geloof berge kan versit. Hier in Haïti het ek al in moeilike situasies beland waar God my enigste uitweg is. Wanneer ek gedwing is om op God te vertrou, het ek ontdek dat Hy steeds wonderwerke doen. Net soos Dawid met die leeu, die beer en die reus, kan ons ook leer dat dit die beste is om met ons hele hart op God te vertrou, en nie bloot as ’n laaste uitweg nie. Wanneer ons eerste op die Here vertrou, wys ons die wêreld iets wonderliks—dat hierdie God wat ons dien, lewe en werklik is.

Hier in Haïti was daar ’n man wat saam met sy vrou en drie jong kinders in ’n plakkershut hoog in die berge gewoon het. Maar daar was ’n probleem—hy was dodelik siek. Eendag het hy gehoor van ’n sendeling wat dikwels deur die berge gereis het. Ek het ’n boodskap van hom ontvang waarin hy sê dat hy amper dood was en dat hy nodig gehad het dat ek moes kom om vir hom te bid. Ek het gou na sy huis gegaan. Ek was verstom oor sy toestand. Hy het waarskynlik nie veel meer as 70 pond geweeg nie. Sy vrou het my vertel dat hy al langer as ’n jaar in die bed was. Hy kon nie praat nie; hy het net gefluister en diep, pynlike asemteue gehaal. Ons het heelwat tyd bestee aan ’n gesprek oor sy lewe, sy sonde en sy toekoms. Hy het vir my gesê dat as God hom sou genees, hy God sou dien en die res van sy lewe op Hom sou vertrou. Ek het geglo dat hy opreg was, maar ek was bang. Ek het begin bid, maar dit was beslis nie ’n kragtige gebed vol geloof nie. Dit was eerder ’n swak, nederige noodroep.

Toe ek huis toe gegaan het en deur daardie nag, kon ek aan niks anders as hom dink nie. Die duiwel het sy aanval begin. Ek het baie verwarrende, ontstellende gedagtes gehad: “Het jy alles gedoen wat jy kon? Wat as hy sterf? Waarom het jy hom nie hospitaal toe geneem nie?” Ek het in gebed na God gegaan. “O God,” het ek gebid, “hierdie man wou hê dat daar vir hom gebid moes word. Hy het nie vir ’n hospitaal gevra nie; hy het nie vir medisyne gevra nie. Asseblief, God, genees hierdie man. As hy sterf, wat sal ek volgende keer doen? O Vader, indien nie ter wille van hom nie, genees hom asseblief ter wille van my. Ek het U nodig, Vader.”

Ek het gebid soos nog nooit tevore nie, en toe het God my vrede gegee. Die volgende oggend het ek haastig teen die berg opgegaan na sy huis, maar hy was nie daar nie. “Nee, Here!” het ek gedink. Ek het rondgehardloop en my kop by ’n ander plakkershut ingesteek. Wat ek gesien het, het my oorweldig. Hy het daar gesit met ’n groot glimlag op sy gesig. Sy vrou het gesê dat hy daardie oggend in die tuin gewerk het. Sy het oor en oor gesê: “God het hom genees! God het hom genees!” Ek sal nooit die gevoel vergeet wat ek gehad het toe ek weer teen daardie berg afgereis het nie. My hart het oorgeloop van vreugde en dankbaarheid. “My God leef! Hy kan enigiets en alles doen! Hy is my God!” Ek het Hom gedank en geprys soos nog nooit tevore nie. “Die leeu” waarvoor ek te staan gekom het, was dood, en my geloof het gegroei. Die duiwel wil nie hê dat ons op God moet vertrou nie, want wanneer ons op God vertrou, doen Hy groot dinge en groei ons geloof.

Wanneer ons op God vertrou, is daar ’n risiko—wat as God nie ingryp nie? Ons kan in die verleentheid kom, of erger nog—“Wat as ek in geloof vorentoe tree en God niks doen nie?” Onthou, dit is nie geloof as ons die uitkoms ken nie. Geloof is om in gehoorsaamheid te wandel en God se Woord te glo wanneer ons nie die uitkoms ken nie. As God Dawid nie gehelp het nie, sou Goliat hom beslis doodgemaak het. Dit was Daniël se geloof wat hom laat aanhou bid het tot God, hoewel hy geweet het dat ’n leeukuil op hom gewag het. Sadrag, Mesag en Abednego het so ’n groot geloof in God gehad dat hulle vir die koning gesê het dat hulle, selfs as God sou kies om hulle nie uit die vuur te red nie, steeds …u gode nie sal dien of die goue beeld wat u opgerig het, sal aanbid nie –Dan 3:18. En dan was daar Gideon en sy driehonderd manne. Die lys godvresende manne wat hulle lewe op die spel geplaas het om te bewys dat hulle God leef, hou aan en aan.

Wanneer ons in geloof vorentoe tree en op ons God vertrou, gebeur daar altyd iets (soms nou, soms later; soms op ’n manier wat sin maak, soms op ’n manier wat skynbaar geen aardse sin maak nie). Tog tree God wel op, en ons geloof groei. Wanneer ons werklik in God glo, sal ons op Hom vertrou. Dan is dit baie makliker om die Evangelieboodskap met ander te deel. Net soos Josua nie ’n vloot stootskrapers gereed gehad het by Jerigo nie, het ons ook nie ’n rugsteunplan nodig wanneer ons op God vertrou nie.

Dit is waar dat die groot denkers en finansiële steun van baie mense in Amerika en ander moderne lande God vervang het. Daar is ’n manier om die meeste praktiese dinge sonder God te doen. Trouens, die meeste mense sê dat dit nie gesonde verstand is om op God te vertrou nie. As jy oor ’n siek kind bid, is dit nie gesonde verstand nie. As jy ’n goed betaalde werk van die hand wys omdat jy nie glo dat dit God se wil is nie, is dit nie gesonde verstand nie. As jy jou besittings verkoop en aan die armes gee, is dit nie gesonde verstand nie. Hierdie mense is reg—om op God te vertrou is nie gesonde verstand nie. Om sewe keer om ’n muur te trek in die geloof dat dit sal omval, is nie gesonde verstand nie. Om met net 300 manne teen ’n groot leër in die stryd te trek, wat so talryk soos sprinkane was, is ook nie gesonde verstand nie. Die meeste dinge wat Christene doen wat op God vertrou, maak nie sin nie, maar dit wys wel vir die wêreld dat hulle werklik op God vertrou, en dit is wat die wêreld vandag weer op sy kop sal keer.

Ek onthou een dag baie goed. Ek was weg van die huis toe ek ’n oproep van my vrou ontvang het. Sy het vir my gesê om gou huis toe te kom—dit was ’n noodgeval! Ons tweejarige seuntjie is deur bye gesteek. Ek het huis toe gejaag en die buurt in chaos aangetref. Mense het oral rondgehardloop. Ek het my vrou en seun by die buurman se huis aangetref, ’n plaaslike predikant. My seun het in my vrou se arms gelê, en sy het my vertel dat hy etlike honderde kere gesteek is. Die predikant het my baie ernstig aangekyk en gesê dat die seun beslis sou sterf as ek hom nie dadelik hospitaal toe neem nie. Ek onthou dat ek aan een ding gedink het—God kan genees! Ek het my seun opgetel, hom oorkant die straat na ons huis geneem en gebid. Dit was nie lank nie of hy het begin herstel—die volgende dag het hy weer buite gespeel.

Baie mense hier in Haïti neem hulle siekes na die toordokter, en hy genees hulle. Dit is maar wat gebeur. Hoeveel te meer kan ons God nie doen nie! Moet my asseblief nie verkeerd verstaan nie. Ek sê nie dat ons nie na die dokter of hospitaal toe moet gaan nie; ek probeer eerder beklemtoon dat ons vertroue op God moet wees.

Jare gelede het ek besluit om ’n deeltydse werk aan te pak deur messe te verkoop. Ek moes hierdie messe van huis tot huis neem. Ek het nie in messe belanggestel nie, maar het net probeer om ’n bietjie ekstra geld te verdien. Ek was ’n vreeslike mesverkoper. Oral waar ek gegaan het, het almal nee gesê.

Eendag het die baas my na sy kantoor geneem en vir my gesê dat hy opgemerk het dat ek geen messe verkoop nie, en besef het dat hy vergeet het om my te wys hoe die messe werk. Ons het toe daar in sy kantoor gesit terwyl hy oor elke mes gepraat het. Hy het ’n klein hopie kombuisgereedskap van ’n ander handelsmerk gehad, wat bekend was vir sy gehalte, en dit as vergelyking gebruik. Eers het hy ’n klein stukkie leer opgetel en my gevra om dit met een van die “ander” messe middeldeur te sny. Ek het die stuk leer redelik maklik deursaag. Toe het hy my aangesê om een van sy messe te gebruik en dieselfde te doen. Die nuwe mes het deur die leer gesny asof dit nie eens daar was nie! Ek was werklik verstom. Toe tel hy ’n pennie op en sê ek moet dit met die “ander” skêr middeldeur sny. Ek het probeer, maar misluk; hulle wou dit eenvoudig nie sny nie. Toe sê hy ek moet dieselfde met sy skêr probeer. Dit het maklik deur die pennie gesny, en ek was weer verstom oor die produk. Hy het gesê dat ek nou geweet het dat hierdie messe die beste was en dat ek hulle voortaan behoort te kan verkoop. Hy was reg. Ek het oral waar ek gegaan het, begin messe verkoop! Ek onthou selfs dat ek by ’n swak onderhoude sleepwa-huis ingestap het sonder veel hoop dat hulle iets sou koop. Tot my verbasing het hulle messe ter waarde van meer as $3,000 gekoop.

Die rede waarom ek begin verkoop het, is duidelik—ek het in my produk geglo. Net so sal ons selfvertroue hê as ons op God vertrou. In ’n tyd wanneer die meeste mense wat sê dat hulle Christene is, hulle vir God skaam en skaam is om vir die waarheid op te staan, kan ons ’n helder, skynende lig wees. Ons kan ’n volk wees wat die wêreld en ons gemeenskappe intrek met ’n Evangelie waarin ons werklik glo! Wanneer ons dit doen, sal die wêreld dit sien en reageer. Baie mense soek; hulle is op soek na antwoorde. Wanneer iemand ons vra waarom ons die dinge doen wat ons doen of die klere dra wat ons dra, wat antwoord ons? Antwoord ons met selfvertroue? Het ons ’n toepaslike Bybelvers? Of raak ons verleë en wil ons ’n gat hê om in weg te kruip? As die wêreld kon sien dat ons vertroue in ons God het en Hom met geesdrif gehoorsaam, sou dit ’n kragtige getuienis wees.

Ek onthou hoe ek een keer saam met ’n klein groepie deur die lughawe gereis het. Terwyl ons in die ry gestaan het, het ek gehoor hoe ’n vrou een van die ongetroude susters in ons groep vra waarom sy daardie “ding” op haar kop dra. Ek was opgewonde om ongemerk te luister, en ek was verheug toe ek haar antwoord hoor. “Het jy al ooit 1 Korintiërs 11 gelees? Daar word ons geleer dat vroue hulle hoofde moet bedek. Dit is ’n teken van onderdanigheid.” Die vrou was verstom oor haar antwoord en het gesê dat sy dit nog nooit gehoor het nie, en dat haar pa ’n predikant was. Hulle het ’n baie interessante gesprek voortgesit, wat geëindig het daarmee dat die vrou huis toe wou gaan om haar Bybel te bestudeer.

’n Traktaatjie kan baie goed doen; so ook ’n kragtige preek of ’n gedrukte artikel, maar waarna hierdie wêreld soek, is iemand wat volkome op God vertrou! Hulle wil “iets sien wat werk”, en waarom nie? Ons God wil ons gebruik om te wys hoe sterk Hy is. Elkeen van ons wil tog deur God gebruik word. Ons kan. Elkeen van ons kan. Die antwoord is om met jou hele hart op die HERE te vertrou en nie op jou eie insig staat te maak nie –Spr 3:5.

If marriage is a covenant, what is the significance of covenant relationship? What makes it a covenant relationship, and how does this differ from any other relationship? These are answers that we must pursue if we are to understand the permanence of marriage and if we are to successfully navigate the rocky shores of a troubled marriage.

Covenant in our society has become archaic. The cultural revolution of the sixties has made divorce culturally acceptable, and life-long fidelity in marriage has become the exception rather than the rule. Unfortunately, this blight has infected most mainstream churches and is currently invading our Anabaptist churches.

Covenant is God’s idea. He is the primary covenant maker. His holy name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word. The Hebrew origin of “Jehovah” is yeh-ho-vaw. This word combines two Hebrew verbs of being. A most literal translation for the name yeh-ho-vaw would be (is is) or as God said to Moses “I am that I am.”

God’s name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word, that he cannot lie, and that He is true to His character. James states it this way: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning –Jas 1:17.

What makes a covenant?

Careful investigation of scripture will reveal that there are three key elements in the establishment of a covenant.

  • Words
  • Witnesses
  • That which ratifies the covenant

Words

Words define the terms and conditions of a covenant. It is very important that the terms and conditions of the covenant be clearly defined and understood by both parties involved. When God made covenant with Abraham, He spake and said, And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee –Gen 17:7.

When God made covenant with the nation of Israel at Mt Sinai, He gave them the Law which was the terms and conditions of the Mosaic covenant.

In our Bibles today we have the Old and the New Testament. This refers to the Old and the New Covenant. In the New Testament we have the teachings of Jesus and His Apostles which supersede the Old Testament law. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said repeatedly, “You have heard that it hath been said, but I say unto you.”

The Hebrew writer had this to say about the New Covenant: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises –Heb 8:6.

On our wedding day we use words with precise meaning to establish a covenant that is binding “…till death do us part.” Wedding vows may contain some variation but should always include a commitment to a mutually loving relationship that is binding for life, and thus irrevocable.

Witnesses

Another important part of a covenant is the witnesses. Witnesses provide validation and accountability to the vows that have been made. This is especially true of a covenant made between two people.

When Joshua re-established the covenant with Israel upon entering the land of Canaan, he challenged them: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses –Jos 24:22. What they were saying was that, “We will hold one another accountable for the commitments that we are making today.”

Regarding the New Covenant, we have the testimony of the Apostle John where he says: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one –1Joh 5:7-8. Here John is saying that in this New Covenant between God and man there are three witnesses in heaven and three witnesses in earth, and these witnesses all agree.

In the establishment of a marriage covenant the wedding guests are the witnesses. Every guest becomes a witness of the vows that are made. By their presence and blessing, they validate the marriage and become personally responsible to ensure that this marriage endures.

This community commitment to the permanence of marriage is the moral fabric of our society and our churches. When a society becomes negligent in enforcing the permanence of marriage, chaos and confusion ensue. We see this in the society around us. Unfortunately, we are also seeing an increasing number of marriage breakups within our Anabaptist churches.

That which ratifies the covenant

The final step in establishing a covenant is that which ratifies and renders binding and effective the terms of the covenant. Historically there have been a variety of methods of binding a covenant. Ancient Bedouins had a practice of using salt to bind a covenant. Each party would give to the other a measure of salt. The salt was mixed with their respective stores of salt making it impossible to ever separate “my salt” from “your salt.” This symbolized the immutability of this treaty.

Then there was the practice of berith. Berith is a Hebrew word that means “to cut.” In ancient Israel a covenant was ratified by “cutting a covenant.” This practice is clearly illustrated in Genesis 15 where God ratified His covenant with Abraham. Abraham asked God, …Lord GOD, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it? –Gen 15:8. God’s response to Abraham’s plea was …Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon –Gen 15:9. Abraham took these animals and divided them in the midst and lay them out as a sacrifice to God. God reaffirmed His covenant with Abraham (with words), and then in verse 17, we have this mysterious event: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces –Gen 15:17. This was “berith” or the “cutting of the covenant.” This ceremony ratified and rendered binding the terms and conditions of the covenant. After this event, we have no record that Abraham ever questioned or doubted the promise of God, although he did take it into his own hands to bring that promise to fruition.

When God made covenant with Israel at Mt Sinai, …Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you concerning all these words –Exo 24:8. This blood rendered binding and effective the terms and conditions set forth in the law—this was the Old Covenant.

When God made covenant with you and I at Mt Calvary, the blood of Jesus became the ratifying evidence or the binding token of His New Covenant with us. When we partake of the communion, we are commemorating the covenant that we have with God through Christ.

What ratifies the marriage covenant? As we have already seen, in a marriage we have words (the vows), and we have witnesses (the guests). Does this complete the marriage? No. The marriage is not complete until there is a coming together in physical intimacy. This completes or, as we sometimes say, consummates the marriage covenant. This is that which ratifies and renders binding and permanent the terms and conditions of the marriage covenant. Early on in Scripture we have example of this. And Adam knew Eve his wife… Gen 4:1. Then later on we see another example, And Isaac brought her [Rebekah] into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her… –Gen 24:67. Physical oneness belongs to covenant. This is why such a relationship outside of marriage is sin. Fornication or adultery takes that which God has ordained to be inextricably linked to marriage and adulterates the covenant.

When a married couple comes together in physical union they are commemorating and celebrating their marriage covenant. This is the start of them establishing a biblical “one flesh” reality. From this blessed union new life emerges in the form of precious “little ones” and of hearts that are renewed by the power of love.

When we partake of the bread and the wine of communion we are commemorating and celebrating our covenant relationship with Christ. From this blessed oneness new life emerges in the form of hearts that are renewed by the power of love. This is the strength of covenant.

Where these three elements exist—vows, witnesses, and that which ratifies—we have a covenant relationship. How does a covenant relationship differ from any other relationship?

A commitment to fidelity

Some of the most noble words that human lips can utter are “I promise to love you till death do us part.” On our wedding day these words are easy to utter, and we may be most sincere when we speak them. The fact is that no one can possibly know what those words may cost in the course of a lifetime.

Love is a choice and must become established and endure as an every day walk of life. We must choose to direct our affection toward the one of our covenant love and away from the enticements of others. Many, many marriages are destroyed through infidelity.

God has designed marriage to be powerfully bonding. The spiritual, emotional, and physical attachment of marriage creates an inseparable bond. In Genesis we read Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh –Gen 2:24. The word cleave in this verse denotes “being welded or glued together in such a way as to be inseparable.”

To break the marriage bond through infidelity causes rending and wounding to both parties. Satan, the great deceiver, would have us to believe that being unfaithful to our spouse will somehow benefit us. This is a huge lie.

A commitment to faithfulness

God demonstrated covenant faithfulness in his dealings with His Old Testament bride—the nation of Israel. She was not true to her covenant vows. She turned from the worship of Jehovah, and she bowed her knee to pagan altars. Despite her unfaithfulness, God continued to pursue her and call her back unto himself. Israel’s unfaithfulness did not alter God’s faithfulness. This is the strength of covenant love. Covenant love is not contingent upon the actions of the other party. Covenant love persists even though it is not reciprocated. This is a kingdom concept. Paul taught, Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head –Rom 12:20. Would this principle not most aptly apply to a broken marriage?

The strength of covenant can only be fully realized through an understanding of the divine love of God for us. Our salvation is dependent upon God’s perfect love for us. He continues to love us even though our love for Him is sometimes flawed. His unfailing love continues to draw us back unto himself. The strength of covenant in marriage is found in seeking to emulate this divine love. This divine love will not be found in romance novels or other books on marriage. This divine love can only be found in an intimate relationship with “The Source” of undying love.

Αν ο γάμος είναι διαθήκη, ποια είναι η σημασία της σχέσης διαθήκης; Τι την κάνει σχέση διαθήκης και σε τι διαφέρει από κάθε άλλη σχέση; Αυτά είναι τα ερωτήματα στα οποία πρέπει να αναζητήσουμε απαντήσεις, αν θέλουμε να κατανοήσουμε τη μονιμότητα του γάμου και να μπορέσουμε να πλεύσουμε με επιτυχία στα βραχώδη νερά ενός προβληματικού γάμου.

Η διαθήκη έχει γίνει κάτι το παρωχημένο στην κοινωνία μας. Η πολιτιστική επανάσταση της δεκαετίας του ’60 έκανε το διαζύγιο πολιτισμικά αποδεκτό, και η ισόβια πίστη στον γάμο έγινε η εξαίρεση αντί για τον κανόνα. Δυστυχώς, αυτή η μάστιγα έχει μολύνει τις περισσότερες κύριες εκκλησίες και εισβάλλει τώρα στις αναβαπτιστικές εκκλησίες μας.

Η διαθήκη είναι ιδέα του Θεού. Εκείνος είναι ο κατεξοχήν συντάκτης διαθηκών. Το άγιο όνομά Του «Ιεχωβά» δείχνει ότι ο Θεός είναι πάντοτε πιστός στον λόγο Του. Η εβραϊκή προέλευση του «Ιεχωβά» είναι yeh-ho-vaw. Η λέξη αυτή συνδυάζει δύο εβραϊκά ρήματα ύπαρξης. Μια όσο το δυνατόν πιο κυριολεκτική απόδοση του ονόματος yeh-ho-vaw θα ήταν «είναι είναι» ή, όπως είπε ο Θεός στον Μωυσή, «Εγώ είμαι αυτός που είμαι».

Το όνομα του Θεού «Ιεχωβά» δείχνει ότι ο Θεός είναι πάντοτε πιστός στον λόγο Του, ότι δεν μπορεί να πει ψέματα και ότι είναι πιστός στον χαρακτήρα Του. Ο Ιάκωβος το διατυπώνει ως εξής: Κάθε αγαθή δόση και κάθε τέλειο δώρημα είναι από ψηλά και κατεβαίνει από τον Πατέρα των φώτων, στον οποίο δεν υπάρχει μεταβολή ούτε σκιά από τροπή –Ιακ 1:17.

Τι κάνει μια διαθήκη;

Μια προσεκτική διερεύνηση της Γραφής αποκαλύπτει ότι υπάρχουν τρία βασικά στοιχεία στη σύναψη μιας διαθήκης.

  • Λόγια
  • Μάρτυρες
  • Εκείνο που επικυρώνει τη διαθήκη

Λόγια

Τα λόγια ορίζουν τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις μιας διαθήκης. Είναι πολύ σημαντικό οι όροι και οι προϋποθέσεις της διαθήκης να ορίζονται με σαφήνεια και να γίνονται κατανοητοί και από τα δύο εμπλεκόμενα μέρη. Όταν ο Θεός σύναψε διαθήκη με τον Αβραάμ, μίλησε και είπε: Και θα θεμελιώσω τη διαθήκη μου ανάμεσα σε μένα και σε σένα και στους απογόνους σου μετά από σένα, στις γενεές τους, ως αιώνια διαθήκη, ώστε να είμαι Θεός δικός σου και των απογόνων σου μετά από σένα –Γεν 17:7.

Όταν ο Θεός σύναψε διαθήκη με το έθνος του Ισραήλ στο όρος Σινά, τους έδωσε τον Νόμο, ο οποίος αποτελούσε τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις της Μωσαϊκής διαθήκης.

Στις σημερινές μας Βίβλους έχουμε την Παλαιά και την Καινή Διαθήκη. Αυτό αναφέρεται στην Παλαιά και την Καινή Διαθήκη. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη έχουμε τις διδασκαλίες του Ιησού και των αποστόλων Του, οι οποίες υπερισχύουν του νόμου της Παλαιάς Διαθήκης. Στην Επί του Όρους Ομιλία, ο Ιησούς είπε επανειλημμένα: «Έχετε ακούσει ότι ειπώθηκε, αλλά εγώ σας λέω».

Ο συγγραφέας της προς Εβραίους επιστολής είπε τα εξής για την Καινή Διαθήκη: Τώρα όμως έχει λάβει μια πολύ ανώτερη διακονία, καθώς είναι και μεσίτης καλύτερης διαθήκης, η οποία θεσπίστηκε με βάση καλύτερες υποσχέσεις –Εβρ 8:6.

Την ημέρα του γάμου μας χρησιμοποιούμε λόγια με ακριβές νόημα για να συνάψουμε μια δεσμευτική διαθήκη «…μέχρι να μας χωρίσει ο θάνατος». Οι γαμήλιοι όρκοι μπορεί να διαφέρουν κάπως, αλλά πρέπει πάντοτε να περιλαμβάνουν τη δέσμευση για μια σχέση αμοιβαίας αγάπης, δεσμευτική για όλη τη ζωή και, επομένως, αμετάκλητη.

Μάρτυρες

Ένα άλλο σημαντικό μέρος μιας διαθήκης είναι οι μάρτυρες. Οι μάρτυρες επικυρώνουν τους όρκους που έχουν δοθεί και διασφαλίζουν τη λογοδοσία. Αυτό ισχύει ιδιαίτερα για μια διαθήκη που συνάπτεται ανάμεσα σε δύο ανθρώπους.

Όταν ο Ιησούς του Ναυή επαναβεβαίωσε τη διαθήκη με τον Ισραήλ κατά την είσοδό τους στη γη Χαναάν, τους προκάλεσε: Και ο Ιησούς είπε στον λαό: Εσείς είστε μάρτυρες εναντίον του εαυτού σας ότι διαλέξατε τον Κύριο για να τον υπηρετείτε. Και εκείνοι είπαν: Είμαστε μάρτυρες –Ιησ Ναυή 24:22. Αυτό που έλεγαν ήταν: «Θα κρατήσουμε ο ένας τον άλλον υπόλογο για τις δεσμεύσεις που αναλαμβάνουμε σήμερα».

Όσον αφορά την Καινή Διαθήκη, έχουμε τη μαρτυρία του αποστόλου Ιωάννη, ο οποίος λέει: Επειδή τρεις είναι αυτοί που μαρτυρούν στον ουρανό: ο Πατέρας, ο Λόγος και το Άγιο Πνεύμα· και αυτοί οι τρεις είναι ένα. Και τρεις είναι αυτοί που μαρτυρούν στη γη: το Πνεύμα, το νερό και το αίμα· και οι τρεις συμφωνούν –Α΄ Ιω 5:7-8. Εδώ ο Ιωάννης λέει ότι σε αυτή την Καινή Διαθήκη ανάμεσα στον Θεό και τον άνθρωπο υπάρχουν τρεις μάρτυρες στον ουρανό και τρεις μάρτυρες στη γη, και όλοι αυτοί οι μάρτυρες συμφωνούν.

Κατά τη σύναψη μιας γαμήλιας διαθήκης, οι καλεσμένοι του γάμου είναι οι μάρτυρες. Κάθε καλεσμένος γίνεται μάρτυρας των όρκων που δίνονται. Με την παρουσία και την ευλογία τους, επικυρώνουν τον γάμο και αναλαμβάνουν προσωπικά την ευθύνη να διασφαλίσουν ότι αυτός ο γάμος θα διαρκέσει.

Αυτή η δέσμευση της κοινότητας στη μονιμότητα του γάμου αποτελεί τον ηθικό ιστό της κοινωνίας μας και των εκκλησιών μας. Όταν μια κοινωνία αμελεί να επιβάλλει τη μονιμότητα του γάμου, ακολουθούν χάος και σύγχυση. Αυτό το βλέπουμε στην κοινωνία γύρω μας. Δυστυχώς, βλέπουμε επίσης να αυξάνονται οι διαλύσεις γάμων στις αναβαπτιστικές εκκλησίες μας.

Εκείνο που επικυρώνει τη διαθήκη

Το τελικό βήμα για τη σύναψη μιας διαθήκης είναι εκείνο που την επικυρώνει και καθιστά τους όρους της δεσμευτικούς και ισχυρούς. Ιστορικά, υπήρξαν διάφοροι τρόποι για να δεσμεύσουν μια διαθήκη. Οι αρχαίοι Βεδουίνοι είχαν τη συνήθεια να χρησιμοποιούν αλάτι για να δεσμεύσουν μια διαθήκη. Κάθε μέρος έδινε στο άλλο μια ποσότητα αλατιού. Το αλάτι αναμειγνυόταν με τα αντίστοιχα αποθέματα αλατιού τους, καθιστώντας αδύνατο να διαχωριστεί ποτέ «το δικό μου αλάτι» από «το δικό σου αλάτι». Αυτό συμβόλιζε το αμετάβλητο της συνθήκης.

Υπήρχε επίσης η πρακτική του μπέριτ. Το μπέριτ είναι εβραϊκή λέξη που σημαίνει «κόβω». Στο αρχαίο Ισραήλ, μια διαθήκη επικυρωνόταν με το «κόψιμο διαθήκης». Αυτή η πρακτική παρουσιάζεται ξεκάθαρα στη Γένεση 15, όπου ο Θεός επικύρωσε τη διαθήκη Του με τον Αβραάμ. Ο Αβραάμ ρώτησε τον Θεό: …Κύριε Θεέ, από τι θα γνωρίσω ότι θα την κληρονομήσω; –Γεν 15:8. Η απάντηση του Θεού στην ικεσία του Αβραάμ ήταν: …Πάρε μου μια δαμάλα τριών χρονών, μια κατσίκα τριών χρονών, ένα κριάρι τριών χρονών, ένα τρυγόνι και ένα νεαρό περιστέρι –Γεν 15:9. Ο Αβραάμ πήρε αυτά τα ζώα, τα έκοψε στη μέση και τα έβαλε στη σειρά ως θυσία στον Θεό. Ο Θεός επαναβεβαίωσε τη διαθήκη Του με τον Αβραάμ (με λόγια) και έπειτα, στο εδάφιο 17, έχουμε αυτό το μυστηριώδες γεγονός: Και όταν ο ήλιος έδυσε και σκοτείνιασε, να, ένα καπνιστό καμίνι και μια αναμμένη λαμπάδα πέρασαν ανάμεσα από εκείνα τα κομμάτια –Γεν 15:17. Αυτό ήταν το «μπέριτ» ή το «κόψιμο της διαθήκης». Η τελετή αυτή επικύρωσε τη διαθήκη και κατέστησε δεσμευτικούς τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις της. Μετά από αυτό το γεγονός, δεν έχουμε καμία καταγραφή ότι ο Αβραάμ αμφισβήτησε ξανά ή αμφέβαλε για την υπόσχεση του Θεού, αν και πήρε την κατάσταση στα χέρια του για να εκπληρώσει εκείνη την υπόσχεση.

Όταν ο Θεός σύναψε διαθήκη με τον Ισραήλ στο όρος Σινά, …ο Μωυσής πήρε το αίμα και το ράντισε επάνω στον λαό και είπε: Να το αίμα της διαθήκης, την οποία ο Κύριος έκανε μαζί σας, σύμφωνα με όλα αυτά τα λόγια –Έξ 24:8. Αυτό το αίμα κατέστησε δεσμευτικούς και ισχυρούς τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις που ορίζονταν στον νόμο — αυτή ήταν η Παλαιά Διαθήκη.

Όταν ο Θεός σύναψε διαθήκη με εσένα κι εμένα στον Γολγοθά, το αίμα του Ιησού έγινε το επικυρωτικό τεκμήριο, ή το δεσμευτικό σημείο, της Καινής Διαθήκης Του μαζί μας. Όταν κοινωνούμε, αναμνημονεύουμε τη διαθήκη που έχουμε με τον Θεό μέσω του Χριστού.

Τι επικυρώνει τη γαμήλια διαθήκη; Όπως έχουμε ήδη δει, στον γάμο έχουμε λόγια (τους όρκους) και μάρτυρες (τους καλεσμένους). Αρκούν αυτά για να ολοκληρωθεί ο γάμος; Όχι. Ο γάμος δεν ολοκληρώνεται μέχρι να υπάρξει σωματική ένωση. Αυτή ολοκληρώνει ή, όπως λέμε μερικές φορές, συντελεί τον γάμο. Αυτό είναι εκείνο που επικυρώνει τη γαμήλια διαθήκη και καθιστά τους όρους και τις προϋποθέσεις της δεσμευτικούς και μόνιμους. Από τα πρώτα κιόλας σημεία της Γραφής έχουμε ένα παράδειγμα αυτού: Και ο Αδάμ γνώρισε την Εύα, τη γυναίκα του… Γεν 4:1. Αργότερα βλέπουμε ένα ακόμη παράδειγμα: Και ο Ισαάκ την έφερε [τη Ρεβέκκα] στη σκηνή της μητέρας του, της Σάρρας, και πήρε τη Ρεβέκκα για γυναίκα του· και την αγάπησε… –Γεν 24:67. Η σωματική ενότητα ανήκει στη διαθήκη. Γι’ αυτό μια τέτοια σχέση έξω από τον γάμο είναι αμαρτία. Η πορνεία ή η μοιχεία παίρνει αυτό που ο Θεός όρισε να είναι άρρηκτα συνδεδεμένο με τον γάμο και νοθεύει τη διαθήκη.

Όταν ένα παντρεμένο ζευγάρι ενώνεται σωματικά, αναμνημονεύει και γιορτάζει τη γαμήλια διαθήκη του. Έτσι αρχίζει να θεμελιώνει τη βιβλική πραγματικότητα του «ενός σώματος». Από αυτή την ευλογημένη ένωση αναδύεται νέα ζωή με τη μορφή πολύτιμων «μικρών» και καρδιών που ανανεώνονται με τη δύναμη της αγάπης.

Όταν κοινωνούμε τον άρτο και τον οίνο, αναμνημονεύουμε και γιορτάζουμε τη σχέση διαθήκης μας με τον Χριστό. Από αυτή την ευλογημένη ενότητα αναδύεται νέα ζωή με τη μορφή καρδιών που ανανεώνονται με τη δύναμη της αγάπης. Αυτή είναι η δύναμη της διαθήκης.

Όπου υπάρχουν αυτά τα τρία στοιχεία —όρκοι, μάρτυρες και εκείνο που επικυρώνει— έχουμε μια σχέση διαθήκης. Σε τι διαφέρει μια σχέση διαθήκης από κάθε άλλη σχέση;

Δέσμευση στην αποκλειστικότητα

Μερικά από τα πιο ευγενή λόγια που μπορούν να προφέρουν ανθρώπινα χείλη είναι: «Υπόσχομαι να σε αγαπώ μέχρι να μας χωρίσει ο θάνατος». Την ημέρα του γάμου μας είναι εύκολο να προφέρουμε αυτά τα λόγια και μπορεί να είμαστε απολύτως ειλικρινείς όταν τα λέμε. Η αλήθεια είναι πως κανείς δεν μπορεί να γνωρίζει τι μπορεί να του κοστίσουν αυτά τα λόγια κατά τη διάρκεια μιας ολόκληρης ζωής.

Η αγάπη είναι επιλογή και πρέπει να εδραιωθεί και να διατηρηθεί ως καθημερινός τρόπος ζωής. Πρέπει να επιλέγουμε να στρέφουμε την αγάπη μας προς εκείνον που αγαπάμε με τη διαθήκη μας και μακριά από τους πειρασμούς των άλλων. Πολλοί, πάρα πολλοί γάμοι καταστρέφονται εξαιτίας της απιστίας.

Ο Θεός σχεδίασε τον γάμο ώστε να δημιουργεί ισχυρό δεσμό. Η πνευματική, συναισθηματική και σωματική σύνδεση του γάμου δημιουργεί έναν αδιάρρηκτο δεσμό. Στη Γένεση διαβάζουμε: Γι’ αυτό ο άνθρωπος θα αφήσει τον πατέρα του και τη μητέρα του και θα προσκολληθεί στη γυναίκα του· και θα είναι οι δύο μία σάρκα –Γεν 2:24. Η λέξη προσκολληθεί σε αυτό το εδάφιο σημαίνει «να συγκολληθεί ή να κολληθεί με τέτοιον τρόπο, ώστε να μην μπορούν να χωριστούν».

Η διάρρηξη του γαμήλιου δεσμού μέσω της απιστίας προκαλεί ρήξη και πληγώνει και τα δύο μέρη. Ο Σατανάς, ο μεγάλος απατεώνας, θέλει να πιστέψουμε ότι η απιστία προς τον σύζυγο ή τη σύζυγό μας θα μας ωφελήσει κατά κάποιον τρόπο. Αυτό είναι ένα τεράστιο ψέμα.

Δέσμευση στην πιστότητα

Ο Θεός έδειξε πιστότητα στη διαθήκη μέσα από τη συμπεριφορά Του προς την αρχαία νύφη Του στην Παλαιά Διαθήκη — το έθνος του Ισραήλ. Εκείνη δεν έμεινε πιστή στους όρκους της διαθήκης της. Αποστράφηκε τη λατρεία του Ιεχωβά και προσκύνησε σε ειδωλολατρικούς βωμούς. Παρά την απιστία της, ο Θεός συνέχισε να την αναζητά και να την καλεί να επιστρέψει κοντά Του. Η απιστία του Ισραήλ δεν άλλαξε την πιστότητα του Θεού. Αυτή είναι η δύναμη της αγάπης της διαθήκης. Η αγάπη της διαθήκης δεν εξαρτάται από τις πράξεις του άλλου μέρους. Επιμένει ακόμη κι όταν δεν ανταποδίδεται. Αυτή είναι μια βασιλική αρχή. Ο Παύλος δίδαξε: Αν ο εχθρός σου πεινάει, τάισέ τον· αν διψάει, πότισέ τον· επειδή, κάνοντας αυτό, θα μαζέψεις αναμμένα κάρβουνα επάνω στο κεφάλι του –Ρωμ 12:20. Δεν θα ίσχυε αυτή η αρχή με τον πιο κατάλληλο τρόπο σε έναν διαλυμένο γάμο;

Η δύναμη της διαθήκης μπορεί να γίνει πλήρως αντιληπτή μόνο μέσω της κατανόησης της θεϊκής αγάπης του Θεού για εμάς. Η σωτηρία μας εξαρτάται από την τέλεια αγάπη του Θεού για εμάς. Εκείνος συνεχίζει να μας αγαπά, παρόλο που η αγάπη μας γι’ Αυτόν είναι μερικές φορές ατελής. Η αδιάλειπτη αγάπη Του εξακολουθεί να μας ελκύει πίσω κοντά Του. Η δύναμη της διαθήκης στον γάμο βρίσκεται στην προσπάθεια να μιμηθούμε αυτή τη θεϊκή αγάπη. Αυτή τη θεϊκή αγάπη δεν θα τη βρούμε σε αισθηματικά μυθιστορήματα ή σε άλλα βιβλία για τον γάμο. Today, I’d like to continue and possibly complete our discussion of Regenerative Medicine. I want to consider where it stands today, and how Christians can navigate the complex maze of treatments. As you may recall, in the previous issue of this magazine we discussed that Regenerative Medicine is man’s attempt to re-create organ systems. We described how fetal tissue was attempted to be used, due to its low rate of rejection by the people receiving it. Medically speaking, it was problematic in that, if used on a large scale, it would require large amounts of aborted fetuses. Later, embryonic stem cells were studied in depth. Here, embryos, which are newly conceived humans in their earliest stages, are dissected (cut apart) and stem cells are taken.

Think of stem cells as indolent, immature adults, who live in their parents’ basements, without direction, not knowing what they want to do with their lives. With a little encouragement and direction, they can finally find their way, finding a specialized skill and important role in life. In like manner, scientists have discovered ways to “program” these stem cells, “encouraging” them to become specialized into types of cells, such as nerve, heart, blood, and insulin producing. These cells would then be grown in a lab, then used to repair or replace the diseased or injured tissue.

However, “taking” stem cells from embryos results in his or her (the embryo’s) destruction. This is obviously problematic for Christians, knowing that one of the seven things that the Lord says is an abomination is …hands that shed innocent blood –Pro 6:17. Additionally, the sixth commandment directs, Thou shalt not kill –Exo 20:13. Because these objections were recognized by the scientific community, there was pressure to find an alternative.

The Apostle Paul states, There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able; but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it –1Co 10:13. His words are as true today as they were 2000 years ago. While Christians suffer from disease just as commonly as non-Christians do, modern medicine can present the “temptation” of a treatment and relief from disease or injury that is actually immoral. But God is faithful, and his escape is twofold. First and foremost, He gave His son to bear our burdens. It is to this Great Physician that we should always turn to first.

In the case of stem cell treatments, it so happens that it was discovered that these immature stem cells are not only found in human embryos, but they are also found in all people, from infants to grown-ups as well. This may be the physical “escape” for His faithful children. These immature stem cells (usually obtained from a patient’s fat tissue or bone marrow) can be grown, cultured, and used just as well as embryonic stem cells. It turns out that “Adult Stem Cells” have actually been more clinically effective, since they are “custom designed” for each individual, and since they come from that person’s own body; therefore, there is very little problem with rejection.

Umbilical cord stem cells have also been shown to be useful, particularly in bone and cartilage treatments. Just as there have been obstacles to overcome when using embryonic stem cells, so too there are problems with developing treatments using adult or umbilical cord stem cells. Think again of a stem cell as an immature, indolent adult. Just having him “hang out” with a master carpenter will not make him a master carpenter if all he does is find entertainment on his cell phone. Stem cells, like an apprentice, need intense, focused training and direction to become specialists in their chosen field of expertise. Learning how to turn these “switches” on is perhaps one of the greatest challenges. The main idea here is that just injecting stem cells that have not been “programmed” or “trained” into damaged or diseased tissue will not automatically make them “know” what to become or how to function.

Similarly, just putting a young electronics apprentice on a bus that is traveling into a city that just had a power grid failure will not result in restoring the power. Here the parallel is placing stem cells into the brain of a stroke victim or a paraplegic accident victim, hoping that the stem cells will “know” what to do, and which specific connections to repair in order to restore function. This may not work as hoped. It would be fruitless to expect success unless and until these problems are also addressed.

Then there is the lingering problem of these eager youngsters (stem cells) knowing when to stop. The problem with fetal tissue turning into cancerous tumors is also a problem to be dealt with in stem cells. Considering this, there is one exception: umbilical cord stem cells are generally not known to turn malignant.1

Here is a short list of treatments that are in development that would use stem cells:

  • Macular Degeneration—Repair a damaged retina.
  • Spinal Cord Injury/Stroke—Repair nerve tissue.
  • Burns—Repair skin tissue.
  • Congestive Heart Failure—Repair damaged heart tissue.
  • Diabetes—Replace or increase the pancreatic tissue that makes insulin.
  • Arthritis—Repair damaged cartilage.
  • Autoimmune diseases (Lupus, Multiple Sclerosis) —Destroy the immune system that is attacking its own body and replace or “reset” it with a new immune system derived from one’s own stem cells.
  • Leukemias—Destroy the cancerous blood cells and replace them with new stem cell derived blood cells.
  • New organs—Replace diseased, damaged, or cancer-ridden organs, such as the kidney, liver, or pancreas, with organs derived from the patient’s own stem cells, grown in a lab, and transplanted surgically, without the need of anti-rejection drugs.

As you can see, there is a very long list of diseases and ailments that may result in effective treatments with stem cells. I am very optimistic that within a decade, remedies for many of these ailments will be commonly available. However, learning how to make stem cells that are expertly specialized into specific tissue types, learning how to turn stems cells on and then turning them off at the necessary time (once the job is finished), and learning how to “teach” the stem cells where and how to make repairs will take time.

I am not the only one who is excited about the possibilities. That is why hundreds of stem cell clinics have sprung up across the country, trying to get in on the excitement. But do the claims of any of these clinics align with reality? Which ones are legitimate? I know that there are many clinics offering stem cell treatments for various ailments, so let’s now look at some of the treatments that are available today—ones that have evidence of actually helping, as well as realistic expectations. Let’s also look at some of the possible complications, to help us make informed decisions.

First, the risks and complications

  • Introduction of infection—For example, bacteria living on the skin can enter a joint space from a simple injection, resulting in destruction of the joint, even under the cleanest of conditions.
  • Stems cells moving from their introduction site and not going where they are intended or not staying contained to the specific area of treatment—One study involving pigs treated with stem cells injected into areas of a damaged heart after a heart attack showed near complete return of function, but then the new heart tissue kept growing, eventually filling the heart’s pumping chamber, which caused all the pigs to die.
  • Stem cells changing into unexpected or inappropriate cell types—Stem cells used for a facial cosmetic effect have actually turned to bone.2
  • Growth of tumors—There are documented cases of different tumors, including brain and kidney tumors that have developed after patients were treated for stroke and kidney failure using stem cells.
  • Failure to work as expected—There are documented cases of people with macular degeneration, who were treated with stem cells injected into the eye, that have resulted in blindness.
  • Stem cells can’t be withdrawn—Unlike medicines such as a pill or an injection, if something goes wrong, one can’t just withhold the next dose. Once stem cells are introduced, they can’t be taken back. The course that has been set will continue.

The rates of complications are hard to know, since there are no reporting requirements when performed outside of formal clinical investigations.

Next, the known benefits

The FDA (the governmental Food and Drug Administration that is tasked with health safety) has approved stem cell treatments for dozens of blood cancers (leukemias) and blood diseases using umbilical cord stem cells. Though not FDA approved, studies have shown some benefit for using stem cells for orthopedic applications, particularly arthritis of the knees. (Using stem cells for such orthopedic uses, without the need to stimulate them to become cartilage cells beforehand, appears to be the exception to the rule. Remember most stem cells need to be specialized before being used.) That’s it! Aside from this, most other uses for stem cells should only be considered either highly experimental or highly suspect of exaggerated benefits. Could there be other beneficial treatments that are not FDA approved? Perhaps, but it’s important to realize that the claims have often far outpaced the science.

So how is one to know? Here are some things to consider when choosing providers of stem cell treatments, as well as red flags, to tell you if there are better places to go for your health care. (These points are also true for just about any other treatment):

  1. Informed consent—Every medical treatment has risks and benefits. These should be routinely discussed with you beforehand, without you needing to ask. Any practitioner who claims there are no risks, only benefits, either is not sufficiently knowledgeable or is not sufficiently honest!
  2. Can they handle the complications? —Joint injections can sometimes result in infection. These can be severe infections that can potentially destroy the joint. Such complications are not just simply treated with antibiotics, but with surgery. These stem cell treatments are better handled by an orthopedic surgeon or practitioner that has a close relationship with one, if complications should arise. Likewise, treatments involving nerves should be done by neurologists or neurosurgeons.
  3. Is the clinic adequately equipped? —Stem cells need to be handled appropriately. The transport of umbilical stem cells and improper thawing from the supplier can drastically reduce numbers, which may have a great deal to do with determining the success of the procedure. Additionally, these cells may be in a state of “shock,” unless they are appropriately re-cultured after being thawed. This allows them to re-enter a desirable growth phase again.3 This may mean having a specialized lab and microbiologist on staff to properly grow and care for the stem cells, ensuring good quality control. This usually requires a university setting, not just a small clinic or office that has a nurse to thaw the stem cells after receiving them from an overnight delivery service. Glitzy web sites, colorful brochures, and informational dinners are not enough.
  4. Guinea pigs and rats are “experimented on,” people go through “clinical trials.” —Please avoid any practitioner who says they are doing experiments. Clinical trials involving people, which have the oversight of ethics boards, only occur after experiments on animals have shown low risk of harm, and a good chance of success. If a treatment is very effective, the FDA has suggested that as few as 42 participants can demonstrate adequate safety to grant approval. This is not an outrageously high threshold to overcome. Additionally, patients involved in clinical trials are usually only expected to cover minimal costs, if any. Practitioners who “experiment” on people rarely do it for free.4
  5. Realistic claims. —Does your practitioner claim 100 percent success? If so, it is better to run away (if your knees will allow you to) than to simply walk away! Knee treatments, for example, may only delay knee replacements for many people. Some may avoid surgery, but certainly not all. Do not expect a cure. Also, do they make claims well outside of what is commonly recognized? “Cures” claimed for Alzheimers, Parkinson’s, or other ailments that are not FDA approved? I cannot totally exclude the possibility that such treatments may exist at some future time. However, these practitioners should be able to point to (and provide to you) published studies. If there is a miraculous cure, the world should be able to benefit from it, and he or she should be able to patent it, so as to reap the financial benefits of sharing their techniques and discoveries with the rest of the world. By doing so, it is independently tested and verified. Anyone who has a “secret” cure, that they alone possess, should be avoided.
  1. Does it make sense? —By simply injecting stem cells (that have not been induced by a lab into their specialty state such as nerve cells, heart cells, etc.) into the bloodstream to treat things like nerve disorders, for example, does not make sense. Clinical trials of legitimate treatments first specialize the stem cells, then directly apply them to the affected area. For example, specific types of nerve cells are injected directly into specific locations of the brain, and heart cells are injected directly into the scarred tissue of the heart. Remember the indolent adult (the unspecialized stem cell)? You can’t expect to put them on a bus (inject them into a vein), send them into the big city (the body), without instructions on what to do (leaving them unspecialized), not knowing where to go (to somehow find the diseased part of the body) and then magically expect success.
  2. The hard sell. —Are you being told that or are you made to feel that you are “missing out” if you decline? Do the clinic advertisements have testimonial bylines, something to the effect of “Individual results may vary, and testimonials are not claimed to represent typical results and are not intended to represent or guarantee that anyone will achieve the same or similar results…”? As the old adage goes, if it’s too good to be true (especially if they actually tell you so), then it probably is. In these cases, consider the claims to be most likely somewhat exaggerated, and also consider working with someone who can give a more honest set of expectations.

I pray that God may grant you wisdom: If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him –Jas 1:5.
