Msaada Wangu na Mkombozi Wangu

Zaburi 40:1 Nilimngoja BWANA kwa saburi; naye akaniinama, akasikia kilio changu. 2 Akanipandisha kutoka katika shimo la kutisha, kutoka katika matope yenye tope zito, akaweka miguu yangu juu ya mwamba, na kuimarisha hatua zangu. 3 Naye akatia wimbo mpya kinywani mwangu, sifa kwa Mungu wetu; wengi wataona, wataogopa, na kumtumaini BWANA. 4 Heri mtu yule anayemfanya BWANA kuwa tumaini lake, wala hawaelekei kwa wenye kiburi, wala kwa wale wanaogeukia uongo. 5 Ee BWANA, Mungu wangu, matendo yako ya ajabu uliyoyafanya ni mengi, na mawazo yako kwetu; hayawezi kuhesabiwa mbele zako kwa mpangilio. Ningetaka kuyatangaza na kuyasema, ni mengi kuliko yanavyoweza kuhesabiwa. 6 Dhabihu na sadaka hukuzitaka; masikio yangu umeyafungua; sadaka ya kuteketezwa na sadaka ya dhambi hukuzitaka. 7 Ndipo nikasema, Tazama, nimekuja; katika gombo la kitabu imeandikwa kunihusu, 8 Napendezwa kuyafanya mapenzi yako, Ee Mungu wangu; naam, sheria yako imo moyoni mwangu. 9 Nimetangaza haki katika kusanyiko kubwa; tazama, sijazuia midomo yangu, Ee BWANA, wewe wajua. 10 Sikuificha haki yako moyoni mwangu; nimetangaza uaminifu wako na wokovu wako; sikuficha fadhili zako na ukweli wako mbele ya kusanyiko kubwa. 11 Ee BWANA, usinizuilie rehema zako; fadhili zako na ukweli wako na vinilinde daima. 12 Maovu yasiyohesabika yamenizunguka; maovu yangu yamenishika, hata nisiweze kutazama juu; ni mengi kuliko nywele za kichwa changu; kwa hiyo moyo wangu umedhoofika. 13 Ee BWANA, upendezwe kuniokoa; Ee BWANA, fanya haraka kunisaidia. 14 Waaibishwe na kufadhaika pamoja wale wanaoitafuta nafsi yangu ili kuiangamiza; warudishwe nyuma na kuaibishwa wale wanaonitakia mabaya. 15 Wale wanaoniambia, Aha, aha, na waachwe ukiwa kuwa thawabu ya aibu yao. 16 Wote wanaokutafuta na wafurahi na kushangilia ndani yako; wale wanaoupenda wokovu wako na waseme daima, BWANA na atukuzwe. 17 Lakini mimi ni maskini na mhitaji; hata hivyo Bwana ananikumbuka; wewe ndiwe msaada wangu na mkombozi wangu; usikawie, Ee Mungu wangu.

Asubuhi yenye utukufu inafunguka mbele yangu, kamilifu na yenye amani, bila kutiwa doa na kushindwa. Anga ni safi na la samawati. Upeo wa macho una rangi ya waridi hafifu, iliyoboreshwa na ukungu mwembamba. Vilima na miti ya mbali vimefunikwa na vivuli vya samawati iliyofifia katika ubaridi wa asubuhi wenye ukungu. Asubuhi inavuma kwa sauti za ndege wakipiga miluzi, wakilia na kuimba kwa sauti fupi. Nyasi zinang'aa kwa mamilioni ya matone ya umande yanayometameta katika mwanga wa asubuhi. Upeo wa waridi juu ya vilima vya mbali vilivyofifia hatua kwa hatua hubadilika na kuwa duara la chungwa linalong'aa, ambalo mwangaza wake unaongezeka zaidi na zaidi.

Ninasimama nikimstaajabia Mungu. Moyo wangu unafurahi sana kwa uzuri uliotandazwa mbele yangu. Pia ninafurahi sana kwa yale ambayo Mungu ametenda maishani mwangu, na kwa uzuri aliouumba kutokana na majivu.

Nilimngoja Bwana kwa saburi; naye akaniinama, akasikia kilio changu. Akanipandisha kutoka katika shimo la kutisha, kutoka katika matope yenye tope zito, akaweka miguu yangu juu ya mwamba, na kuimarisha hatua zangu. Mungu amenipandisha kutoka katika shimo la kukata tamaa na kuvunjika moyo. Ameweka miguu yangu juu ya Mwamba, Yesu Kristo, na kuimarisha hatua zangu. Anajua mipango aliyonayo kwa ajili yangu. Mawazo yake na njia zake ni za juu zaidi kuliko zangu.

Akatia wimbo mpya kinywani mwangu, sifa kwa Mungu wetu; wengi wataona, wataogopa, na kumtumaini Bwana. Ninatamani Mungu atukuzwe kupitia kazi ambayo ametenda na anayoendelea kuitenda maishani mwangu. Ee Bwana, matendo yako ya ajabu uliyoyafanya ni mengi, na mawazo yako kwetu; hayawezi kuhesabiwa mbele zako kwa mpangilio. Ningetaka kuyatangaza na kuyasema, ni mengi kuliko yanavyoweza kuhesabiwa.

Napendezwa kuyafanya mapenzi yako, Ee Mungu; naam, sheria yako imo moyoni mwangu. Kwa kweli napendezwa kuyafanya mapenzi ya Mungu; kumpenda kwa moyo wangu wote, nafsi yangu yote, nguvu zangu zote, na akili yangu yote; kuzitii amri zake kutoka moyoni mwangu.

Sikuificha haki yako moyoni mwangu; nimetangaza uaminifu wako na wokovu wako; sikuficha fadhili zako na ukweli wako mbele ya kusanyiko kubwa. Ni baraka kubwa kuwa na mazungumzo ya kina na yenye kujenga pamoja na ndugu na dada zangu katika Bwana, na kushirikishana yale ambayo Bwana anatenda maishani mwetu. Hilo hunitia nguvu sana katika imani yangu.

Ee Bwana, usinizuilie rehema zako; fadhili zako na ukweli wako na vinilinde daima. Majaribu na mitihani migumu ni mambo halisi sana maishani; jitihada za kuilinda moyo wangu kwa bidii, mapambano dhidi ya kiburi cha ukaidi, na msukumo wa kutamka maneno ya haraka-haraka kwa kufadhaika. Ee Bwana, upendezwe kuniokoa; Ee Bwana, fanya haraka kunisaidia. Waaibishwe na kufadhaika pamoja wale wanaoitafuta nafsi yangu ili kuiangamiza; warudishwe nyuma na kuaibishwa wale wanaonitakia mabaya.

Jua limechomoza juu ya vilima vya mbali na sasa eneo lote la mashambani linang'aa kwa utukufu. Ukungu umetoweka ndani ya misitu, na vilima na miti ya mbali iliyokuwa na rangi hafifu ya samawati imebadili mavazi yake na kuwa vivuli vya kijani vilivyochangamka, vilivyochanganyika na vidokezo vya rangi nyekundu na kahawia. Matone ya umande yanayometameta yanang'aa kwa kuvutia katika mwanga mkali wa jua.

Wale wanaokutafuta na wafurahi na kushangilia ndani yako; wale wanaoupenda wokovu wako na waseme daima, Bwana na atukuzwe. Mimi ni maskini na mhitaji; hata hivyo Bwana ananikumbuka; wewe ndiwe msaada wangu na mkombozi wangu; usikawie, Ee Mungu wangu.

If marriage is a covenant, what is the significance of covenant relationship? What makes it a covenant relationship, and how does this differ from any other relationship? These are answers that we must pursue if we are to understand the permanence of marriage and if we are to successfully navigate the rocky shores of a troubled marriage.

Covenant in our society has become archaic. The cultural revolution of the sixties has made divorce culturally acceptable, and life-long fidelity in marriage has become the exception rather than the rule. Unfortunately, this blight has infected most mainstream churches and is currently invading our Anabaptist churches.

Covenant is God’s idea. He is the primary covenant maker. His holy name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word. The Hebrew origin of “Jehovah” is yeh-ho-vaw. This word combines two Hebrew verbs of being. A most literal translation for the name yeh-ho-vaw would be (is is) or as God said to Moses “I am that I am.”

God’s name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word, that he cannot lie, and that He is true to His character. James states it this way: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning –Jas 1:17.

What makes a covenant?

Careful investigation of scripture will reveal that there are three key elements in the establishment of a covenant.

  • Words
  • Witnesses
  • That which ratifies the covenant

Words

Words define the terms and conditions of a covenant. It is very important that the terms and conditions of the covenant be clearly defined and understood by both parties involved. When God made covenant with Abraham, He spake and said, And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee –Gen 17:7.

When God made covenant with the nation of Israel at Mt Sinai, He gave them the Law which was the terms and conditions of the Mosaic covenant.

In our Bibles today we have the Old and the New Testament. This refers to the Old and the New Covenant. In the New Testament we have the teachings of Jesus and His Apostles which supersede the Old Testament law. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said repeatedly, “You have heard that it hath been said, but I say unto you.”

The Hebrew writer had this to say about the New Covenant: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises –Heb 8:6.

On our wedding day we use words with precise meaning to establish a covenant that is binding “…till death do us part.” Wedding vows may contain some variation but should always include a commitment to a mutually loving relationship that is binding for life, and thus irrevocable.

Witnesses

Another important part of a covenant is the witnesses. Witnesses provide validation and accountability to the vows that have been made. This is especially true of a covenant made between two people.

When Joshua re-established the covenant with Israel upon entering the land of Canaan, he challenged them: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses –Jos 24:22. What they were saying was that, “We will hold one another accountable for the commitments that we are making today.”

Regarding the New Covenant, we have the testimony of the Apostle John where he says: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one –1Joh 5:7-8. Here John is saying that in this New Covenant between God and man there are three witnesses in heaven and three witnesses in earth, and these witnesses all agree.

In the establishment of a marriage covenant the wedding guests are the witnesses. Every guest becomes a witness of the vows that are made. By their presence and blessing, they validate the marriage and become personally responsible to ensure that this marriage endures.

This community commitment to the permanence of marriage is the moral fabric of our society and our churches. When a society becomes negligent in enforcing the permanence of marriage, chaos and confusion ensue. We see this in the society around us. Unfortunately, we are also seeing an increasing number of marriage breakups within our Anabaptist churches.

That which ratifies the covenant

The final step in establishing a covenant is that which ratifies and renders binding and effective the terms of the covenant. Historically there have been a variety of methods of binding a covenant. Ancient Bedouins had a practice of using salt to bind a covenant. Each party would give to the other a measure of salt. The salt was mixed with their respective stores of salt making it impossible to ever separate “my salt” from “your salt.” This symbolized the immutability of this treaty.

Then there was the practice of berith. Berith is a Hebrew word that means “to cut.” In ancient Israel a covenant was ratified by “cutting a covenant.” This practice is clearly illustrated in Genesis 15 where God ratified His covenant with Abraham. Abraham asked God, …Lord GOD, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it? –Gen 15:8. God’s response to Abraham’s plea was …Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon –Gen 15:9. Abraham took these animals and divided them in the midst and lay them out as a sacrifice to God. God reaffirmed His covenant with Abraham (with words), and then in verse 17, we have this mysterious event: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces –Gen 15:17. This was “berith” or the “cutting of the covenant.” This ceremony ratified and rendered binding the terms and conditions of the covenant. After this event, we have no record that Abraham ever questioned or doubted the promise of God, although he did take it into his own hands to bring that promise to fruition.

When God made covenant with Israel at Mt Sinai, …Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you concerning all these words –Exo 24:8. This blood rendered binding and effective the terms and conditions set forth in the law—this was the Old Covenant.

When God made covenant with you and I at Mt Calvary, the blood of Jesus became the ratifying evidence or the binding token of His New Covenant with us. When we partake of the communion, we are commemorating the covenant that we have with God through Christ.

What ratifies the marriage covenant? As we have already seen, in a marriage we have words (the vows), and we have witnesses (the guests). Does this complete the marriage? No. The marriage is not complete until there is a coming together in physical intimacy. This completes or, as we sometimes say, consummates the marriage covenant. This is that which ratifies and renders binding and permanent the terms and conditions of the marriage covenant. Early on in Scripture we have example of this. And Adam knew Eve his wife… Gen 4:1. Then later on we see another example, And Isaac brought her [Rebekah] into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her… –Gen 24:67. Physical oneness belongs to covenant. This is why such a relationship outside of marriage is sin. Fornication or adultery takes that which God has ordained to be inextricably linked to marriage and adulterates the covenant.

When a married couple comes together in physical union they are commemorating and celebrating their marriage covenant. This is the start of them establishing a biblical “one flesh” reality. From this blessed union new life emerges in the form of precious “little ones” and of hearts that are renewed by the power of love.

When we partake of the bread and the wine of communion we are commemorating and celebrating our covenant relationship with Christ. From this blessed oneness new life emerges in the form of hearts that are renewed by the power of love. This is the strength of covenant.

Where these three elements exist—vows, witnesses, and that which ratifies—we have a covenant relationship. How does a covenant relationship differ from any other relationship?

A commitment to fidelity

Some of the most noble words that human lips can utter are “I promise to love you till death do us part.” On our wedding day these words are easy to utter, and we may be most sincere when we speak them. The fact is that no one can possibly know what those words may cost in the course of a lifetime.

Love is a choice and must become established and endure as an every day walk of life. We must choose to direct our affection toward the one of our covenant love and away from the enticements of others. Many, many marriages are destroyed through infidelity.

God has designed marriage to be powerfully bonding. The spiritual, emotional, and physical attachment of marriage creates an inseparable bond. In Genesis we read Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh –Gen 2:24. The word cleave in this verse denotes “being welded or glued together in such a way as to be inseparable.”

To break the marriage bond through infidelity causes rending and wounding to both parties. Satan, the great deceiver, would have us to believe that being unfaithful to our spouse will somehow benefit us. This is a huge lie.

A commitment to faithfulness

God demonstrated covenant faithfulness in his dealings with His Old Testament bride—the nation of Israel. She was not true to her covenant vows. She turned from the worship of Jehovah, and she bowed her knee to pagan altars. Despite her unfaithfulness, God continued to pursue her and call her back unto himself. Israel’s unfaithfulness did not alter God’s faithfulness. This is the strength of covenant love. Covenant love is not contingent upon the actions of the other party. Covenant love persists even though it is not reciprocated. This is a kingdom concept. Paul taught, Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head –Rom 12:20. Would this principle not most aptly apply to a broken marriage?

The strength of covenant can only be fully realized through an understanding of the divine love of God for us. Our salvation is dependent upon God’s perfect love for us. He continues to love us even though our love for Him is sometimes flawed. His unfailing love continues to draw us back unto himself. The strength of covenant in marriage is found in seeking to emulate this divine love. This divine love will not be found in romance novels or other books on marriage. This divine love can only be found in an intimate relationship with “The Source” of undying love.

Jika pernikahan adalah sebuah perjanjian, apa makna hubungan perjanjian? Apa yang menjadikannya hubungan perjanjian, dan apa bedanya dengan hubungan lainnya? Inilah pertanyaan-pertanyaan yang harus kita jawab jika kita ingin memahami kelanggengan pernikahan dan berhasil mengarungi masa-masa sulit dalam pernikahan yang bermasalah.

Perjanjian telah menjadi sesuatu yang kuno dalam masyarakat kita. Revolusi budaya tahun enam puluhan membuat perceraian dapat diterima secara budaya, dan kesetiaan seumur hidup dalam pernikahan kini menjadi pengecualian, bukan lagi kebiasaan. Sayangnya, keadaan buruk ini telah menjangkiti sebagian besar gereja arus utama dan kini merambah gereja-gereja Anabaptis kita.

Perjanjian adalah gagasan Allah. Dialah pembuat perjanjian yang utama. Nama-Nya yang kudus, “Jehovah”, menunjukkan bahwa Allah selalu setia pada firman-Nya. Asal kata Ibrani “Jehovah” adalah yeh-ho-vaw. Kata ini menggabungkan dua kata kerja Ibrani yang menyatakan keberadaan. Terjemahan yang paling harfiah dari nama yeh-ho-vaw adalah (adalah adalah), atau seperti yang Allah katakan kepada Musa, “Aku adalah Aku.”

Nama Allah, “Jehovah”, menunjukkan bahwa Allah selalu setia pada firman-Nya, bahwa Dia tidak dapat berdusta, dan bahwa Dia setia pada karakter-Nya. Yakobus menyatakannya demikian: Setiap pemberian yang baik dan setiap anugerah yang sempurna datang dari atas, turun dari Bapa segala terang, yang pada-Nya tidak ada perubahan atau bayangan karena pergeseran –Yak 1:17.

Apa yang membentuk suatu perjanjian?

Penyelidikan saksama terhadap Kitab Suci akan menunjukkan bahwa ada tiga unsur utama dalam pembentukan suatu perjanjian.

  • Kata-kata
  • Saksi-saksi
  • Hal yang mengesahkan perjanjian

Kata-kata

Kata-kata menetapkan syarat dan ketentuan suatu perjanjian. Sangat penting agar syarat dan ketentuan perjanjian itu dijelaskan dengan gamblang dan dipahami oleh kedua belah pihak yang terlibat. Ketika Allah mengadakan perjanjian dengan Abraham, Dia berfirman, Aku akan mengadakan perjanjian antara Aku dan engkau serta keturunanmu turun-temurun, menjadi perjanjian yang kekal, supaya Aku menjadi Allahmu dan Allah keturunanmu –Kej 17:7.

Ketika Allah mengadakan perjanjian dengan bangsa Israel di Gunung Sinai, Dia memberi mereka Hukum Taurat, yang memuat syarat dan ketentuan perjanjian Musa.

Dalam Alkitab kita sekarang terdapat Perjanjian Lama dan Perjanjian Baru. Ini merujuk pada Perjanjian Lama dan Perjanjian Baru. Dalam Perjanjian Baru terdapat ajaran Yesus dan para rasul-Nya, yang menggantikan hukum Perjanjian Lama. Dalam Khotbah di Bukit, Yesus berulang kali berkata, “Kamu telah mendengar bahwa telah dikatakan, tetapi Aku berkata kepadamu.”

Penulis Ibrani berkata tentang Perjanjian Baru: Tetapi sekarang Ia telah memperoleh pelayanan yang jauh lebih mulia, karena Ia juga menjadi pengantara perjanjian yang lebih baik, yang didasarkan pada janji-janji yang lebih baik –Ibr 8:6.

Pada hari pernikahan, kita menggunakan kata-kata yang maknanya tepat untuk menetapkan suatu perjanjian yang mengikat “…sampai maut memisahkan kita.” Sumpah pernikahan dapat memiliki variasi, tetapi harus selalu mencakup komitmen untuk menjalin hubungan saling mengasihi yang mengikat seumur hidup, dan karena itu tidak dapat dibatalkan.

Saksi-saksi

Bagian penting lainnya dari suatu perjanjian adalah para saksi. Para saksi memberikan pengesahan dan akuntabilitas atas sumpah yang telah diucapkan. Hal ini terutama berlaku bagi perjanjian antara dua orang.

Ketika Yosua memperbarui perjanjian dengan Israel setelah memasuki tanah Kanaan, ia menantang mereka: Yosua berkata kepada bangsa itu, “Kamu menjadi saksi terhadap dirimu sendiri bahwa kamu telah memilih TUHAN untuk melayani-Nya.” Mereka menjawab, “Kami adalah saksi” –Yos 24:22. Yang mereka katakan adalah, “Kami akan saling meminta pertanggungjawaban atas komitmen yang kami buat hari ini.”

Mengenai Perjanjian Baru, kita memiliki kesaksian Rasul Yohanes yang berkata: Sebab ada tiga yang memberi kesaksian di surga: Bapa, Firman, dan Roh Kudus; dan ketiganya adalah satu. Dan ada tiga yang memberi kesaksian di bumi: Roh, air, dan darah; dan ketiganya sependapat –1Yoh 5:7-8. Di sini Yohanes mengatakan bahwa dalam Perjanjian Baru antara Allah dan manusia ini ada tiga saksi di surga dan tiga saksi di bumi, dan semua saksi itu sependapat.

Dalam pembentukan perjanjian pernikahan, para tamu pernikahan adalah saksinya. Setiap tamu menjadi saksi atas sumpah yang diucapkan. Dengan kehadiran dan berkat mereka, mereka mengesahkan pernikahan itu dan menjadi bertanggung jawab secara pribadi untuk memastikan pernikahan ini bertahan.

Komitmen masyarakat terhadap kelanggengan pernikahan ini merupakan jalinan moral masyarakat dan gereja kita. Ketika suatu masyarakat lalai menegakkan kelanggengan pernikahan, kekacauan dan kebingungan pun terjadi. Kita melihat hal ini dalam masyarakat di sekitar kita. Sayangnya, kita juga menyaksikan semakin banyak pernikahan yang berakhir di gereja-gereja Anabaptis kita.

Hal yang mengesahkan perjanjian

Langkah terakhir dalam pembentukan suatu perjanjian adalah hal yang mengesahkan dan membuat syarat-syarat perjanjian itu mengikat serta berlaku. Sepanjang sejarah, ada berbagai cara untuk mengikat suatu perjanjian. Orang Badui kuno memiliki kebiasaan menggunakan garam untuk mengikat perjanjian. Masing-masing pihak memberikan sejumlah garam kepada pihak lainnya. Garam itu dicampurkan dengan persediaan garam masing-masing sehingga mustahil untuk memisahkan “garamku” dari “garammu.” Ini melambangkan ketakterubahan perjanjian tersebut.

Lalu ada praktik berith. Berith adalah kata Ibrani yang berarti “memotong.” Di Israel kuno, suatu perjanjian disahkan dengan “memotong perjanjian.” Praktik ini digambarkan dengan jelas dalam Kejadian 15, ketika Allah mengesahkan perjanjian-Nya dengan Abraham. Abraham bertanya kepada Allah, …Ya Tuhan ALLAH, dari manakah aku tahu bahwa aku akan memilikinya? –Kej 15:8. Allah menjawab permohonan Abraham dengan berkata, …Ambillah bagi-Ku seekor lembu betina berumur tiga tahun, seekor kambing betina berumur tiga tahun, seekor domba jantan berumur tiga tahun, seekor burung tekukur, dan seekor anak burung merpati –Kej 15:9. Abraham mengambil hewan-hewan itu, membelahnya di tengah, lalu membaringkannya sebagai persembahan kepada Allah. Allah meneguhkan kembali perjanjian-Nya dengan Abraham (dengan kata-kata), lalu pada ayat 17 terjadi peristiwa misterius ini: Ketika matahari terbenam dan hari menjadi gelap, tampaklah sebuah perapian yang berasap dan obor yang menyala lewat di antara potongan-potongan itu –Kej 15:17. Inilah “berith” atau “pemotongan perjanjian.” Upacara ini mengesahkan dan menjadikan syarat-syarat perjanjian itu mengikat. Setelah peristiwa ini, tidak ada catatan bahwa Abraham pernah mempertanyakan atau meragukan janji Allah, meskipun ia memang mengambil tindakan sendiri untuk mewujudkan janji itu.

Ketika Allah mengadakan perjanjian dengan Israel di Gunung Sinai, …Musa mengambil darah itu dan memercikkannya kepada bangsa itu, lalu berkata, “Inilah darah perjanjian yang diadakan TUHAN dengan kamu berdasarkan segala firman ini” –Kel 24:8. Darah ini membuat syarat dan ketentuan yang ditetapkan dalam hukum Taurat mengikat dan berlaku—itulah Perjanjian Lama.

Ketika Allah mengadakan perjanjian dengan engkau dan aku di Gunung Kalvari, darah Yesus menjadi bukti pengesahan atau tanda pengikat Perjanjian Baru-Nya dengan kita. Ketika kita mengambil bagian dalam perjamuan kudus, kita memperingati perjanjian yang kita miliki dengan Allah melalui Kristus.

Apa yang mengesahkan perjanjian pernikahan? Seperti yang telah kita lihat, dalam pernikahan terdapat kata-kata (sumpah) dan saksi-saksi (para tamu). Apakah itu sudah melengkapi pernikahan? Tidak. Pernikahan belum lengkap sampai terjadi penyatuan dalam keintiman fisik. Hal ini melengkapi atau, seperti yang kadang kita katakan, menyempurnakan perjanjian pernikahan. Inilah yang mengesahkan dan membuat syarat-syarat perjanjian pernikahan mengikat dan permanen. Sejak awal Kitab Suci kita menemukan contoh tentang hal ini. Adam bersetubuh dengan Hawa, istrinya… Kej 4:1. Kemudian kita melihat contoh lain, Isaak membawa Ribka ke dalam kemah ibunya Sara, lalu mengambil Ribka menjadi istrinya; dan ia mengasihinya… –Kej 24:67. Kesatuan fisik merupakan bagian dari perjanjian. Itulah sebabnya hubungan semacam itu di luar pernikahan adalah dosa. Percabulan atau perzinaan mengambil sesuatu yang telah Allah tetapkan terikat erat pada pernikahan, lalu mencemari perjanjian itu.

Ketika pasangan suami istri bersatu secara fisik, mereka memperingati dan merayakan perjanjian pernikahan mereka. Inilah awal terwujudnya kenyataan “satu daging” yang alkitabiah. Dari penyatuan yang diberkati ini lahirlah kehidupan baru berupa “anak-anak kecil” yang berharga dan hati yang diperbarui oleh kuasa kasih.

Ketika kita mengambil bagian dalam roti dan anggur perjamuan kudus, kita memperingati dan merayakan hubungan perjanjian kita dengan Kristus. Dari kesatuan yang diberkati ini lahirlah kehidupan baru berupa hati yang diperbarui oleh kuasa kasih. Inilah kekuatan perjanjian.

Di mana ketiga unsur ini ada—sumpah, saksi, dan hal yang mengesahkan—di situ terdapat hubungan perjanjian. Apa bedanya hubungan perjanjian dengan hubungan lainnya?

Komitmen untuk setia

Sebagian kata paling luhur yang dapat diucapkan manusia adalah “Aku berjanji akan mengasihimu sampai maut memisahkan kita.” Pada hari pernikahan, kata-kata ini mudah diucapkan, dan ketika mengucapkannya, kita mungkin sungguh-sungguh. Faktanya, tak seorang pun dapat mengetahui apa yang mungkin harus dikorbankan demi kata-kata itu sepanjang hidup.

Kasih adalah pilihan, dan harus diteguhkan serta dijalani setiap hari. Kita harus memilih untuk mengarahkan kasih sayang kita kepada orang yang kita kasihi dalam perjanjian ini dan menjauhi godaan orang lain. Banyak sekali pernikahan hancur karena ketidaksetiaan.

Allah merancang pernikahan agar ikatannya kuat. Keterikatan rohani, emosional, dan fisik dalam pernikahan menciptakan ikatan yang tak terpisahkan. Dalam Kejadian kita membaca Sebab itu seorang laki-laki akan meninggalkan ayah dan ibunya dan bersatu dengan istrinya, sehingga keduanya menjadi satu daging –Kej 2:24. Kata bersatu dalam ayat ini berarti “dilas atau direkatkan sedemikian rupa sehingga tak terpisahkan.”

Memutus ikatan pernikahan melalui ketidaksetiaan menyebabkan luka dan penderitaan bagi kedua belah pihak. Iblis, si penipu besar, ingin membuat kita percaya bahwa ketidaksetiaan kepada pasangan entah bagaimana akan menguntungkan kita. Ini adalah kebohongan besar.

Komitmen untuk tetap setia

Allah menunjukkan kesetiaan-Nya pada perjanjian dalam hubungan-Nya dengan mempelai perempuan-Nya pada zaman Perjanjian Lama—bangsa Israel. Israel tidak setia pada sumpah perjanjiannya. Ia berpaling dari penyembahan kepada Jehovah dan sujud di hadapan mezbah-mezbah kafir. Meskipun Israel tidak setia, Allah terus mengejarnya dan memanggilnya kembali kepada diri-Nya. Ketidaksetiaan Israel tidak mengubah kesetiaan Allah. Inilah kekuatan kasih perjanjian. Kasih perjanjian tidak bergantung pada tindakan pihak yang lain. Kasih perjanjian tetap bertahan meskipun tidak dibalas. Ini adalah prinsip Kerajaan Allah. Paulus mengajarkan, Jika musuhmu lapar, berilah dia makan; jika ia haus, berilah dia minum; sebab dengan berbuat demikian engkau akan menumpukkan bara api di atas kepalanya –Rm 12:20. Bukankah prinsip ini sangat tepat diterapkan pada pernikahan yang retak?

Kekuatan perjanjian hanya dapat sepenuhnya dialami melalui pemahaman akan kasih ilahi Allah bagi kita. Keselamatan kita bergantung pada kasih Allah yang sempurna bagi kita. Dia terus mengasihi kita meskipun kasih kita kepada-Nya terkadang tidak sempurna. Kasih-Nya yang tak pernah gagal terus menarik kita kembali kepada diri-Nya. Kekuatan perjanjian dalam pernikahan ditemukan dalam upaya meneladani kasih ilahi ini. Kasih ilahi ini tidak akan ditemukan dalam novel-novel romantis atau buku-buku lain tentang pernikahan. Kasih ilahi ini hanya dapat ditemukan dalam hubungan akrab dengan “Sumber” kasih yang tak pernah mati.

If we step back and look at our own life, can we honestly say that we trust in the Lord with all our heart? I often think of my children—they trust in me with all their hearts; there is no fear within them; they do not worry. My prayer is that I can trust in my Heavenly Father in the same way.

Here in Haiti a lot of people are driven by fear. They fear the uncertainty of tomorrow. They fear whether they will find food, work, and clothing. It is the opposite of trusting in God. In the western culture, people don’t fear those things. Food and clothing are easy to find, jobs are plentiful, and medical assistance is just one 911 call away.

The poor people here in Haiti say that it would be easier to trust God if they were in America, but is that truly the case? While very few in America fear whether they will have enough to eat, many fear whether they will be accepted by other people. There are some who may fear having enough money to live, but there are many who fear death. Whatever our fear is, trusting in God is our answer.

Let’s look at the life of David. David was a young boy. When his older brothers went to battle, young David went out to feed his father’s sheep. On the battlefield, there was a giant with the Philistine army named Goliath. He challenged the Israelites by saying that if one man would come out and fight him, the victor’s army would rule the other side. In 1 Samuel 17:10-11 we read that Goliath said, …I defy the armies of Israel this day; give me a man, that we may fight together. When Saul and all Israel heard those words of the Philistine, they were dismayed, and greatly afraid.

Later on, we read that Jesse, David’s father, sent him to the place of battle to take some food to his older brothers. David arrived at the place of battle, and he heard Goliath speaking these same words. When David saw that the men of Israel were all afraid, he did not understand. Why were God’s people afraid of this uncircumcised Philistine?

Even though David was young, he was no amateur when it came to putting his trust in God. While he was watching his father’s sheep, most likely he talked much with God, asking Him to help guard the sheep. One day a bear came out to attack the sheep, and David killed the bear. Another day a lion came out to eat some sheep. Again, the God-trusting, fearless youth faced the threat and killed the lion. Now, facing a seemingly greater threat, David simply asks, …who is this uncircumcised Philistine, that he should defy the armies of the living God? –1Sa 17:26. David went to King Saul and said, I …will go and fight with this Philistine –1Sa 17:32. Once more putting his trust in his God, David took five smooth stones, ran out to meet the giant, and killed him. Upon seeing this sudden turn of events, the people marveled.

According to Psalm 20:7, when we put our trust in horses and chariots, then it is not in the Lord our God. In Matthew 21:21, the Bible says that with faith we can move mountains. Here in Haiti I have found myself in tough situations where God is my only option. When I have been forced to put my trust in God, I have discovered that He still works miracles. Just like David with the lion, the bear, and the giant, we too can learn that trusting God with our whole heart is the best way and not just a last resort. When we trust in the Lord first, we show the world something amazing—that this God we serve is alive, and that He is real.

Here in Haiti there was a man living in a shack up in the mountains with his wife and three young children. But there was a problem—he was deathly ill. One day he heard about a missionary who often traveled through the mountains. I received a message from him stating that he was almost dead and that he needed me to come and pray for him. I quickly went up to his home. I was amazed at his condition. His weight was probably not much more than 70 pounds. His wife told me that he had been in bed for over a year. He couldn’t talk, he only whispered with deep agonizing breaths. We spent quite a while discussing his life, his sin, and his future. He told me that if God would heal him, he would serve him and trust him for the rest of his life. I believed his sincerity, yet I was scared. I began to pray, but it was certainly not a powerful prayer full of faith. Rather it was a weak, humble cry.

As I went home and throughout that night, he was all I could think about. The devil began his attack. I had many confusing, troubling thoughts, “Did you do everything you could have done? What if he dies? Why didn’t you take him to the hospital?” I went to God in prayer. “Oh God,” I prayed, “this man wanted prayer. He didn’t ask for a hospital; he didn’t ask for medication. Please God, heal this man. If he dies, what will I do the next time? O Father, if not for him, please, heal him for me. I need you to, Father.”

I prayed like I had never prayed before, and then, God gave me peace. The next morning, I hurried up the mountain to his home, but he wasn’t there. “No, Lord!” I thought. I rushed around and poked my head in another shack. What I saw overwhelmed me. He was sitting there with a big smile on his face. His wife said that he had been working in the garden that morning. Repeatedly she said, “God healed him! God healed him!” I’ll never forget the feeling I had as I travelled back down that mountain. My heart welled up with joy and thankfulness. “My God is alive! He can do anything and everything! He is my God!” I thanked and praised Him like I never had before. “The lion” that I had faced was dead, and my faith was growing. The devil doesn’t want us to trust God, because when we put our trust in God, He does big things, and our faith grows.

When we put our trust in God there is a risk—what if God doesn’t work? We could be embarrassed, or worse—“What if I step out in faith and God does nothing?” Remember, it is not faith if we know the outcome. Faith is walking in obedience and believing God’s Word when we do not know the outcome. If God wouldn’t have helped David, Goliath surely would have killed him. It was Daniel’s faith that kept him praying to God, even though he knew a lion’s den awaited him. Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego had so much faith in God that they told the king that even if God chose to not deliver them from the fire, that they still would …not serve thy gods, nor worship the golden image which thou hast set up –Dan 3:18. Then there was Gideon and his three hundred men. The list goes on and on of godly men who put their life on the line, proving that their God was alive.

When we step out in faith, trusting our God, something always happens (sometimes now, sometimes later; sometimes in a way that makes sense, sometimes in a way that seems to make no earthly sense). Yet God does work, and our faith grows. When we truly believe in God, we will trust him. Then, sharing the Gospel message with others is much easier. Just like Joshua did not have a fleet of bulldozers on standby at Jericho, so also we do not need a backup plan when we trust in God.

It is true that the great minds and financial backing of many in America and other modern countries have replaced God. There is a way to do most physical things without God. In fact, most people say that trusting in God is not common sense. If you pray over a sick child, it’s not common sense. If you turn down a high paying job because you don’t believe that it’s God’s will, that’s not common sense. If you sell your possessions and give to the poor, it’s not common sense. These people are right—trusting in God is not common sense. Marching around a wall seven times, believing it will fall down, is not common sense. Going into battle with only 300 men against a great army who were like grasshoppers for multitude is not common sense either. Most things done by God-trusting Christians don’t make sense, but they do show the world that they really do put their trust in God, and that is what will turn the world upside down again, today.

I remember one day very well. I was away from home when I received a phone call from my wife. She told me to come home quickly—it was an emergency! Our two-year-old son had been stung by bees. I rushed home to see the neighborhood in chaos. People where running around everywhere. I found my wife and son at the neighbor’s house, a local pastor. My son lay in the arms of my wife who told me he had been stung several hundred times. The pastor looked at me quite gravely, telling me that if I didn’t get this boy to a hospital right away, he would surely die. I remember thinking one thing—God can heal! I picked up my son and took him across the street to our house, and I prayed. It didn’t take long before he began to recover—by the next day he was back out playing.

Many people here in Haiti take their sick to the witch doctor, and he heals them. It’s just what happens. How much more can our God do! Please don’t misunderstand me. I’m not saying we shouldn’t go to the medical doctor or to the hospital; rather, I’m trying to emphasize that our trust should be in God.

Years ago, I decided to take up a part-time job selling knives. I was to take these knives and travel from home to home. I didn’t have an interest in knives but was just trying to make some extra money. I was a terrible knife salesman. Everywhere I went everyone said no.

One day the boss took me into his office where he told me that he had noticed I wasn’t selling any knives and realized he had forgotten to show me how the knives worked. So, we sat there in his office as he talked about each knife. He had a small pile of kitchen utensils of another brand, which were known for their quality, that he used for a comparison. First, he held up a small piece of leather and asked me to cut it in half with one of the “other” knives. I sawed through the piece of leather with some ease. Then he instructed me to use one of his knives and do the same thing. The new knife sliced through the leather as if it wasn’t even there! I was truly amazed. He then picked up a penny and told me to cut it in half using the “other” scissors. I tried but failed; they simply would not cut it. He then told me to do the same using his scissors. It easily cut through the penny, and again I was amazed at the product. He told me that I now knew that these knives were the best and from now on I should be able to sell them. He was right. I began selling knives everywhere I went! I even remember walking into a poorly kept trailer home without much hope that they would buy. Surprisingly, they bought over $3,000 worth of knives.

The reason I began to make sales is obvious—I believed in my product. Likewise, if we put our trust in God, we will have confidence. In a day when most proclaiming Christians are ashamed of God and ashamed to stand up for truth, we can be a bright and shining light. We can be a people who go out into the world and into our communities with a Gospel that we truly believe in! As we do, the world will see it and respond. Many are seeking; they are looking for answers. When someone asks us a question about why we do the things we do or wear what we wear, what is our reply? Do we reply with confidence? Do we have a ready Bible verse? Or do we get embarrassed and desire a hole to climb into? If the world could see that we are confident in our God, and that we obey him with enthusiasm, it would be a powerful testimony.

I remember traveling through the airport with a small group. As we were standing in line, I overheard a lady ask one of the single sisters in our group why she wore that “thing” on her head. I was excited to listen unnoticed, and I rejoiced as I heard her response. “Have you ever read 1 Corinthians 11? There it instructs us that women should cover their heads. It’s a sign of submission.” The woman was shocked at her answer, saying she never heard that before, and that her father was a pastor. They continued to have a very interesting conversation that ended with that lady desiring to go home and study her Bible.

A tract can do a lot of good; so likewise, a powerful sermon or a printed article, but someone putting all his trust in God is what this world is looking for! They want to “see something that works,” and why not? Our God wants to use us to show Himself strong. Surely each one of us wants to be used by God. We can. Each one of us can. The answer is to trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding –Pro 3:5.

Se facciamo un passo indietro e guardiamo alla nostra vita, possiamo dire onestamente di confidare nel Signore con tutto il cuore? Penso spesso ai miei figli: confidano in me con tutto il cuore; non hanno paura, non si preoccupano. La mia preghiera è di riuscire a confidare nel mio Padre celeste allo stesso modo.

Qui ad Haiti molte persone sono spinte dalla paura. Temono l’incertezza del domani. Temono di non riuscire a trovare cibo, lavoro e vestiti. È l’opposto del confidare in Dio. Nella cultura occidentale, le persone non temono queste cose. È facile trovare cibo e vestiti, i posti di lavoro abbondano e basta una chiamata al 911 per ricevere assistenza medica.

I poveri qui ad Haiti dicono che sarebbe più facile confidare in Dio se si trovassero in America, ma è davvero così? Sebbene in America pochissimi temano di non avere abbastanza da mangiare, molti temono di non essere accettati dagli altri. Alcuni possono temere di non avere abbastanza denaro per vivere, ma molti hanno paura della morte. Qualunque sia la nostra paura, confidare in Dio è la risposta.

Consideriamo la vita di Davide. Davide era un ragazzo. Quando i suoi fratelli maggiori andarono in battaglia, il giovane Davide uscì a pascolare le pecore di suo padre. Sul campo di battaglia c’era un gigante dell’esercito dei Filistei, di nome Golia. Sfidò gli Israeliti dicendo che, se un uomo fosse uscito a combattere contro di lui, l’esercito del vincitore avrebbe dominato quello dell’altra parte. In 1 Samuele 17:10-11 leggiamo che Golia disse: …Io sfido oggi gli eserciti d’Israele; datemi un uomo e combatteremo insieme. Quando Saul e tutto Israele udirono quelle parole del Filisteo, rimasero sgomenti e furono presi da grande paura.

Più avanti leggiamo che Isai, padre di Davide, lo mandò sul campo di battaglia a portare del cibo ai suoi fratelli maggiori. Davide arrivò sul campo di battaglia e sentì Golia pronunciare quelle stesse parole. Vedendo che tutti gli uomini d’Israele erano impauriti, non riusciva a capire. Perché il popolo di Dio aveva paura di quel Filisteo incirconciso?

Sebbene Davide fosse giovane, non era affatto un principiante quando si trattava di confidare in Dio. Mentre custodiva le pecore di suo padre, probabilmente parlava spesso con Dio, chiedendogli di aiutarlo a proteggere il gregge. Un giorno un orso uscì per attaccare le pecore e Davide uccise l’orso. Un altro giorno un leone uscì per divorare alcune pecore. Ancora una volta, il giovane intrepido che confidava in Dio affrontò la minaccia e uccise il leone. Ora, di fronte a una minaccia apparentemente più grande, Davide si limita a chiedere: …Chi è questo Filisteo incirconciso, che osa sfidare gli eserciti del Dio vivente? –1 Samuele 17:26. Davide andò dal re Saul e disse: Io … andrò a combattere contro questo Filisteo –1 Samuele 17:32. Confidando ancora una volta nel suo Dio, Davide prese cinque pietre lisce, corse incontro al gigante e lo uccise. Vedendo questo improvviso capovolgimento degli eventi, il popolo rimase meravigliato.

Secondo il Salmo 20:7, quando confidiamo nei cavalli e nei carri, allora non confidiamo nel Signore, nostro Dio. In Matteo 21:21 la Bibbia dice che con la fede possiamo spostare le montagne. Qui ad Haiti mi sono trovato in situazioni difficili in cui Dio era la mia unica possibilità. Quando sono stato costretto a confidare in Dio, ho scoperto che egli opera ancora miracoli. Proprio come Davide con il leone, l’orso e il gigante, anche noi possiamo imparare che confidare in Dio con tutto il cuore è la strada migliore, e non soltanto l’ultima risorsa. Quando confidiamo prima di tutto nel Signore, mostriamo al mondo qualcosa di straordinario: che il Dio che serviamo è vivo e reale.

Qui ad Haiti c’era un uomo che viveva con la moglie e i tre figli piccoli in una baracca sui monti. Ma c’era un problema: era gravemente malato, in punto di morte. Un giorno venne a sapere di un missionario che spesso viaggiava attraverso i monti. Ricevetti un messaggio da lui in cui mi diceva che era quasi morto e che aveva bisogno che andassi a pregare per lui. Mi recai in fretta a casa sua. Rimasi stupito dalle sue condizioni. Probabilmente pesava poco più di 70 libbre. Sua moglie mi disse che era a letto da più di un anno. Non riusciva a parlare; sussurrava soltanto, con respiri profondi e angosciosi. Parlammo a lungo della sua vita, del suo peccato e del suo futuro. Mi disse che, se Dio lo avesse guarito, lo avrebbe servito e avrebbe confidato in lui per il resto della vita. Credevo alla sua sincerità, eppure avevo paura. Cominciai a pregare, ma di certo non fu una preghiera potente e piena di fede. Fu piuttosto un debole e umile grido d’aiuto.

Mentre tornavo a casa e per tutta quella notte, non riuscivo a pensare ad altro che a lui. Il diavolo cominciò ad attaccarmi. Mi assalirono molti pensieri confusi e inquietanti: «Hai fatto tutto quello che potevi? E se muore? Perché non l’hai portato in ospedale?». Mi rivolsi a Dio in preghiera. «Oh Dio», pregai, «quest’uomo voleva che pregassi per lui. Non ha chiesto un ospedale; non ha chiesto medicine. Ti prego, Dio, guarisci quest’uomo. Se muore, cosa farò la prossima volta? O Padre, se non per lui, ti prego, guariscilo per me. Ne ho bisogno, Padre».

Pregai come non avevo mai fatto prima, e allora Dio mi diede pace. La mattina seguente mi affrettai a salire il monte fino a casa sua, ma lui non c’era. «No, Signore!» pensai. Corsi di qua e di là e infilai la testa in un’altra baracca. Ciò che vidi mi lasciò senza parole. Era seduto lì con un gran sorriso sul volto. Sua moglie disse che quella mattina aveva lavorato nell’orto. Continuava a ripetere: «Dio lo ha guarito! Dio lo ha guarito!». Non dimenticherò mai quello che provai mentre ridiscendevo quel monte. Il cuore mi traboccava di gioia e gratitudine. «Il mio Dio è vivo! Può fare qualsiasi cosa, ogni cosa! È il mio Dio!». Lo ringraziai e lo lodai come non avevo mai fatto prima. Il «leone» che avevo affrontato era morto e la mia fede cresceva. Il diavolo non vuole che confidiamo in Dio, perché quando riponiamo la nostra fiducia in Dio, egli compie grandi cose e la nostra fede cresce.

Quando confidiamo in Dio corriamo un rischio: e se Dio non intervenisse? Potremmo fare una brutta figura, o peggio: «E se faccio un passo di fede e Dio non fa nulla?». Ricordate: non è fede se conosciamo l’esito. La fede è camminare nell’ubbidienza e credere alla Parola di Dio quando non conosciamo l’esito. Se Dio non avesse aiutato Davide, Golia lo avrebbe certamente ucciso. Fu la fede di Daniele a mantenerlo nella preghiera a Dio, benché sapesse che lo attendeva la fossa dei leoni. Sadrac, Mesac e Abed-Nego avevano tanta fede in Dio che dissero al re che, anche se Dio avesse scelto di non liberarli dal fuoco, loro comunque …non avrebbero servito i tuoi dèi, né adorato la statua d’oro che tu hai fatto innalzare –Daniele 3:18. Poi c’erano Gedeone e i suoi trecento uomini. L’elenco degli uomini pii che misero in gioco la propria vita, dimostrando che il loro Dio era vivo, continua all’infinito.

Quando facciamo un passo di fede e confidiamo nel nostro Dio, succede sempre qualcosa (a volte subito, a volte più tardi; a volte in un modo che ha senso, a volte in un modo che sembra non avere alcun senso umano). Eppure Dio opera, e la nostra fede cresce. Quando crediamo davvero in Dio, confidiamo in lui. Allora è molto più facile condividere con gli altri il messaggio del Vangelo. Proprio come Giosuè non aveva una flotta di bulldozer pronta all’uso a Gerico, così anche noi non abbiamo bisogno di un piano di riserva quando confidiamo in Dio.

È vero che le grandi menti e il sostegno finanziario di molti in America e in altri paesi moderni hanno preso il posto di Dio. Si può fare quasi ogni cosa sul piano materiale senza Dio. Anzi, la maggior parte delle persone dice che confidare in Dio non è buon senso. Se preghi per un bambino malato, non è buon senso. Se rifiuti un lavoro ben pagato perché non credi che sia la volontà di Dio, non è buon senso. Se vendi i tuoi beni e dai il ricavato ai poveri, non è buon senso. Hanno ragione: confidare in Dio non è buon senso. Marciare intorno a un muro sette volte, credendo che crollerà, non è buon senso. Neppure andare in battaglia con soli 300 uomini contro un grande esercito, numeroso come le cavallette, è buon senso. Molte delle cose che fanno i cristiani che confidano in Dio non hanno senso, ma mostrano al mondo che confidano davvero in Dio; ed è questo che oggi rimetterà ancora una volta il mondo sottosopra.

Ricordo molto bene un giorno. Ero lontano da casa quando ricevetti una telefonata da mia moglie. Mi disse di tornare subito a casa: era un’emergenza! Nostro figlio di due anni era stato punto dalle api. Tornai di corsa e trovai il quartiere nel caos. La gente correva dappertutto. Trovai mia moglie e mio figlio a casa del vicino, un pastore del posto. Mio figlio era tra le braccia di mia moglie, che mi disse che era stato punto centinaia di volte. Il pastore mi guardò con aria molto seria e mi disse che, se non avessi portato subito il bambino in ospedale, sarebbe certamente morto. Ricordo che pensai a una sola cosa: Dio può guarire! Presi in braccio mio figlio, lo portai dall’altra parte della strada, a casa nostra, e pregai. Non ci volle molto perché cominciasse a riprendersi; il giorno dopo era già tornato a giocare fuori.

Qui ad Haiti molte persone portano i malati dal guaritore, e lui li guarisce. È proprio quello che succede. Quanto di più può fare il nostro Dio! Vi prego, non fraintendetemi. Non sto dicendo che non dovremmo andare dal medico o in ospedale; sto cercando piuttosto di sottolineare che la nostra fiducia deve essere in Dio.

Qualche anno fa decisi di trovare un lavoro part-time vendendo coltelli. Dovevo prendere quei coltelli e andare di casa in casa. Non mi interessavano i coltelli; cercavo soltanto di guadagnare qualcosa in più. Ero un pessimo venditore di coltelli. Dovunque andassi, tutti dicevano di no.

Un giorno il capo mi portò nel suo ufficio e mi disse che aveva notato che non vendevo coltelli e si era reso conto di aver dimenticato di mostrarmi come funzionavano. Così restammo seduti nel suo ufficio mentre mi parlava di ciascun coltello. Aveva un piccolo assortimento di utensili da cucina di un’altra marca, rinomati per la loro qualità, che usò per fare un confronto. Per prima cosa prese un piccolo pezzo di cuoio e mi chiese di tagliarlo a metà con uno degli «altri» coltelli. Riuscii a segare il pezzo di cuoio senza troppa fatica. Poi mi disse di usare uno dei suoi coltelli e fare la stessa cosa. Il nuovo coltello tagliò il cuoio come se non ci fosse nemmeno! Rimasi davvero sbalordito. Poi prese un penny e mi disse di tagliarlo a metà con le «altre» forbici. Ci provai, ma non ci riuscii: non lo tagliavano proprio. Allora mi disse di fare lo stesso con le sue forbici. Tagliarono facilmente il penny e, ancora una volta, rimasi stupito dal prodotto. Mi disse che ormai sapevo che quei coltelli erano i migliori e che da quel momento avrei dovuto riuscire a venderli. Aveva ragione. Cominciai a vendere coltelli dappertutto! Ricordo perfino di essere entrato in una roulotte malandata, senza grandi speranze che comprassero. Con mia sorpresa, comprarono coltelli per oltre 3.000 dollari.

È chiaro perché cominciai a vendere: credevo nel prodotto. Allo stesso modo, se confidiamo in Dio, avremo fiducia. In un’epoca in cui la maggior parte di coloro che si professano cristiani si vergogna di Dio e di prendere posizione per la verità, possiamo essere una luce splendente. Possiamo essere un popolo che esce nel mondo e nelle proprie comunità con un Vangelo in cui crede davvero! Se lo facciamo, il mondo lo vedrà e reagirà. Molti sono in cerca; cercano risposte. Quando qualcuno ci chiede perché facciamo le cose che facciamo o indossiamo ciò che indossiamo, cosa rispondiamo? Rispondiamo con sicurezza? Abbiamo pronta una citazione biblica? O ci imbarazziamo e vorremmo sprofondare? Se il mondo vedesse che abbiamo fiducia nel nostro Dio e che gli ubbidiamo con entusiasmo, sarebbe una testimonianza potente.

Ricordo di aver attraversato l’aeroporto con un piccolo gruppo. Mentre eravamo in fila, sentii una signora chiedere a una delle sorelle nubili del nostro gruppo perché portasse quella «cosa» in testa. Ero entusiasta di poter ascoltare senza farmi notare, e fui felice di sentire la sua risposta. «Ha mai letto 1 Corinzi 11? Lì ci viene insegnato che le donne dovrebbero coprirsi il capo. È un segno di sottomissione». La donna rimase stupita dalla risposta e disse che non aveva mai sentito una cosa simile, e che suo padre era pastore. Continuarono a fare una conversazione molto interessante, che terminò con il desiderio della signora di tornare a casa e studiare la Bibbia.

Un opuscolo può fare molto bene; così anche un sermone potente o un articolo stampato; ma ciò che il mondo cerca è qualcuno che riponga tutta la propria fiducia in Dio! Vogliono «vedere qualcosa che funziona», e perché no? Dio vuole servirsi di noi per mostrare la sua potenza. Certamente ognuno di noi vuole essere usato da Dio. Possiamo esserlo. Ognuno di noi può esserlo. La risposta è confida nel SIGNORE con tutto il tuo cuore e non ti appoggiare sul tuo discernimento –Proverbi 3:5.

And he [Jesus] spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees; When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand. So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand –Luk 21:29-31.

Summer truly is upon us; and the trees have shot forth. What an interesting term for our modern-day English language, yet we still understand its meaning and have a mental picture of what is happening—the leaves pushing out from places that over winter were bare. For me, I think it is easier to have this mental picture since I have seen time-lapse videos of plants growing or sprouting to life.

Anyway, so much for that. What about the rest of this verse? (…when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.) Surely most of us continue to see the end of time approaching—the wars and rumors of wars, the earthquakes, the political upheaval in nation after nation, societies moving further and further away from God, and churches and families being ravished by sin and scandal.

We have God’s own promise that what we know and experience here on this earth was designed, created, and expected by Him to be only a temporary reality. And, Thou, Lord, in the beginning hast laid the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the works of thine hands: They shall perish; but thou remainest; and they all shall wax old as doth a garment; And as a vesture shalt thou fold them up, and they shall be changed: but thou art the same, and thy years shall not fail –Heb 1:10-12.

The Prevailing Menace of Doubt & Fear

As we, as a church (FCF) and as a ministry (TBV), interact with numerous challenging situations (broken homes, struggling marriages, adopted children, faltering youth, immoral addictions, emotional struggles, and mental health issues) we repeatedly run into questions of doubt. “Why did this happen to me?” “Why doesn’t God change my circumstances?” “How can I trust God when all these painful things have happened to me?” “How can I surrender my life to God when He isn’t trustworthy?”

Most believers claim to trust God and believe His Word. The challenge that seems to come for each of us is two-fold. First, many of us tend to think that believing is primarily “feeling” instead of “choosing.” Secondly, many of us find it easy to believe what God says when it agrees with our experience, our thoughts, and our feelings; the problem arises when what the Scriptures say pushes on my will, my view, my belief, my experience, etc.

On the first point (believing=feeling) we have God’s clear answer from the Apostle Paul, for we walk by faith, not by sight: –2Co 5:7. On the second point the reality is that each of these struggles are a clear test of whether we will obey God rather than man (including ourselves), whether we will let God be true and every man a liar (including ourselves), and whether we will allow God to be the authority on all things or if we will still insist on our own will. Many of us claim (give lip service) to trust and believe God in all things, yet when we are faced with our own time of testing, we fail miserably (I know I have).

Additionally, many of us define our lifestyle of doubts and worry as being something normal, yet the Bible tells us to be anxious for nothing and to cast all our cares upon our Lord. Here the world has slowly deadened our senses to the clear teaching of the Scriptures, in that we have come to accept as normal that which God would have us to rise above. If we step back and consider the definition of “fear” as being on a spectrum, with some fear being quite minor and some being quite severe, we will see that many of our accepted patterns of behavior are outside of God’s perfect will for our lives. Doubt would be on the lesser end of the spectrum, with worry having a slightly stronger presence and effect, while panicking or being frantic would obviously cause much greater interference in our normal lives. Yet the truth is that each one of these is still in the family of “fear,” with the outcome being that we are allowing fear to control us and dictate our thoughts and behaviors. God’s will is that all His children would walk by faith instead of by fear.

God never gives us grace for any of our worries, nor for any future possible “what ifs”. God only gives us grace to go through what He is placing in front of us moment by moment. In the same way that a woman with child must go through the scary possibilities of the pain of childbirth, so likewise, all human beings must go through each circumstance that God decides is our lot in life. Nothing that we try to think or do (fear, worry, move, change our location, spend money, or ask others to intervene, etc.) will stop or change what God wills for our life. It is our choice to either accept or resist the inevitable in our lives.

The reality is this—each of us will either yield [our] members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin by believing the lies of Satan and continuing to allow fear to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions, OR we will yield [ourself] unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and our members as instruments of righteousness unto God (Rom 6:13), by choosing to believe what God says in His Word and allowing faith to motivate and direct our thoughts and actions.

Here a balancing perspective needs to be brought in. This does not mean that we never wrestle with difficult situations—Jesus did in the Garden of Gethsemane. It also doesn’t mean that we never appeal to God or our authorities to consider changing our current painful situation—again, Jesus did. Rather, we are to be honest with God (like Jesus was) about the struggle of our heart, but then we need to eventually walk forward in obedience, by faith, with courage (like Jesus did).

Ongoing Support Needed

A big thank you to all who so faithfully continue to support the work of The Berean Voice. It is through the many prayers, emails and phone calls of encouragement and suggestions, and the financial contributions of many believers that we can continue to minister to the needs of others. As a non-profit ministry of the church, we do not charge for our material or services, therefore we rely entirely on the ongoing freewill offerings of God’s people. Please prayerfully consider how God would have you to partner with us in this work.

If you believe that God would have you support us financially, monthly support makes our work easier since most of our bills are monthly. However, if this doesn’t work as well for you that is fine. For your convenience there is a remittance envelope in the center of each copy of the magazine or you can go to our website www.bereanvoice.org and use the “donate” feature there for online donations. Naye [Yesu] akawaambia mfano: Tazameni mtini na miti yote; inapoanza kuchipua, ninyi wenyewe huona na kujua kwamba majira ya joto yamekaribia. Vivyo hivyo nanyi, mtakapoona mambo hayo yakitukia, jueni kwamba ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia –Luka 21:29-31.

Kwa kweli majira ya joto yamewadia; na miti imechipua. Hili ni neno la kuvutia katika lugha yetu ya Kiingereza ya kisasa, lakini bado tunaelewa maana yake na tunaweza kuwazia kinachotendeka—majani yakichomoza kutoka mahali ambapo wakati wa majira ya baridi yalikuwa matupu. Kwa upande wangu, nadhani ni rahisi zaidi kuwazia jambo hili kwa kuwa nimeona video za muda mfupi zinazoonyesha mimea ikikua au kuchipua na kuwa hai.

Hata hivyo, hayo yanatosha kuhusu jambo hilo. Vipi kuhusu sehemu iliyobaki ya mstari huu? (…mtakapoona mambo hayo yakitukia, jueni kwamba ufalme wa Mungu umekaribia.) Hakika wengi wetu tunaendelea kuona mwisho wa wakati ukikaribia—vita na habari za vita, matetemeko ya ardhi, misukosuko ya kisiasa katika taifa baada ya taifa, jamii zikizidi kumwacha Mungu, na makanisa na familia zikiharibiwa na dhambi na kashfa.

Tunalo ahadi ya Mungu mwenyewe kwamba mambo tunayoyajua na kuyapitia hapa duniani yalipangwa, yakaumbwa, na kutarajiwa na Yeye kuwa hali ya muda tu. Na Wewe, Bwana, hapo mwanzo uliweka msingi wa dunia; na mbingu ni kazi ya mikono yako: Hizo zitaangamia, bali Wewe wabaki; nazo zote zitachakaa kama vazi; Na kama vazi utazikunja, nazo zitabadilika; bali Wewe u yeye yule, na miaka yako haitakoma –Ebr 1:10-12.

Tishio Linaloendelea la Mashaka na Hofu

Tunapokabiliana, kama kanisa (FCF) na kama huduma (TBV), na hali nyingi ngumu (nyumba zilizovunjika, ndoa zinazopitia shida, watoto walioasiliwa, vijana wanaoyumba, uraibu wa uasherati, matatizo ya kihisia, na matatizo ya afya ya akili), mara kwa mara tunakutana na maswali ya mashaka. “Kwa nini jambo hili limenitokea?” “Kwa nini Mungu habadili hali yangu?” “Ninawezaje kumtumaini Mungu wakati mambo haya yote yenye kuumiza yamenitokea?” “Ninawezaje kuyasalimisha maisha yangu kwa Mungu ilhali hastahili kutumainiwa?”

Waumini wengi hudai kumtumaini Mungu na kuliamini Neno lake. Changamoto ambayo inaonekana kutukabili kila mmoja wetu ina sehemu mbili. Kwanza, wengi wetu huwa tunafikiri kwamba kuamini hasa ni “kuhisi” badala ya “kuchagua.” Pili, wengi wetu huona ni rahisi kuamini yale Mungu anayosema yanapokubaliana na yale tunayopitia, mawazo yetu na hisia zetu; tatizo hutokea wakati yale Maandiko yasemayo yanapokinzana na mapenzi yangu, mtazamo wangu, imani yangu, yale ninayopitia, na kadhalika.

Kuhusu jambo la kwanza (kuamini=kuhisi), tunalo jibu lililo wazi la Mungu kutoka kwa Mtume Paulo: kwa maana twaenenda kwa imani, si kwa kuona –2Kor 5:7. Kuhusu jambo la pili, ukweli ni kwamba kila mojawapo ya mapambano haya ni jaribio lililo wazi la kuona ikiwa tutamtii Mungu badala ya mwanadamu (pamoja na sisi wenyewe), ikiwa tutamruhusu Mungu awe wa kweli na kila mwanadamu awe mwongo (pamoja na sisi wenyewe), na ikiwa tutamruhusu Mungu kuwa mamlaka katika mambo yote au bado tutasisitiza kufuata mapenzi yetu wenyewe. Wengi wetu hudai (husema tu kwa midomo) kwamba tunamtumaini Mungu na kumwamini katika mambo yote, lakini tunapokabiliwa na wakati wetu wenyewe wa kujaribiwa, tunashindwa vibaya sana (najua nimefanya hivyo).

Zaidi ya hayo, wengi wetu hufafanua mtindo wetu wa maisha wenye mashaka na wasiwasi kuwa jambo la kawaida, ilhali Biblia inatuambia tusiwe na wasiwasi juu ya jambo lolote na tumtwike Bwana wetu fadhaa zetu zote. Hapa ulimwengu umepunguza polepole uwezo wetu wa kuhisi uzito wa mafundisho yaliyo wazi ya Maandiko, kwa kuwa tumekubali kuwa jambo la kawaida kile ambacho Mungu angetaka tukishinde. Tukitulia kidogo na kufikiria ufafanuzi wa “hofu” kuwa kwenye mwendelezo wa viwango tofauti, ambapo hofu fulani ni ndogo sana na nyingine ni kali sana, tutaona kwamba mienendo yetu mingi ambayo tumeikubali haimo katika mapenzi makamilifu ya Mungu kwa maisha yetu. Mashaka yangekuwa upande wa chini wa mwendelezo huo, wasiwasi ukiwa na nguvu na athari kubwa kidogo, huku kuingiwa na hofu au kuwa na wasiwasi uliopitiliza bila shaka kukisababisha kuingiliwa zaidi kwa maisha yetu ya kawaida. Hata hivyo, ukweli ni kwamba kila mojawapo ya haya bado imo katika kundi la “hofu,” na matokeo yake ni kwamba tunairuhusu hofu itutawale na kuamuru mawazo na mienendo yetu. Mapenzi ya Mungu ni kwamba watoto wake wote waenende kwa imani badala ya hofu.

Mungu hatupi kamwe neema kwa ajili ya wasiwasi wetu wowote, wala kwa ajili ya “vipi ikiwa” zozote zinazoweza kutokea baadaye. Mungu hutupa neema tu ya kuvumilia yale anayoyaweka mbele yetu, dakika baada ya dakika. Kama vile mwanamke mwenye mimba anavyopaswa kupitia uwezekano wa kutisha wa uchungu wa kuzaa, vivyo hivyo wanadamu wote wanapaswa kupitia kila hali ambayo Mungu ameamua kuwa sehemu yetu maishani. Hakuna jambo tunalojaribu kufikiri au kufanya (kuogopa, kuwa na wasiwasi, kuhama, kubadili mahali tunapoishi, kutumia pesa, au kuwaomba wengine waingilie kati, na kadhalika) litakalozuia au kubadili mapenzi ya Mungu kwa maisha yetu. Ni uchaguzi wetu ama kukubali au kupinga yale yasiyoepukika maishani mwetu.

Ukweli ni huu—kila mmoja wetu ama ataitoa miili [yake] iwe silaha za dhuluma kwa dhambi kwa kuziamini uongo wa Shetani na kuendelea kuiruhusu hofu ichochee na kuongoza mawazo na matendo yetu, AU atajiweka [mwenyewe] kwa Mungu, kama walio hai kutoka kwa wafu, na viungo vyake viwe silaha za haki kwa Mungu (Rum 6:13), kwa kuchagua kuamini yale ambayo Mungu anasema katika Neno lake na kuruhusu imani ichochee na kuongoza mawazo na matendo yetu.

Hapa tunahitaji kuweka mtazamo wenye uwiano. Hii haimaanishi kwamba hatutahangaika kamwe na hali ngumu—Yesu alifanya hivyo katika Bustani ya Gethsemane. Wala haimaanishi kwamba hatutamsihi Mungu au wenye mamlaka yetu wafikirie kubadili hali yetu ya sasa yenye uchungu—Yesu alifanya hivyo tena. Badala yake, tunapaswa kuwa waaminifu kwa Mungu (kama Yesu alivyokuwa) kuhusu mapambano yaliyo moyoni mwetu, lakini kisha tunahitaji hatimaye kuendelea mbele kwa utii, kwa imani na kwa ujasiri (kama Yesu alivyofanya).

Msaada Unaohitajika Kuendelea

Shukrani nyingi kwa wote wanaoendelea kwa uaminifu kuunga mkono kazi ya The Berean Voice. Ikiwa unaamini kwamba Mungu angependa utusaidie kifedha, msaada wa kila mwezi hurahisisha kazi yetu kwa kuwa bili zetu nyingi ni za kila mwezi. Hata hivyo, ikiwa hilo halikufai sana, ni sawa.
