Si el matrimonio es un pacto, ¿qué importancia tiene la relación de pacto? ¿Qué la convierte en una relación de pacto y en qué se diferencia de cualquier otra relación? Estas son preguntas que debemos procurar responder si queremos entender la permanencia del matrimonio y navegar con éxito por las aguas turbulentas de un matrimonio en crisis.

El pacto se ha vuelto algo arcaico en nuestra sociedad. La revolución cultural de los años sesenta hizo que el divorcio fuera culturalmente aceptable, y la fidelidad matrimonial para toda la vida se ha convertido en la excepción y no en la regla. Lamentablemente, esta plaga ha infectado a la mayoría de las iglesias tradicionales y actualmente está invadiendo nuestras iglesias anabaptistas.

El pacto es una idea de Dios. Él es quien establece los pactos principalmente. Su santo nombre, «Jehová», indica que Dios siempre cumple su palabra. El origen hebreo de «Jehová» es yeh-ho-vaw. Esta palabra combina dos verbos hebreos que expresan el ser. Una traducción muy literal del nombre yeh-ho-vaw sería «es es», o, como Dios le dijo a Moisés: «Yo soy el que soy».

El nombre de Dios, «Jehová», indica que Dios siempre cumple su palabra, que no puede mentir y que es fiel a su carácter. Santiago lo expresa así: Toda buena dádiva y todo don perfecto viene de lo alto y desciende del Padre de las luces, en quien no hay cambio ni sombra de variación –Stg 1:17.

¿Qué constituye un pacto?

Un examen cuidadoso de las Escrituras revela que hay tres elementos clave para establecer un pacto.

  • Palabras
  • Testigos
  • Aquello que ratifica el pacto

Palabras

Las palabras definen los términos y las condiciones de un pacto. Es muy importante que ambas partes involucradas definan y comprendan claramente los términos y las condiciones del pacto. Cuando Dios hizo un pacto con Abraham, habló y dijo: Estableceré mi pacto entre mí y ti, y con tu descendencia después de ti, en sus generaciones, por pacto perpetuo, para ser tu Dios y el de tu descendencia después de ti –Gén 17:7.

Cuando Dios hizo un pacto con la nación de Israel en el monte Sinaí, les dio la Ley, que contenía los términos y las condiciones del pacto mosaico.

En nuestras Biblias tenemos el Antiguo y el Nuevo Testamento. Esto se refiere al Antiguo y al Nuevo Pacto. En el Nuevo Testamento encontramos las enseñanzas de Jesús y sus apóstoles, que prevalecen sobre la ley del Antiguo Testamento. En el Sermón del Monte, Jesús dijo repetidamente: «Oísteis que fue dicho, pero yo os digo».

El escritor de Hebreos dijo lo siguiente acerca del Nuevo Pacto: Pero ahora ha obtenido un ministerio tanto más excelente, cuanto que es mediador de un mejor pacto, establecido sobre mejores promesas –Heb 8:6.

El día de nuestra boda usamos palabras de significado preciso para establecer un pacto vinculante «…hasta que la muerte nos separe». Los votos matrimoniales pueden variar, pero siempre deben incluir el compromiso de mantener una relación de amor mutuo que dure toda la vida y, por tanto, sea irrevocable.

Testigos

Otra parte importante de un pacto son los testigos. Los testigos validan los votos pronunciados y contribuyen a que se rindan cuentas por ellos. Esto es especialmente cierto en un pacto entre dos personas.

Cuando Josué restableció el pacto con Israel al entrar en la tierra de Canaán, los desafió: Y Josué dijo al pueblo: Vosotros sois testigos contra vosotros mismos de que habéis escogido al SEÑOR para servirle. Y ellos dijeron: Somos testigos –Jos 24:22. Lo que decían era: «Nos haremos mutuamente responsables de los compromisos que asumimos hoy».

En cuanto al Nuevo Pacto, tenemos el testimonio del apóstol Juan, quien dice: Porque tres son los que dan testimonio en el cielo: el Padre, el Verbo y el Espíritu Santo; y estos tres son uno. Y tres son los que dan testimonio en la tierra: el Espíritu, el agua y la sangre; y estos tres concuerdan –1 Jn 5:7-8. Aquí Juan dice que en este Nuevo Pacto entre Dios y el hombre hay tres testigos en el cielo y tres testigos en la tierra, y que todos estos testigos concuerdan.

Al establecer un pacto matrimonial, los invitados a la boda son los testigos. Cada invitado da testimonio de los votos que se pronuncian. Con su presencia y bendición, validan el matrimonio y adquieren la responsabilidad personal de velar por que este perdure.

Este compromiso comunitario con la permanencia del matrimonio es el tejido moral de nuestra sociedad y de nuestras iglesias. Cuando una sociedad descuida hacer valer la permanencia del matrimonio, sobrevienen el caos y la confusión. Vemos esto en la sociedad que nos rodea. Lamentablemente, también estamos viendo un número cada vez mayor de rupturas matrimoniales en nuestras iglesias anabaptistas.

Aquello que ratifica el pacto

El paso final para establecer un pacto es aquello que lo ratifica y hace vinculantes y efectivos sus términos. Históricamente, ha habido diversos métodos para sellar un pacto. Los antiguos beduinos tenían la costumbre de usar sal para sellar un pacto. Cada parte daba a la otra una medida de sal. La sal se mezclaba con las respectivas reservas de sal de cada uno, haciendo imposible separar alguna vez «mi sal» de «tu sal». Esto simbolizaba la inmutabilidad del tratado.

También existía la práctica de berith. Berith es una palabra hebrea que significa «cortar». En el antiguo Israel, un pacto se ratificaba «cortando un pacto». Esta práctica se ilustra claramente en Génesis 15, donde Dios ratificó su pacto con Abraham. Abraham le preguntó a Dios: …Señor DIOS, ¿en qué sabré que la he de heredar? –Gén 15:8. La respuesta de Dios a la súplica de Abraham fue: …Tómame una becerra de tres años, una cabra de tres años, un carnero de tres años, una tórtola y un pichón –Gén 15:9. Abraham tomó estos animales, los partió por la mitad y los dispuso como sacrificio para Dios. Dios reafirmó su pacto con Abraham (con palabras) y luego, en el versículo 17, ocurrió este misterioso acontecimiento: Y sucedió que, cuando se puso el sol y ya estaba oscuro, he aquí un horno humeante y una antorcha de fuego que pasó entre aquellos pedazos –Gén 15:17. Esto era «berith», o el «corte del pacto». Esta ceremonia ratificó e hizo vinculantes los términos y las condiciones del pacto. Después de este suceso, no hay constancia de que Abraham volviera a cuestionar o dudar de la promesa de Dios, aunque sí tomó el asunto en sus propias manos para hacer realidad esa promesa.

Cuando Dios hizo un pacto con Israel en el monte Sinaí, …Moisés tomó la sangre y la roció sobre el pueblo, y dijo: He aquí la sangre del pacto que el SEÑOR ha hecho con vosotros conforme a todas estas palabras –Éx 24:8. Esta sangre hizo vinculantes y efectivos los términos y las condiciones establecidos en la ley: este era el Antiguo Pacto.

Cuando Dios hizo un pacto contigo y conmigo en el monte Calvario, la sangre de Jesús se convirtió en la prueba ratificadora, o la señal vinculante, de su Nuevo Pacto con nosotros. Cuando participamos de la comunión, conmemoramos el pacto que tenemos con Dios por medio de Cristo.

¿Qué ratifica el pacto matrimonial? Como ya hemos visto, en el matrimonio tenemos palabras (los votos) y testigos (los invitados). ¿Basta con esto para completar el matrimonio? No. El matrimonio no está completo hasta que se produce la unión en la intimidad física. Esto completa o, como a veces decimos, consuma el pacto matrimonial. Esto es lo que ratifica y hace vinculantes y permanentes los términos y las condiciones del pacto matrimonial. Ya desde los primeros pasajes de las Escrituras encontramos un ejemplo de esto: Y Adán conoció a Eva, su mujer… Gén 4:1. Más adelante vemos otro ejemplo: E Isaac la llevó [a Rebeca] a la tienda de su madre Sara, tomó a Rebeca, y ella se convirtió en su mujer; y él la amó… –Gén 24:67. La unión física pertenece al pacto. Por eso una relación así fuera del matrimonio es pecado. La fornicación o el adulterio toma aquello que Dios ordenó que estuviera indisolublemente ligado al matrimonio y adultera el pacto.

Cuando una pareja casada se une físicamente, conmemora y celebra su pacto matrimonial. Este es el comienzo de establecer una realidad bíblica de «una sola carne». De esta unión bendita surge una nueva vida en forma de preciosos «pequeñitos» y de corazones renovados por el poder del amor.

Cuando participamos del pan y del vino de la comunión, conmemoramos y celebramos nuestra relación de pacto con Cristo. De esta bendita unidad surge una nueva vida en forma de corazones renovados por el poder del amor. Esta es la fuerza del pacto.

Donde existen estos tres elementos —votos, testigos y aquello que ratifica—, hay una relación de pacto. ¿En qué se diferencia una relación de pacto de cualquier otra relación?

Un compromiso de fidelidad

Algunas de las palabras más nobles que pueden pronunciar los labios humanos son: «Prometo amarte hasta que la muerte nos separe». El día de nuestra boda es fácil pronunciar estas palabras, y quizá seamos muy sinceros al decirlas. Lo cierto es que nadie puede saber qué costo pueden tener esas palabras a lo largo de toda una vida.

El amor es una decisión, y debe arraigarse y perdurar como una forma de vida cotidiana. Debemos elegir dirigir nuestro afecto hacia aquella persona a quien nos une nuestro pacto de amor y apartarlo de las tentaciones de otras personas. Muchísimos matrimonios se destruyen por la infidelidad.

Dios diseñó el matrimonio para que fuera un vínculo poderoso. El apego espiritual, emocional y físico del matrimonio crea un lazo inseparable. En Génesis leemos: Por tanto, dejará el hombre a su padre y a su madre, y se unirá a su mujer, y serán una sola carne –Gén 2:24. La palabra unirá en este versículo denota «estar soldados o pegados de tal manera que sea imposible separarlos».

Romper el vínculo matrimonial por medio de la infidelidad causa desgarramiento y heridas a ambas partes. Satanás, el gran engañador, quiere hacernos creer que ser infieles a nuestro cónyuge nos beneficiará de alguna manera. Esto es una gran mentira.

Un compromiso de fidelidad

Dios demostró fidelidad al pacto en su trato con su esposa del Antiguo Testamento, la nación de Israel. Ella no fue fiel a sus votos del pacto. Se apartó de la adoración a Jehová y se postró ante altares paganos. A pesar de su infidelidad, Dios siguió procurándola y llamándola a volver a él. La infidelidad de Israel no alteró la fidelidad de Dios. Esta es la fuerza del amor de pacto. El amor de pacto no depende de las acciones de la otra parte. Persiste aunque no sea correspondido. Este es un principio del reino. Pablo enseñó: Por tanto, si tu enemigo tiene hambre, dale de comer; si tiene sed, dale de beber; pues haciendo esto, amontonarás ascuas de fuego sobre su cabeza –Rom 12:20. ¿No sería este principio especialmente aplicable a un matrimonio quebrantado?

La fuerza del pacto solo puede comprenderse plenamente si entendemos el amor divino de Dios por nosotros. Nuestra salvación depende del amor perfecto que Dios nos tiene. Él sigue amándonos aunque nuestro amor por él sea a veces imperfecto. Su amor inagotable sigue atrayéndonos de vuelta a él. La fuerza del pacto matrimonial se encuentra en procurar imitar este amor divino. Este amor divino no se encontrará en novelas románticas ni en otros libros sobre el matrimonio. Solo se encuentra en una relación íntima con «la Fuente» del amor eterno.

My Help and My Deliverer

Psalm 40:1 I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. 2 He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. 3 And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. 4 Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. 5 Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered. 6 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, 8 I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. 9 I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. 10 I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation. 11 Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. 12 For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me. 13 Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me. 14 Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil. 15 Let them be desolate for a reward of their shame that say unto me, Aha, aha. 16 Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. 17 But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

A glorious morning unfolds before me, perfect and peaceful, unmarred by failure. The sky is clear and blue. The horizon is a soft, blushing pink, enhanced by a misty fog. The distant hills and trees are shaded a dusky blue in the misty morning coolness. The morning is ringing with the warbling, twittering, chirping of birds. The grass glows with millions of dew droplets sparkling in the morning light. The pink horizon above the distant, dusky hills gradually fades into a glowing orange sphere that becomes brighter and brighter.

I stand in awe of God. My heart is thrilled at the beauty spread out before me. I am also thrilled at what God has done in my life, and the beauty He has created out of ashes.

I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. God has brought me up out of the pit of despair and discouragement. He has set my feet upon the Rock, Jesus Christ, and He has established my goings. He knows the plans He has for me. His thoughts and His ways are much higher than mine.

He hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. I desire that God will be glorified through the work He has done and is continuing to do in my life. Many, O Lord, are Thy wonderful works which Thou hast done, and Thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto Thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

I delight to do Thy will, O God: yea, Thy law is within my heart. It is truly my delight to do the will of God; to love Him with my whole heart, soul, strength, and mind; to obey His commandments from my heart.

I have not hid Thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared Thy faithfulness and Thy salvation: I have not concealed Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth from the great congregation. It is such a blessing to have deep and edifying conversations with my brothers and sisters in the Lord, and to share together what the Lord is doing in our lives. It is a great strengthening to my faith.

Withhold not Thy tender mercies from me, O Lord: let Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth continually preserve me. Temptations and hard tests are a very real thing in life; the struggle to keep my heart with a diligence, the battle against stubborn pride, and the urge to utter hasty words of frustration. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me. Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.

The sun has risen above the distant hills and the countryside is now glowing gloriously. The mist has faded into the woods and the distant dusky blue hills and trees have exchanged their robes for vivid shades of green intermixed with hints of red and brown. The sparkling droplets of dew are dazzling in the brilliant sunlight.

Let those that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: let such as love Thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified. I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: Thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

Children, obey your parents in all things: for this is well pleasing unto the Lord –Col 3:20.

Years ago, there was a boy named Joey who lived with his father and mother on the outskirts of a city. One day Joey’s father gave him a brand new red and white bike, which he had been wanting for a long time.

There was a big hill close to their house where the big boys in the neighborhood enjoyed riding their bikes. Joey’s father strictly forbade him from riding with the big boys on the hill, since it was too dangerous. Instead, he was only allowed to ride down the nice smooth sidewalk, past numerous houses, through a little alley, and then finally back to his house once again.

As the days and weeks went by, this began to lose its excitement. He watched enviously as the big boys walked their bikes up the hill almost directly in front of his house. At the top they would jump on their bikes, and with gleeful shouts, race down the hardtop road, swiftly turning onto the adjoining street at the bottom of the hill.

“Whee, here we come!” they would shout as they rushed by, leaving Joey to pedal calmly on around his little block again and again.

“Come on Joey!” the boys hollered. “Why don’t you come up with us? See what fun we are having! You are too scared,” they teased.

Joey was too embarrassed to tell them that his father had forbidden him since he was too little and might fall off his bike and hurt himself. The boys would have only made more fun of him, so he remained silent. How he wished he could go up and show his friends that he was not afraid. Joey thought, “Maybe if I would go down the hill just once, my dad would realize that I’m not so little after all. Then Dad would be proud of me and let me go down the hill with the big boys anytime I want to. Oh, how exciting that would be.” The very thought made his heart beat quickly in anticipation.

Joey did not need to wait very long for his opportunity. His father was going to be gone for a couple of days on business. Joey thought this would be his chance to prove to his dad that he was able to ride his bike with the big boys. With excitement and anticipation, he took his bike up the hill. He felt so grown-up in the big boys’ company. Surely his father was wrong! Now he would prove to everybody that he knew better than anyone else what he was able to do and not do.

With a run and a hop, he was on his bike. As the bike went faster and faster, he grabbed the handlebars more firmly. At that moment, one of the mischievous boys, coming up the hill, tossed a stone at Joey’s tire as he flew by. Joey swerved sharply to avoid the stone. Before he knew what was happening, he was sailing thru the air without his bike. He rolled and skidded and bumped, before coming to a painful stop. Joey was one big mess. His pants and shirt were torn. He had cuts and bruises on his hands, knees, and face. No more was he thinking of being a hero of the great biking hill. Our little, humbled “hero” of the hill was taken home to his mother, who sympathetically and lovingly washed and patched his wounds.

The next day Joey’s father returned home. When he saw the bandages on his son and the damaged bicycle, he guessed the story immediately. Joey’s bike was put away in storage for several weeks as punishment for his disobedience.

Joey sat on the curb as the boys raced down the hill, then on to the other street. Now Joey had no desire to sneak off and ride his bike with the big boys. He had learned his lesson—to always obey his father, even when he thought he knew better. He realized that his father was not trying to ruin his fun but instead he was trying to keep him safe.

When Joey was again allowed to ride his bike, he was quite content to ride peacefully around his little block of houses. From now on he was going to obey his father, not only in matters of safety, but in all things.

Enyi watoto, watiini wazazi wenu katika mambo yote: kwa maana jambo hili humpendeza Bwana sana –Kol 3:20.

Miaka mingi iliyopita, kulikuwa na mvulana mmoja aliyeitwa Joey aliyeishi na baba na mama yake pembezoni mwa jiji. Siku moja baba yake Joey alimpa baiskeli mpya kabisa, nyekundu na nyeupe, ambayo alikuwa akiitamani kwa muda mrefu.

Karibu na nyumba yao kulikuwa na kilima kikubwa ambacho wavulana wakubwa wa jirani walifurahia kushukia kwa baiskeli zao. Baba yake Joey alimkataza kabisa kuendesha baiskeli pamoja na wavulana wakubwa kwenye kilima hicho, kwa kuwa kilikuwa hatari mno. Badala yake, aliruhusiwa tu kuendesha baiskeli kwenye njia nzuri, tambarare ya watembea kwa miguu, akipita nyumba nyingi, kupitia kichochoro kidogo, na hatimaye kurudi tena nyumbani kwake.

Siku na majuma yalivyopita, jambo hilo lilianza kupoteza msisimko wake. Aliwatazama kwa wivu wavulana wakubwa wakitembeza baiskeli zao kupanda kilima karibu moja kwa moja mbele ya nyumba yake. Wakiwa juu kabisa, waliruka juu ya baiskeli zao, na kwa shangwe wakashuka kwa kasi kwenye barabara ya lami, wakigeukia kwa wepesi barabara nyingine iliyoungana nayo chini ya kilima.

“Whee, tunakuja!” walipiga kelele walipokuwa wakipita kwa kasi, huku Joey akiendelea kukanyaga taratibu kuzunguka mtaa wake mdogo tena na tena.

“Njoo, Joey!” wavulana walipiga kelele. “Mbona hupandi pamoja nasi? Tazama tunavyofurahia! Unaogopa sana,” walimtania.

Joey aliona aibu mno kuwaambia kwamba baba yake alikuwa amemkataza kwa sababu alikuwa mdogo sana na huenda akaanguka kutoka kwenye baiskeli yake na kujiumiza. Wavulana wangemdhihaki zaidi tu, kwa hiyo alikaa kimya. Alitamani sana kupanda huko na kuwaonyesha rafiki zake kwamba hakuwa mwoga. Joey aliwaza, “Labda nikishuka kilima mara moja tu, baba yangu atatambua kwamba mimi si mdogo sana tena. Kisha Baba atajivunia na kuniruhusu kushuka kilima pamoja na wavulana wakubwa wakati wowote nitakapotaka. Lo, hilo lingefurahisha sana.” Wazo hilo tu lilifanya moyo wake upige kwa kasi kwa hamu ya kutarajia.

Joey hakuhitaji kusubiri muda mrefu kupata nafasi yake. Baba yake alipaswa kwenda kikazi kwa siku kadhaa. Joey alifikiri kwamba hii ingekuwa nafasi yake ya kumthibitishia baba yake kwamba alikuwa na uwezo wa kuendesha baiskeli pamoja na wavulana wakubwa. Akiwa na msisimko na hamu ya kutarajia, aliipandisha baiskeli yake kilimani. Alijihisi mtu mzima sana akiwa pamoja na wavulana wakubwa. Kwa hakika baba yake alikuwa amekosea! Sasa angemthibitishia kila mtu kwamba yeye ndiye aliyejua kuliko mtu mwingine yeyote kile alichoweza na asichoweza kufanya.

Kwa kujikimbiza na kuruka, alikuwa juu ya baiskeli yake. Baiskeli ilipozidi kwenda kasi, alizishika kwa nguvu zaidi ncha za usukani. Wakati huo, mmoja wa wavulana watundu, aliyekuwa akipanda kilima, alirusha jiwe kwenye tairi la Joey alipokuwa akipita kwa kasi. Joey aligeuka ghafla ili kulikwepa jiwe. Kabla hajatambua kilichokuwa kikitokea, alikuwa akiruka angani bila baiskeli yake. Alijiviringisha, akateleza na kujigonga, kabla ya kusimama kwa maumivu. Joey alikuwa amechafuka vibaya. Suruali na shati lake vilikuwa vimechanika. Alikuwa na michubuko na majeraha mikononi, magotini na usoni. Hakuwa tena akiwaza kuwa shujaa wa kile kilima kikubwa cha baiskeli. “Shujaa” wetu mdogo, aliyekuwa amenyenyekezwa, alirudishwa nyumbani kwa mama yake, ambaye kwa huruma na upendo alisafisha na kufunga majeraha yake.

Siku iliyofuata baba yake Joey alirudi nyumbani. Alipoona bendeji kwenye mwili wa mwanawe na baiskeli iliyoharibika, alikisia mara moja kilichotokea. Baiskeli ya Joey ilihifadhiwa kwa majuma kadhaa kama adhabu kwa kutotii kwake.

Joey aliketi kwenye ukingo wa barabara wavulana walipokuwa wakishuka kwa kasi kilima, kisha kuelekea barabara nyingine. Sasa Joey hakutaka tena kujificha na kuendesha baiskeli pamoja na wavulana wakubwa. Alikuwa amejifunza somo lake—kumtii baba yake sikuzote, hata alipofikiri kwamba yeye ndiye aliyejua zaidi. Alitambua kwamba baba yake hakuwa akijaribu kumnyang’anya furaha, bali alikuwa akijaribu kumlinda asiwe hatarini.

Joey alipopewa tena ruhusa ya kuendesha baiskeli yake, aliridhika kabisa kuendesha kwa amani kuzunguka mtaa wake mdogo wenye nyumba. Kuanzia wakati huo, angemtii baba yake, si katika mambo ya usalama tu, bali katika mambo yote.

If marriage is a covenant, what is the significance of covenant relationship? What makes it a covenant relationship, and how does this differ from any other relationship? These are answers that we must pursue if we are to understand the permanence of marriage and if we are to successfully navigate the rocky shores of a troubled marriage.

Covenant in our society has become archaic. The cultural revolution of the sixties has made divorce culturally acceptable, and life-long fidelity in marriage has become the exception rather than the rule. Unfortunately, this blight has infected most mainstream churches and is currently invading our Anabaptist churches.

Covenant is God’s idea. He is the primary covenant maker. His holy name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word. The Hebrew origin of “Jehovah” is yeh-ho-vaw. This word combines two Hebrew verbs of being. A most literal translation for the name yeh-ho-vaw would be (is is) or as God said to Moses “I am that I am.”

God’s name “Jehovah” indicates that God is always true to His word, that he cannot lie, and that He is true to His character. James states it this way: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning –Jas 1:17.

What makes a covenant?

Careful investigation of scripture will reveal that there are three key elements in the establishment of a covenant.

  • Words
  • Witnesses
  • That which ratifies the covenant

Words

Words define the terms and conditions of a covenant. It is very important that the terms and conditions of the covenant be clearly defined and understood by both parties involved. When God made covenant with Abraham, He spake and said, And I will establish my covenant between me and thee and thy seed after thee in their generations for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee –Gen 17:7.

When God made covenant with the nation of Israel at Mt Sinai, He gave them the Law which was the terms and conditions of the Mosaic covenant.

In our Bibles today we have the Old and the New Testament. This refers to the Old and the New Covenant. In the New Testament we have the teachings of Jesus and His Apostles which supersede the Old Testament law. In the Sermon on the Mount, Jesus said repeatedly, “You have heard that it hath been said, but I say unto you.”

The Hebrew writer had this to say about the New Covenant: But now hath he obtained a more excellent ministry, by how much also he is the mediator of a better covenant, which was established upon better promises –Heb 8:6.

On our wedding day we use words with precise meaning to establish a covenant that is binding “…till death do us part.” Wedding vows may contain some variation but should always include a commitment to a mutually loving relationship that is binding for life, and thus irrevocable.

Witnesses

Another important part of a covenant is the witnesses. Witnesses provide validation and accountability to the vows that have been made. This is especially true of a covenant made between two people.

When Joshua re-established the covenant with Israel upon entering the land of Canaan, he challenged them: And Joshua said unto the people, Ye are witnesses against yourselves that ye have chosen you the LORD, to serve him. And they said, We are witnesses –Jos 24:22. What they were saying was that, “We will hold one another accountable for the commitments that we are making today.”

Regarding the New Covenant, we have the testimony of the Apostle John where he says: For there are three that bear record in heaven, the Father, the Word, and the Holy Ghost: and these three are one. And there are three that bear witness in earth, the Spirit, and the water, and the blood: and these three agree in one –1Joh 5:7-8. Here John is saying that in this New Covenant between God and man there are three witnesses in heaven and three witnesses in earth, and these witnesses all agree.

In the establishment of a marriage covenant the wedding guests are the witnesses. Every guest becomes a witness of the vows that are made. By their presence and blessing, they validate the marriage and become personally responsible to ensure that this marriage endures.

This community commitment to the permanence of marriage is the moral fabric of our society and our churches. When a society becomes negligent in enforcing the permanence of marriage, chaos and confusion ensue. We see this in the society around us. Unfortunately, we are also seeing an increasing number of marriage breakups within our Anabaptist churches.

That which ratifies the covenant

The final step in establishing a covenant is that which ratifies and renders binding and effective the terms of the covenant. Historically there have been a variety of methods of binding a covenant. Ancient Bedouins had a practice of using salt to bind a covenant. Each party would give to the other a measure of salt. The salt was mixed with their respective stores of salt making it impossible to ever separate “my salt” from “your salt.” This symbolized the immutability of this treaty.

Then there was the practice of berith. Berith is a Hebrew word that means “to cut.” In ancient Israel a covenant was ratified by “cutting a covenant.” This practice is clearly illustrated in Genesis 15 where God ratified His covenant with Abraham. Abraham asked God, …Lord GOD, whereby shall I know that I shall inherit it? –Gen 15:8. God’s response to Abraham’s plea was …Take me an heifer of three years old, and a she goat of three years old, and a ram of three years old, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon –Gen 15:9. Abraham took these animals and divided them in the midst and lay them out as a sacrifice to God. God reaffirmed His covenant with Abraham (with words), and then in verse 17, we have this mysterious event: And it came to pass, that, when the sun went down, and it was dark, behold a smoking furnace, and a burning lamp that passed between those pieces –Gen 15:17. This was “berith” or the “cutting of the covenant.” This ceremony ratified and rendered binding the terms and conditions of the covenant. After this event, we have no record that Abraham ever questioned or doubted the promise of God, although he did take it into his own hands to bring that promise to fruition.

When God made covenant with Israel at Mt Sinai, …Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which the LORD hath made with you concerning all these words –Exo 24:8. This blood rendered binding and effective the terms and conditions set forth in the law—this was the Old Covenant.

When God made covenant with you and I at Mt Calvary, the blood of Jesus became the ratifying evidence or the binding token of His New Covenant with us. When we partake of the communion, we are commemorating the covenant that we have with God through Christ.

What ratifies the marriage covenant? As we have already seen, in a marriage we have words (the vows), and we have witnesses (the guests). Does this complete the marriage? No. The marriage is not complete until there is a coming together in physical intimacy. This completes or, as we sometimes say, consummates the marriage covenant. This is that which ratifies and renders binding and permanent the terms and conditions of the marriage covenant. Early on in Scripture we have example of this. And Adam knew Eve his wife… Gen 4:1. Then later on we see another example, And Isaac brought her [Rebekah] into his mother Sarah’s tent, and took Rebekah, and she became his wife; and he loved her… –Gen 24:67. Physical oneness belongs to covenant. This is why such a relationship outside of marriage is sin. Fornication or adultery takes that which God has ordained to be inextricably linked to marriage and adulterates the covenant.

When a married couple comes together in physical union they are commemorating and celebrating their marriage covenant. This is the start of them establishing a biblical “one flesh” reality. From this blessed union new life emerges in the form of precious “little ones” and of hearts that are renewed by the power of love.

When we partake of the bread and the wine of communion we are commemorating and celebrating our covenant relationship with Christ. From this blessed oneness new life emerges in the form of hearts that are renewed by the power of love. This is the strength of covenant.

Where these three elements exist—vows, witnesses, and that which ratifies—we have a covenant relationship. How does a covenant relationship differ from any other relationship?

A commitment to fidelity

Some of the most noble words that human lips can utter are “I promise to love you till death do us part.” On our wedding day these words are easy to utter, and we may be most sincere when we speak them. The fact is that no one can possibly know what those words may cost in the course of a lifetime.

Love is a choice and must become established and endure as an every day walk of life. We must choose to direct our affection toward the one of our covenant love and away from the enticements of others. Many, many marriages are destroyed through infidelity.

God has designed marriage to be powerfully bonding. The spiritual, emotional, and physical attachment of marriage creates an inseparable bond. In Genesis we read Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife: and they shall be one flesh –Gen 2:24. The word cleave in this verse denotes “being welded or glued together in such a way as to be inseparable.”

To break the marriage bond through infidelity causes rending and wounding to both parties. Satan, the great deceiver, would have us to believe that being unfaithful to our spouse will somehow benefit us. This is a huge lie.

A commitment to faithfulness

God demonstrated covenant faithfulness in his dealings with His Old Testament bride—the nation of Israel. She was not true to her covenant vows. She turned from the worship of Jehovah, and she bowed her knee to pagan altars. Despite her unfaithfulness, God continued to pursue her and call her back unto himself. Israel’s unfaithfulness did not alter God’s faithfulness. This is the strength of covenant love. Covenant love is not contingent upon the actions of the other party. Covenant love persists even though it is not reciprocated. This is a kingdom concept. Paul taught, Therefore if thine enemy hunger, feed him; if he thirst, give him drink: for in so doing thou shalt heap coals of fire on his head –Rom 12:20. Would this principle not most aptly apply to a broken marriage?

The strength of covenant can only be fully realized through an understanding of the divine love of God for us. Our salvation is dependent upon God’s perfect love for us. He continues to love us even though our love for Him is sometimes flawed. His unfailing love continues to draw us back unto himself. The strength of covenant in marriage is found in seeking to emulate this divine love. This divine love will not be found in romance novels or other books on marriage. This divine love can only be found in an intimate relationship with “The Source” of undying love.

As die huwelik ’n verbond is, wat is die betekenis van ’n verbondsverhouding? Wat maak dit ’n verbondsverhouding, en hoe verskil dit van enige ander verhouding? Dit is vrae waarop ons antwoorde moet soek as ons die permanensie van die huwelik wil verstaan en die rotsagtige strande van ’n huwelik in beroering suksesvol wil navigeer.

Die verbond het in ons samelewing verouderd geraak. Die kulturele revolusie van die sestigerjare het egskeiding kultureel aanvaarbaar gemaak, en lewenslange getrouheid in die huwelik het eerder die uitsondering as die reël geword. Ongelukkig het hierdie plaag die meeste hoofstroomkerke besmet en is dit tans besig om ons Anabaptistiese kerke binne te dring.

Die verbond is God se idee. Hy is die vernaamste verbondmaker. Sy heilige naam “Jehovah” dui daarop dat God altyd getrou is aan sy woord. Die Hebreeuse oorsprong van “Jehovah” is yeh-ho-vaw. Hierdie woord kombineer twee Hebreeuse werkwoorde van bestaan. ’n Baie letterlike vertaling van die naam yeh-ho-vaw sou wees (is is), of soos God vir Moses gesê het: “Ek is wat Ek is.”

God se naam “Jehovah” dui daarop dat God altyd getrou is aan sy woord, dat Hy nie kan lieg nie, en dat Hy getrou is aan sy karakter. Jakobus stel dit só: Elke goeie gawe en elke volmaakte geskenk kom van bo af en daal neer van die Vader van die ligte, by wie daar geen verandering of skaduwee van omkering is nie –Jak 1:17.

Wat maak ’n verbond?

Noukeurige ondersoek van die Skrif sal aan die lig bring dat daar drie sleutelelemente is wanneer ’n verbond tot stand kom.

  • Woorde
  • Getuies
  • Dit wat die verbond bekragtig

Woorde

Woorde omskryf die bepalings en voorwaardes van ’n verbond. Dit is baie belangrik dat die bepalings en voorwaardes van die verbond duidelik omskryf en deur albei betrokke partye verstaan word. Toe God ’n verbond met Abraham gesluit het, het Hy gespreek en gesê: En Ek sal my verbond oprig tussen My en jou en jou nageslag ná jou in hulle geslagte as ’n ewige verbond, om vir jou ’n God te wees en vir jou nageslag ná jou –Gen 17:7.

Toe God by die berg Sinai ’n verbond met die volk Israel gesluit het, het Hy aan hulle die Wet gegee, wat die bepalings en voorwaardes van die Mosaïese verbond was.

In ons Bybels het ons vandag die Ou en die Nuwe Testament. Dit verwys na die Ou en die Nuwe Verbond. In die Nuwe Testament het ons die leringe van Jesus en sy apostels, wat die Ou-Testamentiese wet vervang. In die Bergpredikasie het Jesus herhaaldelik gesê: “Julle het gehoor dat daar gesê is, maar Ek sê vir julle.”

Die skrywer van Hebreërs het die volgende oor die Nuwe Verbond gesê: Maar nou het Hy ’n voortrefliker bediening verkry, net soos Hy ook Middelaar is van ’n beter verbond wat op beter beloftes gegrond is –Heb 8:6.

Op ons troudag gebruik ons woorde met ’n presiese betekenis om ’n bindende verbond te sluit, “…totdat die dood ons skei.” Huweliksbeloftes kan ietwat verskil, maar moet altyd ’n verbintenis tot ’n wedersyds liefdevolle verhouding insluit wat lewenslank bindend en dus onherroeplik is.

Getuies

Getuies is nog ’n belangrike deel van ’n verbond. Getuies bevestig die geldigheid van die geloftes wat afgelê is en hou die partye daarvoor verantwoordelik. Dit geld veral vir ’n verbond wat tussen twee mense gesluit word.

Toe Josua die verbond met Israel hernu het nadat hulle die land Kanaän binnegegaan het, het hy hulle uitgedaag: En Josua het aan die volk gesê: Julle is getuies teen julleself dat julle die HERE vir julle gekies het om Hom te dien. En hulle het gesê: Ons is getuies –Jos 24:22. Wat hulle gesê het, was: “Ons sal mekaar verantwoordelik hou vir die verbintenisse wat ons vandag aangaan.”

Wat die Nuwe Verbond betref, het ons die getuienis van die apostel Johannes, waar hy sê: Want daar is drie wat getuig in die hemel: die Vader, die Woord en die Heilige Gees; en hierdie drie is een. En daar is drie wat getuig op die aarde: die Gees en die water en die bloed; en hierdie drie stem ooreen –1 Joh 5:7-8. Johannes sê hier dat daar in hierdie Nuwe Verbond tussen God en die mens drie getuies in die hemel en drie getuies op aarde is, en dat hierdie getuies almal saamstem.

By die sluiting van ’n huweliksverbond is die bruilofsgaste die getuies. Elke gas word ’n getuie van die geloftes wat afgelê word. Deur hulle teenwoordigheid en seën bevestig hulle die huwelik en word hulle persoonlik daarvoor verantwoordelik om toe te sien dat hierdie huwelik standhou.

Hierdie gemeenskaplike verbintenis tot die permanensie van die huwelik is die morele weefsel van ons samelewing en ons kerke. Wanneer ’n samelewing nalaat om die permanensie van die huwelik te handhaaf, volg chaos en verwarring. Ons sien dit in die samelewing rondom ons. Ongelukkig sien ons ook ’n toenemende aantal huweliksverbintenisse wat binne ons Anabaptistiese kerke verbrokkel.

Dit wat die verbond bekragtig

Die laaste stap in die sluiting van ’n verbond is dit wat die bepalings van die verbond bekragtig en bindend en van krag maak. Histories was daar ’n verskeidenheid maniere om ’n verbond te bind. Antieke Bedoeïene het die gebruik gehad om sout te gebruik om ’n verbond te bind. Elke party het vir die ander ’n hoeveelheid sout gegee. Die sout is met hulle onderskeie soutvoorrade gemeng, wat dit onmoontlik gemaak het om “my sout” ooit van “jou sout” te skei. Dit het die onveranderlikheid van hierdie verdrag gesimboliseer.

Dan was daar die gebruik van berith. Berith is ’n Hebreeuse woord wat “om te sny” beteken. In antieke Israel is ’n verbond bekragtig deur “’n verbond te sny”. Hierdie gebruik word duidelik geïllustreer in Genesis 15, waar God sy verbond met Abraham bekragtig het. Abraham het God gevra: …Here HERE, waaraan sal ek weet dat ek dit in besit sal neem? –Gen 15:8. God se antwoord op Abraham se versoek was: …Neem vir My ’n driejarige vers, ’n driejarige bokooi, ’n driejarige ram, ’n tortelduif en ’n jong duif –Gen 15:9. Abraham het hierdie diere geneem, hulle middeldeur gesny en hulle as ’n offer aan God uitgelê. God het sy verbond met Abraham (met woorde) herbevestig, en toe, in vers 17, het hierdie geheimsinnige gebeurtenis plaasgevind: En ná sononder, toe dit heeltemal donker was, was daar ’n rokende oond en vuurvlamme wat tussen die stukke deurgegaan het –Gen 15:17. Dit was “berith”, oftewel die “sny van die verbond”. Hierdie seremonie het die bepalings en voorwaardes van die verbond bekragtig en bindend gemaak. Ná hierdie gebeurtenis is daar geen aanduiding dat Abraham ooit God se belofte bevraagteken of daaraan getwyfel het nie, hoewel hy wel sake in eie hande geneem het om daardie belofte te verwesenlik.

Toe God by die berg Sinai ’n verbond met Israel gesluit het, het …Moses die bloed geneem en dit op die volk gesprinkel en gesê: Dit is die bloed van die verbond wat die HERE met julle gesluit het op grond van al hierdie woorde –Eks 24:8. Hierdie bloed het die bepalings en voorwaardes wat in die wet uiteengesit is bindend en van krag gemaak—dit was die Ou Verbond.

Toe God by die berg Golgota ’n verbond met jou en my gesluit het, het Jesus se bloed die bekragtigende bewys, oftewel die bindende teken, van sy Nuwe Verbond met ons geword. Wanneer ons aan die nagmaal deelneem, herdenk ons die verbond wat ons deur Christus met God het.

Wat bekragtig die huweliksverbond? Soos ons reeds gesien het, het ons in ’n huwelik woorde (die geloftes) en getuies (die gaste). Maak dit die huwelik volledig? Nee. Die huwelik is nie volledig voordat daar fisieke intimiteit is nie. Dit voltooi, of, soos ons soms sê, voltrek die huweliksverbond. Dit is wat die bepalings en voorwaardes van die huweliksverbond bekragtig en bindend en blywend maak. Vroeg in die Skrif kry ons ’n voorbeeld hiervan: En Adam het sy vrou Eva beken… Gen 4:1. Later sien ons nog ’n voorbeeld: En Isak het haar [Rebekka] in die tent van sy moeder Sara gebring en Rebekka geneem, en sy het sy vrou geword; en hy het haar liefgehad… –Gen 24:67. Fisieke eenheid hoort by die verbond. Daarom is so ’n verhouding buite die huwelik sonde. Hoerery of egbreuk neem dit wat God bestem het om onlosmaaklik aan die huwelik verbind te wees en besoedel die verbond.

Wanneer ’n getroude paartjie in fisieke eenheid saamkom, herdenk en vier hulle hul huweliksverbond. Dit is die begin van die vestiging van ’n Bybelse werklikheid van “een vlees”. Uit hierdie geseënde vereniging spruit nuwe lewe voort in die vorm van kosbare “kleintjies” en harte wat deur die krag van liefde vernuwe word.

Wanneer ons aan die brood en die wyn van die nagmaal deelneem, herdenk en vier ons ons verbondsverhouding met Christus. Uit hierdie geseënde eenheid spruit nuwe lewe voort in die vorm van harte wat deur die krag van liefde vernuwe word. Dit is die krag van die verbond.

Waar hierdie drie elemente voorkom—geloftes, getuies en dit wat die verbond bekragtig—het ons ’n verbondsverhouding. Hoe verskil ’n verbondsverhouding van enige ander verhouding?

’n Verbintenis tot getrouheid

Sommige van die edelste woorde wat mense kan uiter, is: “Ek belowe om jou lief te hê totdat die dood ons skei.” Op ons troudag is hierdie woorde maklik om uit te spreek, en wanneer ons hulle sê, kan ons heel opreg wees. Die feit is dat niemand kan weet wat daardie woorde in die loop van ’n leeftyd kan kos nie.

Liefde is ’n keuse en moet gevestig word en as ’n daaglikse lewenswandel voortduur. Ons moet kies om ons liefde te rig op die een vir wie ons ons in die verbond verbind het, en weg van die verleidings van ander. Baie, baie huwelike word deur ontrouheid verwoes.

God het die huwelik ontwerp om ’n kragtige binding te wees. Die geestelike, emosionele en fisieke verbondenheid van die huwelik skep ’n onafskeibare band. In Genesis lees ons: Daarom sal die man sy vader en moeder verlaat en sy vrou aankleef. En hulle sal een vlees wees –Gen 2:24. Die woord aankleef in hierdie vers dui daarop dat hulle “aanmekaar gesweis of vasgegom word op so ’n manier dat hulle nie geskei kan word nie”.

Om die huweliksband deur ontrouheid te verbreek, veroorsaak skeuring en verwonding by albei partye. Satan, die groot bedrieër, wil ons laat glo dat ontrou aan ons huweliksmaat ons op die een of ander manier sal bevoordeel. Dit is ’n groot leuen.

’n Verbintenis tot getrou bly

God het verbondstrou gedemonstreer in sy omgang met sy Ou-Testamentiese bruid—die volk Israel. Sy was nie getrou aan haar verbondsgeloftes nie. Sy het haar van die aanbidding van Jehovah afgekeer en voor heidense altare gekniel. Ten spyte van haar ontrouheid het God aangehou om haar na Hom toe te roep en terug te roep. Israel se ontrouheid het nie God se getrouheid verander nie. Dit is die krag van verbondsliefde. Verbondsliefde is nie afhanklik van die optrede van die ander party nie. Verbondsliefde hou aan, selfs wanneer dit nie beantwoord word nie. Dit is ’n koninkryksbeginsel. Paulus het geleer: As jou vyand dan honger het, gee hom iets om te eet; as hy dors het, gee hom iets om te drink; want so sal jy op sy hoof vurige kole ophoop –Rom 12:20. Sou hierdie beginsel nie uiters toepaslik wees op ’n verbrokkelde huwelik nie?

Die krag van die verbond kan slegs ten volle besef word deur ’n begrip van God se goddelike liefde vir ons. Ons redding is afhanklik van God se volmaakte liefde vir ons. Hy hou aan om ons lief te hê, selfs wanneer ons liefde vir Hom soms gebrekkig is. Sy onfeilbare liefde hou aan om ons na Hom toe terug te trek. Die krag van die verbond in die huwelik lê daarin dat ons hierdie goddelike liefde probeer navolg. Hierdie goddelike liefde sal nie in romanseboeke of ander boeke oor die huwelik gevind word nie. Hierdie goddelike liefde kan slegs gevind word in ’n intieme verhouding met “Die Bron” van liefde wat nooit sterf nie.

My Help and My Deliverer

Psalm 40:1 I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. 2 He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. 3 And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. 4 Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. 5 Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered. 6 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, 8 I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. 9 I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. 10 I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation. 11 Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. 12 For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me. 13 Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me. 14 Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil. 15 Let them be desolate for a reward of their shame that say unto me, Aha, aha. 16 Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. 17 But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

A glorious morning unfolds before me, perfect and peaceful, unmarred by failure. The sky is clear and blue. The horizon is a soft, blushing pink, enhanced by a misty fog. The distant hills and trees are shaded a dusky blue in the misty morning coolness. The morning is ringing with the warbling, twittering, chirping of birds. The grass glows with millions of dew droplets sparkling in the morning light. The pink horizon above the distant, dusky hills gradually fades into a glowing orange sphere that becomes brighter and brighter.

I stand in awe of God. My heart is thrilled at the beauty spread out before me. I am also thrilled at what God has done in my life, and the beauty He has created out of ashes.

I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. God has brought me up out of the pit of despair and discouragement. He has set my feet upon the Rock, Jesus Christ, and He has established my goings. He knows the plans He has for me. His thoughts and His ways are much higher than mine.

He hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. I desire that God will be glorified through the work He has done and is continuing to do in my life. Many, O Lord, are Thy wonderful works which Thou hast done, and Thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto Thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

I delight to do Thy will, O God: yea, Thy law is within my heart. It is truly my delight to do the will of God; to love Him with my whole heart, soul, strength, and mind; to obey His commandments from my heart.

I have not hid Thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared Thy faithfulness and Thy salvation: I have not concealed Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth from the great congregation. It is such a blessing to have deep and edifying conversations with my brothers and sisters in the Lord, and to share together what the Lord is doing in our lives. It is a great strengthening to my faith.

Withhold not Thy tender mercies from me, O Lord: let Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth continually preserve me. Temptations and hard tests are a very real thing in life; the struggle to keep my heart with a diligence, the battle against stubborn pride, and the urge to utter hasty words of frustration. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me. Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil.

The sun has risen above the distant hills and the countryside is now glowing gloriously. The mist has faded into the woods and the distant dusky blue hills and trees have exchanged their robes for vivid shades of green intermixed with hints of red and brown. The sparkling droplets of dew are dazzling in the brilliant sunlight.

Let those that seek Thee rejoice and be glad in Thee: let such as love Thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified. I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: Thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

Meine Hilfe und mein Erretter

Psalm 40:1 Ich harrte des HERRN; da neigte er sich zu mir und hörte mein Schreien. 2 Er zog mich aus der grausigen Grube, aus dem Schlamm und Morast, und stellte meine Füße auf einen Felsen und machte meine Schritte fest. 3 Er legte mir ein neues Lied in den Mund, einen Lobgesang für unseren Gott. Viele werden es sehen und sich fürchten und auf den HERRN vertrauen. 4 Wohl dem, der sein Vertrauen auf den HERRN setzt und sich nicht zu den Hoffärtigen wendet, noch zu denen, die sich zur Lüge halten. 5 HERR, mein Gott, groß sind deine Wunder und deine Gedanken, die du für uns hast; nichts ist dir gleich. Wollte ich sie verkünden und davon reden, so wären sie nicht zu zählen. 6 Schlacht- und Speisopfer hast du nicht gewollt; meine Ohren hast du geöffnet. Brand- und Sündopfer hast du nicht verlangt. 7 Da sprach ich: Siehe, ich komme; im Buch ist von mir geschrieben. 8 Deinen Willen zu tun, mein Gott, ist meine Lust, und dein Gesetz ist in meinem Herzen. 9 Ich verkündete Gerechtigkeit in der großen Gemeinde; siehe, ich hielt meine Lippen nicht zurück, HERR, du weißt es. 10 Ich verbarg deine Gerechtigkeit nicht in meinem Herzen; ich verkündete deine Treue und deine Rettung. Deine Gnade und Wahrheit verschwieg ich nicht vor der großen Gemeinde. 11 HERR, entziehe mir dein Erbarmen nicht; deine Gnade und Wahrheit mögen mich allezeit behüten. 12 Denn unzählige Übel haben mich umringt. Meine Sünden haben mich ereilt, sodass ich nicht aufblicken kann; sie sind zahlreicher als die Haare auf meinem Haupt, und mein Herz verlässt mich. 13 HERR, lass es dir gefallen, mich zu retten; HERR, eile mir zu Hilfe. 14 Lass alle zuschanden und verwirrt werden, die mir nach dem Leben trachten, um es zu vernichten; lass sie zurückweichen und beschämt werden, die mir Böses wünschen. 15 Lass sie wegen ihrer Schande verstummen, die zu mir sagen: »Aha! Aha!« 16 Lass alle, die dich suchen, sich freuen und fröhlich sein in dir; die deine Rettung lieben, sollen stets sagen: »Der HERR sei gepriesen!« 17 Ich aber bin arm und bedürftig; doch der Herr denkt an mich. Du bist meine Hilfe und mein Erretter; säume nicht, mein Gott.

Ein herrlicher Morgen breitet sich vor mir aus, vollkommen und friedlich, ungetrübt von einem Missgeschick. Der Himmel ist klar und blau. Der Horizont ist zart rosa gefärbt und wird von einem nebligen Dunst verstärkt. Die fernen Hügel und Bäume zeichnen sich in der kühlen, nebligen Morgenluft in einem düsteren Blau ab. Der Morgen klingt vom Trillern, Zwitschern und Piepsen der Vögel. Das Gras glitzert im Morgenlicht mit Millionen Tautropfen. Der rosafarbene Horizont über den fernen, dunkelblauen Hügeln geht allmählich in eine leuchtende orangefarbene Kugel über, die immer heller wird.

Ich stehe voller Ehrfurcht vor Gott. Mein Herz ist bewegt von der Schönheit, die sich vor mir ausbreitet. Auch das, was Gott in meinem Leben getan hat und die Schönheit, die er aus Asche geschaffen hat, erfüllt mich mit Freude.

Ich harrte des HERRN; da neigte er sich zu mir und hörte mein Schreien. Er zog mich aus der grausigen Grube, aus dem Schlamm und Morast, und stellte meine Füße auf einen Felsen und machte meine Schritte fest. Gott hat mich aus der Grube der Verzweiflung und Entmutigung herausgeholt. Er hat meine Füße auf den Felsen Jesus Christus gestellt und meine Schritte fest gemacht. Er kennt die Pläne, die er für mich hat. Seine Gedanken und seine Wege sind viel höher als meine.

Er legte mir ein neues Lied in den Mund, einen Lobgesang für unseren Gott. Viele werden es sehen und sich fürchten und auf den Herrn vertrauen. Ich wünsche mir, dass Gott durch das Werk verherrlicht wird, das er in meinem Leben getan hat und weiterhin tut. HERR, groß sind deine Wunder und deine Gedanken, die du für uns hast; nichts ist dir gleich. Wollte ich sie verkünden und davon reden, so wären sie nicht zu zählen.

Deinen Willen zu tun, mein Gott, ist meine Lust, und dein Gesetz ist in meinem Herzen. Es ist wahrhaftig meine Freude, den Willen Gottes zu tun; ihn von ganzem Herzen, ganzer Seele, mit aller Kraft und ganzem Verstand zu lieben; seine Gebote von Herzen zu befolgen.

Ich verbarg deine Gerechtigkeit nicht in meinem Herzen; ich verkündete deine Treue und deine Rettung. Deine Gnade und Wahrheit verschwieg ich nicht vor der großen Gemeinde. Es ist ein großer Segen, tiefgründige und erbauliche Gespräche mit meinen Brüdern und Schwestern im Herrn zu führen und miteinander zu teilen, was der Herr in unserem Leben tut. Das stärkt meinen Glauben sehr.

HERR, entziehe mir dein Erbarmen nicht; deine Gnade und Wahrheit mögen mich allezeit behüten. Versuchungen und schwere Prüfungen gehören im Leben ganz real dazu: der Kampf, mein Herz mit aller Sorgfalt zu bewahren, der Kampf gegen hartnäckigen Stolz und der Drang, voreilige Worte der Frustration auszusprechen. HERR, lass es dir gefallen, mich zu retten; HERR, eile mir zu Hilfe. Lass alle zuschanden und verwirrt werden, die mir nach dem Leben trachten, um es zu vernichten; lass sie zurückweichen und beschämt werden, die mir Böses wünschen.

Die Sonne ist über den fernen Hügeln aufgegangen, und die Landschaft erstrahlt nun in herrlichem Glanz. Der Nebel hat sich in die Wälder zurückgezogen, und die fernen, dunkelblauen Hügel und Bäume haben ihre Gewänder gegen leuchtende Grüntöne eingetauscht, durchsetzt mit roten und braunen Nuancen. Die glitzernden Tautropfen blenden im strahlenden Sonnenlicht.

Alle, die dich suchen, sollen sich freuen und fröhlich sein in dir; die deine Rettung lieben, sollen stets sagen: »Der Herr sei gepriesen!« Ich aber bin arm und bedürftig; doch der Herr denkt an mich. Du bist meine Hilfe und mein Erretter; säume nicht, mein Gott.

My Help and My Deliverer

Psalm 40:1 I waited patiently for the LORD; and he inclined unto me, and heard my cry. 2 He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. 3 And he hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the LORD. 4 Blessed is that man that maketh the LORD his trust, and respecteth not the proud, nor such as turn aside to lies. 5 Many, O LORD my God, are thy wonderful works which thou hast done, and thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered. 6 Sacrifice and offering thou didst not desire; mine ears hast thou opened: burnt offering and sin offering hast thou not required. 7 Then said I, Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me, 8 I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart. 9 I have preached righteousness in the great congregation: lo, I have not refrained my lips, O LORD, thou knowest. 10 I have not hid thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared thy faithfulness and thy salvation: I have not concealed thy lovingkindness and thy truth from the great congregation. 11 Withhold not thou thy tender mercies from me, O LORD: let thy lovingkindness and thy truth continually preserve me. 12 For innumerable evils have compassed me about: mine iniquities have taken hold upon me, so that I am not able to look up; they are more than the hairs of mine head: therefore my heart faileth me. 13 Be pleased, O LORD, to deliver me: O LORD, make haste to help me. 14 Let them be ashamed and confounded together that seek after my soul to destroy it; let them be driven backward and put to shame that wish me evil. 15 Let them be desolate for a reward of their shame that say unto me, Aha, aha. 16 Let all those that seek thee rejoice and be glad in thee: let such as love thy salvation say continually, The LORD be magnified. 17 But I am poor and needy; yet the Lord thinketh upon me: thou art my help and my deliverer; make no tarrying, O my God.

A glorious morning unfolds before me, perfect and peaceful, unmarred by failure. The sky is clear and blue. The horizon is a soft, blushing pink, enhanced by a misty fog. The distant hills and trees are shaded a dusky blue in the misty morning coolness. The morning is ringing with the warbling, twittering, chirping of birds. The grass glows with millions of dew droplets sparkling in the morning light. The pink horizon above the distant, dusky hills gradually fades into a glowing orange sphere that becomes brighter and brighter.

I stand in awe of God. My heart is thrilled at the beauty spread out before me. I am also thrilled at what God has done in my life, and the beauty He has created out of ashes.

I waited patiently for the Lord; and He inclined unto me, and heard my cry. He brought me up also out of an horrible pit, out of the miry clay, and set my feet upon a rock, and established my goings. God has brought me up out of the pit of despair and discouragement. He has set my feet upon the Rock, Jesus Christ, and He has established my goings. He knows the plans He has for me. His thoughts and His ways are much higher than mine.

He hath put a new song in my mouth, even praise unto our God: many shall see it, and fear, and shall trust in the Lord. I desire that God will be glorified through the work He has done and is continuing to do in my life. Many, O Lord, are Thy wonderful works which Thou hast done, and Thy thoughts which are to us-ward: they cannot be reckoned up in order unto Thee: if I would declare and speak of them, they are more than can be numbered.

I delight to do Thy will, O God: yea, Thy law is within my heart. It is truly my delight to do the will of God; to love Him with my whole heart, soul, strength, and mind; to obey His commandments from my heart.

I have not hid Thy righteousness within my heart; I have declared Thy faithfulness and Thy salvation: I have not concealed Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth from the great congregation. It is such a blessing to have deep and edifying conversations with my brothers and sisters in the Lord, and to share together what the Lord is doing in our lives. It is a great strengthening to my faith.

Withhold not Thy tender mercies from me, O Lord: let Thy lovingkindness and Thy truth continually preserve me. Temptations and hard tests are a very real thing in life; the struggle to keep my heart with a diligence, the battle against stubborn pride, and the urge to utter hasty words of frustration. Be pleased, O Lord, to deliver me: O Lord, make haste to help me. Моя помощь и мой Избавитель

Псалом 40:1 Я терпеливо ждал Господа, и Он склонился ко мне и услышал мой вопль. 2 Он извлек меня из страшной ямы, из вязкой грязи, поставил мои ноги на скалу и укрепил мои шаги. 3 Он вложил в мои уста новую песнь — хвалу нашему Богу. Многие увидят это, устрашатся и будут уповать на Господа. 4 Блажен человек, который уповает на Господа и не обращается к надменным и к тем, кто уклоняется ко лжи. 5 Много дивных дел совершил Ты, Господи, Боже мой, и много замыслов Твоих о нас; нет равного Тебе. Если бы я стал возвещать и говорить о них, их оказалось бы больше, чем можно счесть. 6 Жертвы и приношения Ты не пожелал; Ты открыл мои уши; всесожжения и жертвы за грех Ты не потребовал. 7 Тогда я сказал: «Вот, я иду; в свитке книги написано обо мне: 8 Я желаю исполнить волю Твою, Боже мой, и закон Твой у меня в сердце». 9 Я возвещал правду в великом собрании; вот, я не удерживал уст моих — Ты знаешь это, Господи. 10 Я не скрывал правды Твоей в сердце моем; я возвещал верность Твою и спасение Твое; не утаивал милости Твоей и истины Твоей от великого собрания. 11 Не удерживай от меня щедрых милостей Твоих, Господи; да хранят меня непрестанно милость Твоя и истина Твоя. 12 Ибо окружили меня неисчислимые беды; беззакония мои постигли меня, так что я не могу поднять глаз; их больше, чем волос на голове моей, и сердце мое оставило меня. 13 Благоволи, Господи, избавить меня; Господи, поспеши на помощь мне. 14 Да постыдятся и посрамятся вместе ищущие погубить душу мою; да обратятся назад и будут посрамлены желающие мне зла. 15 Да оцепенеют от стыда те, кто говорит мне: «Ага! Ага!» 16 Да радуются и веселятся о Тебе все ищущие Тебя; да говорят непрестанно любящие спасение Твое: «Да возвеличится Господь!» 17 Я же беден и нуждаюсь, но Господь заботится обо мне. Ты — помощь моя и Избавитель мой; не медли, Боже мой.

Передо мной расстилается славное утро — безмятежное и совершенное, не омраченное неудачей. Небо ясное и голубое. Горизонт нежно-розовый, словно заря, и окутан легкой дымкой. Далекие холмы и деревья в прохладе туманного утра окрашены в сумрачные голубые тона. Утро звенит мелодичным щебетом и трелями птиц. Трава сияет мириадами росинок, сверкающих в утреннем свете. Розовый горизонт над далекими темно-голубыми холмами постепенно переходит в сияющий оранжевый диск, который становится все ярче и ярче.

Я стою в благоговении перед Богом. Мое сердце ликует при виде раскинувшейся передо мной красоты. Я также ликую о том, что Бог совершил в моей жизни, и о красоте, которую Он создал из пепла.

Я терпеливо ждал Господа, и Он склонился ко мне и услышал мой вопль. Он извлек меня из страшной ямы, из вязкой грязи, поставил мои ноги на скалу и укрепил мои шаги. Бог извлек меня из ямы отчаяния и уныния. Он поставил мои ноги на Скалу — Иисуса Христа — и укрепил мои шаги. Он знает, какие замыслы имеет обо мне. Его мысли и Его пути намного выше моих.

Он вложил в мои уста новую песнь — хвалу нашему Богу. Многие увидят это, устрашатся и будут уповать на Господа. Я желаю, чтобы Бог прославлялся через то, что Он совершил и продолжает совершать в моей жизни. Много дивных дел совершил Ты, Господи, и много замыслов Твоих о нас; нет равного Тебе. Если бы я стал возвещать и говорить о них, их оказалось бы больше, чем можно счесть.

Я желаю исполнить волю Твою, Боже мой, и закон Твой у меня в сердце. Исполнять волю Бога — поистине радость для меня: любить Его всем сердцем, всей душой, всей крепостью и всем разумом; от всего сердца соблюдать Его заповеди.

Я не скрывал правды Твоей в сердце моем; я возвещал верность Твою и спасение Твое; не утаивал милости Твоей и истины Твоей от великого собрания. Какое благословение — вести глубокие и назидательные беседы с братьями и сестрами во Господе и делиться друг с другом тем, что Господь совершает в нашей жизни. Это очень укрепляет мою веру.

Не удерживай от меня щедрых милостей Твоих, Господи; да хранят меня непрестанно милость Твоя и истина Твоя. Искушения и тяжелые испытания — неотъемлемая часть жизни: борьба за то, чтобы усердно хранить свое сердце, борьба с упрямой гордостью и порыв произнести поспешные слова, вызванные досадой. Благоволи, Господи, избавить меня; Господи, поспеши на помощь мне. Да постыдятся и посрамятся вместе ищущие погубить душу мою; да обратятся назад и будут посрамлены желающие мне зла.

Солнце поднялось над далекими холмами, и теперь вся окрестность сияет великолепием. Туман рассеялся в лесу, а далекие темно-голубые холмы и деревья сменили свои одеяния на яркие оттенки зеленого с примесью красного и коричневого. Сверкающие капли росы ослепительно блестят в ярком солнечном свете.

Да радуются и веселятся о Тебе ищущие Тебя; да говорят непрестанно любящие спасение Твое: «Да возвеличится Господь!» Я же беден и нуждаюсь, но Господь заботится обо мне. Ты — помощь моя и Избавитель мой; не медли, Боже мой.

Pertolonganku dan Pembebasku

Mazmur 40:1 Aku menanti-nantikan TUHAN dengan sabar; Ia berpaling kepadaku dan mendengar seruanku. 2 Ia mengangkat aku juga dari lubang yang mengerikan, dari tanah berlumpur, dan menempatkan kakiku di atas batu, serta meneguhkan langkahku. 3 Ia menaruh nyanyian baru dalam mulutku, pujian kepada Allah kita; banyak orang akan melihatnya, lalu takut dan percaya kepada TUHAN. 4 Berbahagialah orang yang menjadikan TUHAN kepercayaannya, dan tidak berpaling kepada orang-orang congkak, atau kepada mereka yang menyimpang kepada kebohongan. 5 Banyaklah karya-Mu yang ajaib, ya TUHAN, Allahku, dan pikiran-Mu bagi kami; semuanya tidak terhitung di hadapan-Mu. Jika aku hendak mengumumkan dan menyatakannya, jumlahnya lebih banyak daripada yang dapat dihitung. 6 Engkau tidak menginginkan korban dan persembahan; telingaku telah Kaubuka; korban bakaran dan korban penghapus dosa tidak Kaukehendaki. 7 Lalu aku berkata, “Lihat, aku datang; dalam gulungan kitab tertulis tentang aku. 8 Aku suka melakukan kehendak-Mu, ya Allahku; hukum-Mu ada di dalam hatiku.” 9 Aku telah memberitakan kebenaran dalam jemaah yang besar; lihat, aku tidak menahan bibirku, ya TUHAN, Engkau mengetahuinya. 10 Aku tidak menyembunyikan kebenaran-Mu di dalam hatiku; aku telah menyatakan kesetiaan-Mu dan keselamatan-Mu; kasih setia-Mu dan kebenaran-Mu tidak kusembunyikan dari jemaah yang besar. 11 Janganlah menahan belas kasihan-Mu yang lembut dariku, ya TUHAN; biarlah kasih setia-Mu dan kebenaran-Mu senantiasa melindungiku. 12 Sebab malapetaka yang tak terhitung jumlahnya mengepung aku; kesalahanku telah menjeratku sehingga aku tak mampu menengadah; jumlahnya lebih banyak daripada rambut di kepalaku; karena itu hatiku tawar. 13 Berkenanlah, ya TUHAN, untuk menyelamatkanku; ya TUHAN, bersegeralah menolongku. 14 Biarlah mereka yang mencari nyawaku untuk membinasakannya dipermalukan dan dikejutkan bersama-sama; biarlah mereka yang menginginkan celakaku mundur dan mendapat malu. 15 Biarlah mereka yang berkata kepadaku, “Aha, aha,” menjadi terlantar sebagai ganjaran atas rasa malu mereka. 16 Biarlah semua orang yang mencari Engkau bersukacita dan bergembira di dalam Engkau; biarlah mereka yang mencintai keselamatan-Mu senantiasa berkata, “TUHAN dimuliakan.” 17 Tetapi aku miskin dan berkekurangan; namun Tuhan memperhatikanku; Engkaulah pertolonganku dan pembebasku; jangan berlambat-lambat, ya Allahku.

Pagi yang gemilang terbentang di hadapanku, sempurna dan tenteram, tanpa cela karena kegagalan. Langit cerah dan biru. Cakrawala berwarna merah muda lembut, diselimuti kabut tipis. Bukit-bukit dan pepohonan di kejauhan tampak biru kelabu dalam kesejukan pagi berkabut. Pagi bergema oleh kicauan dan celoteh burung. Rumput berkilau oleh jutaan tetes embun yang berkilauan dalam cahaya pagi. Cakrawala merah muda di atas bukit-bukit kelabu di kejauhan perlahan memudar menjadi bola jingga bercahaya yang semakin lama semakin terang.

Dengan takjub aku berdiri di hadapan Allah. Hatiku tergetar oleh keindahan yang terbentang di hadapanku. Aku juga tergetar oleh apa yang telah Allah lakukan dalam hidupku, dan keindahan yang telah Ia ciptakan dari abu.

Aku menanti-nantikan Tuhan dengan sabar; Ia berpaling kepadaku dan mendengar seruanku. Ia mengangkat aku juga dari lubang yang mengerikan, dari tanah berlumpur, dan menempatkan kakiku di atas batu, serta meneguhkan langkahku. Allah telah mengangkatku keluar dari lubang keputusasaan dan patah semangat. Ia telah menempatkan kakiku di atas Batu Karang, Yesus Kristus, dan meneguhkan langkahku. Ia mengetahui rencana-rencana yang dimiliki-Nya bagiku. Pikiran dan jalan-Nya jauh lebih tinggi daripada pikiranku.

Ia menaruh nyanyian baru dalam mulutku, pujian kepada Allah kita; banyak orang akan melihatnya, lalu takut dan percaya kepada Tuhan. Aku ingin agar Allah dimuliakan melalui pekerjaan yang telah Ia lakukan dan yang terus Ia lakukan dalam hidupku. Banyaklah karya-Mu yang ajaib, ya Tuhan, dan pikiran-Mu bagi kami; semuanya tidak terhitung di hadapan-Mu. Jika aku hendak mengumumkan dan menyatakannya, jumlahnya lebih banyak daripada yang dapat dihitung.

Aku suka melakukan kehendak-Mu, ya Allah; hukum-Mu ada di dalam hatiku. Sungguh, merupakan kesukaanku untuk melakukan kehendak Allah; mengasihi Dia dengan segenap hati, jiwa, kekuatan, dan pikiranku; menaati perintah-perintah-Nya dari dalam hatiku.

Aku tidak menyembunyikan kebenaran-Mu di dalam hatiku; aku telah menyatakan kesetiaan-Mu dan keselamatan-Mu; kasih setia-Mu dan kebenaran-Mu tidak kusembunyikan dari jemaah yang besar. Sungguh merupakan berkat untuk bercakap-cakap secara mendalam dan membangun dengan saudara-saudari seiman, serta berbagi bersama tentang apa yang sedang Tuhan lakukan dalam hidup kami. Hal itu sangat menguatkan imanku.

Janganlah menahan belas kasihan-Mu yang lembut dariku, ya Tuhan; biarlah kasih setia-Mu dan kebenaran-Mu senantiasa melindungiku. Pencobaan dan ujian berat benar-benar merupakan bagian dari kehidupan; perjuangan untuk menjaga hatiku dengan tekun, pergumulan melawan kesombongan yang keras kepala, dan dorongan untuk melontarkan kata-kata frustrasi yang gegabah. Berkenanlah, ya Tuhan, untuk menyelamatkanku; ya Tuhan, bersegeralah menolongku. Biarlah mereka yang mencari nyawaku untuk membinasakannya dipermalukan dan dikejutkan bersama-sama; biarlah mereka yang menginginkan celakaku mundur dan mendapat malu.

Matahari telah terbit di atas bukit-bukit yang jauh dan pedesaan kini bercahaya dengan gemilang. Kabut telah menghilang di antara pepohonan, dan bukit-bukit serta pepohonan kelabu di kejauhan telah menukar jubahnya dengan nuansa hijau yang cerah, bercampur dengan semburat merah dan cokelat. Tetes-tetes embun yang berkilauan menyilaukan dalam sinar matahari yang cemerlang.

Biarlah mereka yang mencari Engkau bersukacita dan bergembira di dalam Engkau; biarlah mereka yang mencintai keselamatan-Mu senantiasa berkata, “TUHAN dimuliakan.” Aku miskin dan berkekurangan; namun Tuhan memperhatikanku; Engkaulah pertolonganku dan pembebasku; jangan berlambat-lambat, ya Allahku.
